aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.description: AARON (St.) High Priest of the Old Law. (July 1) (15th cent. B.C.) The great grandson of Levi, son of Jacob, and the first of the Jewish High Priests, to which office he was appointed by God Himself. He was the brother of Moses, the Hebrew Lawgiver, with whom he shared the leadership of the people of Israel. Like Moses, he never entered the land of but died on Mount Hor, on the Promise ; borders of Edom. He was succeeded by his In art he is represented son Eliezer (B.C. 1471) with a rod in flower, a censer and a Jewish The Book of Exodus contains all that mitre. we know concerning him.

abban of kill-abban.name: Abban Of Kill-Abban
abban of kill-abban.description: An Irish Saint, contemporary of St. Patrick and nephew of St. Ibar. He was the Founder of Kill-Abban Abbey (Lein-

abban of magh-armuidhe.name: Abban Of Magh-Armuidhe
abban of magh-armuidhe.description: •ABBO (St.) M. Abbot. (6th cent.) A nephew of St. Kevin, and Founder of many monasteries, mostly in the Butler and others conSouth of Ireland. fuse the two Saints Abban. Of neither have we reliable Lives. (Nov. 13) (10th cent.) A French Benedictine monk of literary attainments rare in the age in which he lived, who was invited by St. Oswald of Worcester to preside over the community he had founded at Ramsey Abbey. After the death of St. Oswald St. Abbo returned to France and became Abbot of Fleury on the Loire. He afterwards conducted skilfully and successfully various negotiations between the Holy See and the King of France. He lost his life while endeavouring to stop a riot (a.d. 1004), and by his people was at once honoured as a Martyr. (May 16)

abdecalas.name: Abdecalas
abdecalas.description: St. with (April 21) (4th cent.) A Persian of advanced age who, St. Ananias, together with another priest, and about a hundred Christians, was a fellowof sufferer Seleucia and Ctesiphon, under the tyrant King Sapor II. They were put to death as Christians The Greek historian on Good Friday, A.d. 345. Sozomen reckons at sixteen thousand the number of the Faithful in Persia who laid down their lives for Christ during the forty years of the reign of Sapor. Archbishop Simeon, ABDIAS (OBADIAH) (St.) Prophet. (9th cent. B.C.) (Nov. 19) Abdis (Servant of the Lord) is the fourth of the twelve minor prophets, and is generally supposed to have been a contemBut porary of Osee (Hosea), Joel and Amos. some identify him with Achab's steward (3 3), making him much more Kings, xviii. His prophetic writings are short and ancient. are contained in a single chapter of twenty-five verses. He foretells the destruction of Edom on account of the pride of the Idumaeans and of the wrongs they had done to the Jews. (4th cent.) ABDIESUS (HEBEDJESUS) (St.) M. (April 22) Styled a deacon in the Roman Martyrology, he was one of the vast multitude of Persians (named and unnamed), who by the savage edict of their King Sapor were called to the crown of martyrdom. This persecution raged from A.D. 341 to a.d. 380, that is, at intervals during the last forty years of Sapor's reign.

abdon and sennen.name: Abdon And Sennen
abdon and sennen.description: Two Persian nobles who, coming to Rome, or rather brought thither as captives by Decius, when returning from his first successful campaign against the Persians, under the Emperor Gordian, devoted themselves to the service of the imprisoned Christians and to the reverent interring of the bodies of They were themselves thrown the Martyrs. to the wild beasts in the Amphitheatre in the persecution decreed by Decius when he became Emperor (a.d. 250). They were long gratefully remembered by the Christians of Rome and are still annually commemorated in the Liturgy of the Church. The details given concerning them in the otherwise doubtful Acts of St. Laurence the Martyr, their contemporary, seem fairly trustworthy. ABEL (Thomas) (St.) M. See Bl. THOMAS ABEL. (July 30)

abibus.name: Abibus
abibus.description: A Martyr at Edessa in Syria under the Emperor Licinius (a.d. 316). He was burned to death at the stake. (First

abilius.name: Abilius
abilius.description: cent.) (Feb. 22) The third Bishop, in succession to SS. Mark and Anianus, of Alexandria in Egypt, to which See he was advanced A.D. 84, and over which he presided for thirteen The particulars of his life and Episcoyears. pate have been lost. *ABRA (ABRE) (St.) V. (Dec. 13) (4th cent.) A daughter of St. Hilary of Poitiers, born before his father's conversion. Following her father's advice, she consecrated herself to God as a nun ; but died (a.d. 361) when only in her eighteenth year. ABRAHAM (ABRAAMIUS) (St.) Bp. M (Feb. 5) Bishop of Abela in Assyria, a place famous for the victory there of Alexander the over St. Abraham was put to death (a.d. 348) by the persecuting King Sapor II. (4th cent.) Persians. Great ABRAHAM (ABRAAMES) (St.) Bp. (Feb. 14) (5th cent.) A famous Solitary of Mount Lebanon, who, as Bishop of Carrhes (Charan), showed himself a zealous pastor of souls and, later, did much work useful to the Church at the Court of the Emperor Theodosius the Younger. He died at Constantinople, a.d. 422. (March 16) (4th cent.) A hermit of Edessa and native of Chidana in Mesopotamia, famous for his austerity of life, for his fruitful preaching and for the miraculous conversion of his niece, venerated with him as St. Mary. His life was written by St. Ephrem and he is honoured in all the Liturgies. He died about A.D. 360.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.description: The Father of all believers, and the progenitor, according to the flesh, of the Hebrew nation. He is also the father of Ismael, from whom the Ismaelites or Arabs are descended. When seventy years of age, he went forth from Babylonia, his native land, at God's bidding, to dwell henceforth in Canaan, the land flowing with milk and honey promised to his seed. There, he led a pastoral and nomad life. Moreover, God made a covenant with him, changing his name from Abram to Abraham (Father of nations), promising at the same time that his descendants should be more numerous than the stars of Heaven and that in his seed all peoples should " Abraham Of him Our Lord said : be blessed. rejoiced that he might see my day ; He saw it and was glad " (John viii. 56). All through their eventful history it was the glory of the Jewish people to claim descent from him and from his son and grandson, Isaac and Jacob. To them, in words spoken to Moses (Exod. iii. 6), God was the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. The Patriarch died in Palestine at the age of one hundred and seventy-five years These and similar Old Testament (B.C. 1821). dates are given according to the traditional Chronology ; but are still disputed.

abrosimus.name: Abrosimus
abrosimus.description: A Persian priest stoned to death, with many of his flock, under King Sapor II, A.D. 341. (March 2)

abudemius.name: Abudemius
abudemius.description: A native of the Island of Tenedos in the Mge&n Sea who, after enduring frightful torture, was there put to death as a Christian in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian and his colleagues in the first years of the fourth century.

abundius.name: Abundius
abundius.description: A celebrated Bishop of Como in North Italy, charged by Pope St. Leo the Great with the important mission to the Emperor Theodosius the Younger which resulted in the convocation of the great Council of Chalcedon (a.d. 451) and in the final condemnation of the heresiarch Eutyches, who denied the two-fold Nature of Christ God-Man (whence his followers have their name of Monophysites—assertors St. Abundius died of One Nature only). a.d. 469. He is often represented in art in the act of raising a dead man to life, one of the miracles he wrought and which led to his enrolment in the catalogue of Saints.

acathius.name: Acathius
acathius.description: A Christian centurion in the Roman army, at Constantinople under Diocletian 303). Constantine the Great built a noble church in his honour. He is the St. Agazio venerated at Squillace in Calabria. beheaded (a.d. tortured and ACATHIUS (ACACIUS) (St.) Bp. (April 9) (5th cent.) A Bishop of Amida in Mesopotamia, distinguished for his compassionate charity to the Persian prisoners taken in their successful invasion of Persia by the Romans of Constantinople in the reign of King Bahram (or Varannes) V, who is said chiefly on that account to have ceased for a time from perseSt. Acathius died some cuting the Christians. time after a.d. 421. Some of his letters are still extant. ACATIUS (ACATHIUS) M. See SS. PATRITIUS, ACATIUS, &c. (April 28)

acca.name: Acca
acca.description: A disciple of Bosa of York and of St. Wilfrid, and successor of the latter Saint at Hexham. St. Acca was held in the highest veneration by Venerable Bede. He seems to have died (a.d. exile, or shortly after his return to Hexham. acepsimas.name: Acepsimas
acepsimas.description: A venerable old man, Bishop of Honita in Assyria, who was imprisoned, tortured and put to death by King Sapor II of Persia, between a.d. 341 and A.d. 380.

acestes.name: Acestes
acestes.description: One of the three soldiers that tradition tells us were converted by St. Paul, They while acting as guards at his execution. sealed their Faith with their own blood, a few davs later (July 2, A..D. 67).

ache and acheul.name: Ache And Acheul
ache and acheul.description: Otherwise SS. ACIUS and ACEOLUS, which see.

achillas.name: Achillas
achillas.description: hypocrisy (Nov. 7) The Patriarch of Alexandria who Deceived by succeeded St. Peter the Martyr. the notorious heretic Arius, he ordained him priest. Two years later (a.d. 313) St. Achillas passed away, reverenced by all for his many virtues, and had for his successor St. Alexander, who was followed by the great St. Athanasius. the afterwards of

achilles.name: Achilles
achilles.description: A Bishop of Larissa in Thessaly, who died a.d. 331 and is venerated in the East as a Saint.

acisclus and victoria.name: Acisclus And Victoria
acisclus and victoria.description: A brother and sister who, arrested as Christians, underwent many cruel tortures before being beheaded, under Diocletian, at Cordova (a.d. 304). Their cultus is widespread in Spain.

acyllinus.name: Acyllinus
acyllinus.description: See SCILLITAN MARTYRS. (Sept. 19) (July 17) case. each ADAL-, AETHEL-, AL-, AU-, EDIL-, ETHELAll these prefixes to names of Teutonic origin are more or less interchangeable. Thus, St. Etheldreda, St. Ediltrudis, St. Audrey, are one and the same personage. That which appears the more usual manner of spelling a Saint's name in English has, as a rule, been followed in these In Latinising Proper pages in Names, mediaeval writers usually substitute D for TH, or simply omit the H. So, the letter T, especially in terminations, has a tendency to be Again, the terminations BERT replaced by C. and BRIGHT are mere variants. Thus, we talk of St. Cuthbert. but we write Kirkcudbright for the town that takes its appellation from him. In fine, FRED, FRIDE, FRID, FRIDA, FREDE, &c, are undistinguishable. *ADALARDUS (ADELHARDUS, ALARD) (St.) Abbot. (Jan. 2) (9th cent.) An Abbot of Corbie (France), related to the Emperor Charlemagne and one of his chief ministers and advisers. At one time he lost the favour of that monarch's son and successor, Louis the Pious, and was banished. On his return, he gave himself entirely to the discharge of his monastic duties, dying at Corbie, a.d. 827, at the age of seventy-three. During his tenure of office he founded the great Abbev of New Corbie in Saxony.

adalbald.name: Adalbald
adalbald.description: A pious nobleman of the Court He was the of King Clovis II of France. husband of St. Rictrude, and, like their parents, their four children are publicly venerated as St. Adalbald was murdered while on Saints. a journey (A.D. 645), under circumstances which have led to his being honoured in many places as a Martyr.

adalbert.name: Adalbert
adalbert.description: One of the Patron Saints of Bohemia and Poland. A Bohemian bv birth, his infancy to Our "Blessed consecrated in Lady, he was educated by Adalbert, Archbishop of Magdeburg and, on his return to Bohemia, was ordained priest by Diethmar, Archbishop of Prague, whom he succeeded Driven from Prague, he shortly afterwards. retired for a time to the Abbey of St. Boniface in Rome ; and after vain efforts to re-enter his own Diocese, directed his zeal to the conversion of Hungary, Poland and Prussia. His missionary success was great, and his labours only ceased on his receiving the crown of martyrdom at Dantzig (a.d. 997).

adalsindis.name: Adalsindis
adalsindis.description: One of the daughters of SS. Adalbald and Rictrudis, who sanctified herself in the monastery of Hamay, of which her own A.D. 715 is sister, St. Eusebia, was Abbess. given as the year of her death.

adamnan.name: Adamnan
adamnan.description: A monk of Coklingham Abbey in the Saxon Kingdom of Northumbria. He expiated by a long life of austerities and prayer the sins of his youth, and deserved well of the Church by co-operating with St. Ebba in reforming the discipline of the convent which she had founded and over which she presided St. Adamnan himself to the day of her death. passed away about the vear 679. ADAMNAN (ADAM) (St.) Abbot. (Sept. 6) land— " a wise and good man, well versed in (8th cent.) An Irish Abbot of Iona in Scotthe Holy Scriptures "—best known by the Life of St. Columba he has left and by a description of the Holy Places of Palestine which he compiled. He was remarkable for his success Scotland and Ireland the in procuring in adoption of the Roman practice as to the date of Easter. He died A.D. Whether or not he is one and the same with St. Eunan the Patron Saint of the Diocese of Raphoe in His name Ireland, remains an open question. has been popularly abbreviated into Adam, and is still frequently given in Scotland at Baptism. 704. ADAUCUS (ADAUCTUS) (St.) M. (Feb. 7) (4th cent.) By birth an Italian, and an Imperial favourite at the Court of the pitiless Diocletian, who sacrificed him on discovering religion. He was executed in Phrygia his (A.D. 304), and had a number of companions his Martyrdom, some of M'hom were of in senatorial or other high rank. Among them there were also manv women and children. Historians attribute the special barbarity of the tortures he endured rather to the savageness of Galerius, Diocletian's colleague, than to the evil disposition of the old Emperor himself. (July 30)

adauctus and callisthene.name: Adauctus And Callisthene
adauctus and callisthene.description: Ephesians, one of whom, St. Adauctus, suffered under the tyrant Maximinus The Martyr's Daza, year 312. Callisthene, escaped and lived a daughter, saintly life, devoted to works of charity, till her death at Ephesus.

adela.name: Adela
adela.description: The wife of Count Baldwin IV of Flanders who, after her husband's death, took the veil at the hands of Pope Alexander II (A.D. 1067) and retired to the Benedictine Abbey of Messines, near Ipres, where she died a.d. 1071.

adela and irmina.name: Adela And Irmina
adela and irmina.description: Two sisters, daughters of Dagobert, King of the Franks, for whom he founded a monastery at Treves, where their devotedness to the service of the poor led to their being after their deaths honoured as Saints. ADELAIDE (ADELHEID) (St.) Empress. (Dec. 16) (10th cent.) A Burgundian princess, wife of Lothaire, King of Italy, and, after his death and much persecution endured, married to Otho, Emperor of Germany. She was an able woman and, especially during her second widowhood and guardianship of her grandson, Otho III, rendered great services to Church and State, acting as the Peacemaker of Europe in that lawless age. It is said of St. Adelaide that " she never forgot a kindness, nor ever remembered an injury." In the end she retired to a monastery in Alsace, where she died A.D. 999. patiently

adelbert.name: Adelbert
adelbert.description: A Northumbrian by birth and He became said to have been of royal blood. a disciple of St. Egbert and afterwards joined St. Willebrord, in the latter's Apostolate of He was made Archdeacon of the Holland. recently founded See of Utrecht and died at Egmund about A.D. 740.

adelelmus.name: Adelelmus
adelelmus.description: A French monk, who, having given great proofs of skill and piety in the government of his Abbey was called to Spain by King Alphonsus V and there re-established good order and monastic discipline in the monasteries committed to his charge. The date of his death early in the twelfth century is uncertain. (Feb. 5) (11th cent.) An Abbess of Villich (Gueldres),

adelheid.name: Adelheid
adelheid.description: ADELOGA (HADELOGA) (St.) V. Otherwise St. ADELAIDE, ivhich see. (Feb. 2) (8th cent.) A Frankish Princess, daughter of the famous Charles Martel, and foundress of the great Abbey of Kitzingen, under the Rule of St. Benedict (A.D. 745). (Dec. 16)

adelphius.name: Adelphius
adelphius.description: The successor of St. Rufus in the See of Metz, which Diocese he governed for seventeen years, converting many pagans to But nothing certain concerning Christianity. him is known ; and it is only conjeeturally that he is dated in the fifth century. His cultus at Metz from early ages is, however, indisputable ; and the Solemn Translation of his relics to Neuweiler in Alsace in the ninth century was the occasion of great popular rejoicings. ADEODATUS. ADERITUS (ABDERITUS, ADERY) (St.) Bp. Saints of this name are better known as DEUSDEDIT or DIEUDONNE (God-Given). (2nd cent.) A Greek by birth and the first successor of St. Apollinaris (the missionary sent thither by the Apostle St. Peter) in the See of Ravenna, where he died early in the second century. No reliable account of his life now His body, originally buried outside exists. the walls of Ravenna, was in the Middle Ages enshrined in one of the chief churches of the city.

adilia.name: Adilia
adilia.description: Otherwise St. OTHILIA or ODILIA, which ADJUTOR (AJUTRE). (April 30) (12th cent.) A Norman knight who took part in the Crusades, and, on his return from the Holy Land, led the life of a hermit at Vernon on the river Seine, where he died (A.D. 1131).

ado.name: Ado
ado.description: Born in Burgundy of rich and noble parents (a.d. 799), St. Ado was educated in the Benedictine Abbey of Ferrieres in the Ordained priest, he taught Diocese of Sens. sacred and profane science in the Schools of the Abbey of Brum, near Treves. He next spent four years in Rome, engaged in literary researches, and returning to France, discovered at Ravenna much important material from which he published his famous Martyrology. He worked on this at Lyons as the guest of St. Remigius, Archbishop of that city. On the death of Agilmar, Archbishop of Vienne in Dauphine, St. Ado was consecrated his successor and received the Ballium from Fope Nicholas I. He died in the year 875. In art, he is usually represented studying the Scriptures Besides the Martyrology. we have in a library. Dom Quentin (issued in 1908) should be consulted for details.

adolphus.name: Adolphus
adolphus.description: cent.) A Bishop of Osnabruck in Germany, remarkable for his saintliness of life and especially for his self-sacrificing care for the poor. He died A.D. 1222. (13th See SS. EUSEBIUS, MARCELLUS, &c. (Dec. 2)

adrian.name: Adrian
adrian.description: This proper name is also spelled in certain cases with an initial H (Hadrian). cent.) An African by (Jan. 9) birth who embraced the religious life as a Benedictine in Italy and was sent to England with the famous St. Theodore, by Pope St. Vitalian. St. Adrian succeeded St. Benet Biscop as Abbot of Canterbury. He was a man not only of saintly life, but also of great learning and conspicuous ability. He founded in England several schools for the education of vouth. He died A.D. 710. (July 10) (16th cent.) A brave knight, condemned to death for refusing to admit the supremacy in matters of religion of King Henry VIII. He was beheaded on Tower Hill A.D. 1539.

adrian and others.name: Adrian And Others
adrian and others.description: A band of Martyrs (some say many thousands in number) massacred by the Heathen Danes (a.d. 874) in the Isle of May St. Adrian, Bishop of St. (Firth of Forth). Andrews, was leader of this glorious array of Their burial-place was a Christian victims. noted pilgrimage in Catholic Scotland.

adrio, victor and basilla.name: Adrio, Victor And Basilla
adrio, victor and basilla.description: MM. (4th cent.) (May 17) Egyptian Martyrs at Alexandria. It seems certain that they suffered in one of the persecutions of the fourth century, but whether at the hands of the Pagans at its commencement, or later under the Allans, is not clear, all particulars being lost.

adulphus.name: Adulphus
adulphus.description: The brother of St. Botolph, who with that Saint journeyed in his youth from England to Saxony, where he remained for many years and was promoted to the Episcopal dignity. He seems, however, to have returned to England before his death, which happened about the year 700, and his relics were there mingled with those of his holy brother. (March 19) (7th cent.) A disciple of St. Landoald who was murdered by robbers wliile begging alms for his community near Maestricht (a.d. 668 about) and afterwards locally venerated as a Martyr.

adulphus and john.name: Adulphus And John
adulphus and john.description: Martyrs at Cordova in Spain (about a.d. 850) in the fierce persecution under which the Christians suffered under the Moorish Caliph Abderrahman. (Nov. 20) ADVENTOR (S.) iemilian.name: Iemilian
iemilian.description: enlarges especially on his fearless denunciation of the Iconoclasts. He was brought before the Emperor Leo the Armenian, subjected to many indignities, and died in exile (a.d. 820). Cyzicus, standing on the island of the same name off the Southern shore of the Sea of Marmora, was one of the most important of the Greek cities in Asia Minor, a great Christian centre, and boasted of a succession of fifty-nine Bishops. (Sept. 11) In the ancient records of the Church of Vercelli (Piedmont), St. iEmilian is said to have lived as a hermit for forty years before his elevation to the Bishopric of that city. He thrice visited Rome and attended the three Synods held by Pope St. Symmachus. He died, a centenarian in the year 520. Translations of his relics took place in the year 1181 and again towards the end of the seventeenth century. (Oct 11) (Date uncertain.) The Roman Martyrology assigns this St. iEmilian to Rennes in Brittany ; but no trace of a Saint of this name can be found in the Breton records. The Bollandists conclude that iEmilian in this case is a corruption of the name Melanius. A Saint Melanius, according to Albert Legrand and other local authorities, was Bishop of Rennes for sixty-two years and died on the Feast of the Epiphany, In the year 878 the body of this a.d. 567. jetius.name: Jetius
jetius.description: A General in the Christian army and chief among the heroic band of forty-two soldiers who, taken prisoners by the Caliph Montassem (a.d. 836) at Amorium in Syria, resisted all threats and allurements to become Mohammedans, and, after nine years of prison and repeated tortures, were put to death by his orders.

afan.name: Afan
afan.description: A Welsh Saint of the Cunedda family, by some supposed to have been a Bishop. He has given its title to the Church of Llanafan (Brecknock). AFRIQUE (AFRICUS) Bp. (April 28) (7th cent.; A Bishop of Comminges in the South of France, celebrated for his zeal for His memory is still held in great Orthodoxy. veneration, though his shrine and relics were destroyed by the Calvinists in the sixteenth century.
