galganus.description: to (7th cent.) converted Born in Christianity GALL (GALLUS) (St.) Abbot. (Oct. 16) Ireland about the middle of the sixth century and educated in the great monastery of Ben-Chor under the Abbots SS. Comgall and Columban, St. Gall was well versed in the Holy Scriptures. He accompanied St. Columban to England and France (a.d. 585), and assisted in the foundation of the Abbey of Luxeuil. Both St. Columban and St. Gall were banished by King Theodoric, and St. Gall, settling near Lake Constance in the Switzerland, people of that territory. He was chosen Abbot of Luxeuil, A.D. 625, but would not accept the dignity, preferring his poor cell in Switzerland. He died A.D. 646. His Abbey, famous through the Middle Ages, has given its name to one of the Swiss Cantons.

galla.name: Galla
galla.description: Daughter of Symmachus the Younger, a learned Roman. From her childhood she served God, and having lost her husband in early life, she, out of devotion to the Apostles, chose a small cottage on the She reduced Vatican Hill for her dwelling. her body by her austerities to a mere skeleton. Struck by her sanctity, St. Fulgentius of Spain wrote again and again to her. Afflicted with cancer in the breast, she bore her sufferings with incredible patience and resignation, and She is comdied in a.d. 550 or thereabouts. memorated by St. Gregory the Great, almost her contemporary, in his Dialogues. Devotion to her is still very popular in Rome.

gallgo.name: Gallgo
gallgo.description: A Welsh Saint, (Nov. 27) of founder Llanallgo in Anglesey.

gallicanus.name: Gallicanus
gallicanus.description: A General in the army of Constantine who, having promised to become a Christian, should he be victorious, defeated the Scythians in the East. He attained to the Consulate at Rome, but, renouncing the world, soon retired to Ostia, where he founded a Under Hospital and ministered to the sick. Julian the Apostate he was banished to Egypt, and there suffered martyrdom a.d. 362. A church was erected at Alexandria over his tomb, and his Feast is still solemnly kept at Rome, where his memory is associated with that of the Martyrs SS. John and Paul. (July 1) (Feb. 27) attended Pope St. Hilary's Council of Rome (a.d. 465), but about whom no particulars are His relics are venerated at Verona extant. in the ancient Basilica of St. Stephen.

gangulphus.name: Gangulphus
gangulphus.description: A holy layman of a rich and noble Burgundian family, distinguished by his gift of prayer and by his charitable zeal in the cause of the poor and oppressed. He was murdered a.d. 760, at the instigation of his wife's paramour. The circumstances of his death and the miracles wrought at his tomb appear to have led to his being honoured as a Martyr. (Jan. 1)

garbh.name: Garbh
garbh.description: GARBHAN (St.) Abbot. Otherwise St. FANCHEA, which see. (March 26) (7th cent.) The Irish Saint who appears to Nothing have left his name to Dungarvan. certain is known about him. GARDINER (GERMAN) (Bl.) M. GARMIER (GERMIER) (St.)

garnat.name: Garnat
garnat.description: Otherwise St. GERVADIUS, which see. *GASPAR (CASPAR) (St.) (1st cent.) (Jan. 6) The name traditionally given to one of the Three Kings or " Wise Men from the East," who brought their offerings of gold, frankincense and myrrh to the Infant Saviour. Their shrine, formerly at Constantinople, and later at Milan, is now at Cologne.

gatien.name: Gatien
gatien.description: GAUCHER (GAULTIER, WALTER) Otherwise St. GRATIAN, which see. (Feb. 6) (Dec. 18 (April 9) (St.) Abbot. (12th cent.) An Abbot in the Limousin (France), fellow-worker with St. Stephen of Grandmount. He died a.d. 1130, and was the author of a reformed Rule for Canons Regular.

gaudentia and others.name: Gaudentia And Others
gaudentia and others.description: VV.MM. (Date unknown.) St. Gaudentia, a Roman maiden, is said to have suffered with three other Christians in one of the early persecutions ; but the more ancient Martyrologies do not rank her among the Martyrs. All dates and particulars concerning her have been lost.

gaudentius of novara.name: Gaudentius Of Novara
gaudentius of novara.description: Laurence, Bishop of (Jan. 22) (5th cent.) A priest of Ivrea near Turin, who, driven from that city, took refuge with Having St. attended St. Eusebius of Vercelli dining the latter's banishment, brought about by the Arians, St. Gaudentius became the successor of of Episcopate, he converted many sinners, built several churches and reformed his clergy. He passed away about a.d. 418. In his twenty years Laurence. Novara.

gaudentius of verona.name: Gaudentius Of Verona
gaudentius of verona.description: A holy Bishop of Verona in North Italy, who flourished in the middle of the fifth century, and who appears to have St. MM. (4th cent.) St. Gaudentius, a Bishop, and St. Culmatius, his deacon, are stated by the Roman Martyrology to have been murdered by Pagans at Arezzo in Tuscany in the time of 364). With them suffered Andrew, a layman with his wife and children, and other Cliristians to the number of fifty-three. the Emperor Valentinian I (a.d. a.d. later (5th cent.) Ecclesiastical 332.

gaudentius of rimini.name: Gaudentius Of Rimini
gaudentius of rimini.description: An Asiatic born at Ephesus, who came to Rome about A.D. 308, and embraced state. He was ordained the Fourteen he years priest became Bishop of Rimini, and suffered with the other Catholic prelates from the Arians, who dominated the famous Council of a.d. 357. In fine, he was done to death by these enemies of the Faith (a.d. 359 or A.D. 360).

gaudentius of brescia.name: Gaudentius Of Brescia
gaudentius of brescia.description: Educated by St. (Oct. 25) Philastrius, Bishop of Brescia, whom he styles his father, St. Gaudentius entered a monastery in Csesarea of Cappadocia, in order to shun the honours and applause of the world. He early distinguished himself for piety and learning. On as the people of the death of Brescia sought Gaudentius for their Bishop and would have no other, he was forced to return home under pain of excommunication, and was consecrated Bishop of Brescia, a.d. 387. His people showed themselves devoted to him, and he obtained great gain of souls by his sermons, some of which are still extant. In A.d. 405, sent to the East to defend the cause St. Chrysostom, he was imprisoned in of Thrace. He died a.d. 420 or shortly after. Philastrius, (5th

gaudiosus of brescia.name: Gaudiosus Of Brescia
gaudiosus of brescia.description: cent.) The thirteenth (March 7) fifteenth Bishop of Brescia in Lombardy, where his The particulars of his relics are venerated. life are lost, and even the century in which he But a.d. 445 is often flourished is uncertain. given as the year of his holy death.

gaudiosus of salerno.name: Gaudiosus Of Salerno
gaudiosus of salerno.description: A holy Bishop who appears to have occupied the See of Salerno near Naples in the middle of the seventh century, and whose relics are now venerated at Naples. The particulars of his life are lost.

gaudiosus the african.name: Gaudiosus The African
gaudiosus the african.description: A Bishop of Abitina, one among those banished by the Arian Vandal, King Genseric, a.d. 440. He took refuge at Naples, where he built a monastery and crowned a zealous life by a holy death soon after the The ancient mosaic middle of the century. inscription on his tomb lauding his virtues, was still legible in the time of Baronius (end of sixteenth century). (7th cent.) GAUGERICUS (GAU, GERY) (St.) Bp. (Aug. 11) Born in the Diocese of Treves, he was ordained priest by the Bishop of that city, and later made fourth Bishop of Cambrai, which See he ruled with great gain of souls for thirty-nine years, dying A.D. 622. or GEDEON (GIDEON) (St.) of cent. (14th B.C.) The Judge (Sept. 1) Israel (Judges vi.-viii.), commemorated with Josue in the Catholic Church on Sept. 1, on which The day he is also venerated by the Greeks. Copts keep his Feast on Dec. 16 ; and the Armenians on the second Saturday of August. (Aug. 26) (3rd cent.) gelasius.name: Gelasius
gelasius.description: An Abbot of the Columbian Derry. He was consecrated monastery of With St. Archbishop of Armagh, A.D. 1137. Malachy O'Morghair, he held a Synod in the at which fifteen church of Holin Patrick, Bishops and two hundred priests were present. He was the first Irish Bishop privileged to wear the Pallium. In A.d. 1162 he consecrated St. Laurence O'Toole, Archbishop of Dublin. He died March 27, A.D. 1174. of the (Nov. 21) (5th cent.) Roman-born but of African descent, St. Gelasius succeeded St. Felix III in the Chair of St. Peter (A.D. 492). He corrected and in the end converted Euphemius, Bishop of Constantinople, a favourer of the Eutychian heretics and vigorously asserted the rights of the Holy See. He abolished the heathen and otherwise Lupercalia, festival repressed evil living. He was a very learned man, and the Roman Liturgy owes much The famous Sacramentary which to goes under his name contains much that is really due to his talent and research ; and he may be said to have finally fixed the Canon or Order of Books of Holy Scripture. He repressed the Manichaeans by compelling the laity to receive Holy Communion under both kinds, made other useful disciplinary laws, and has left us valuable writings. He died Nov. 21, A.D. 496. him. (Dec. 23)

gemellus.name: Gemellus
gemellus.description: A Christian put to the torture and crucified at Ancyra in Galatia (Asia Minor) under Julian the Apostate, a.d. 362. *GEMMA (St). V.M. (June 20) (Date unknown.) The Christian daughter of a Pagan nobleman in Saintonge (France), who was so severely beaten by her own father for refusing to marry a Pagan that she died of the injuries received in the prison to which she had been consigned.

geminian of modena.name: Geminian Of Modena
geminian of modena.description: A Bishop of Modena, friend of St. Ambrose of Milan and of St. Severus of Ravenna, who took part in the Council of 390.—Another St. Geminian, a Milan, a.d. Bishop (probably also of Modena), about sixty years later, worked with St. Leo the Great to bring about the Council of Chalcedon, and is said to have saved his people from the fury of Attila the Hun.

geminus of fossombrone.name: Geminus Of Fossombrone
geminus of fossombrone.description: See SS. AQUILINUS, GEMINUS, GELA SIUS, Ac.

generosus.name: Generosus
generosus.description: His Relics are enshrined (Mav 15) under the High Altar of Tivoli Cathedral ; but nothing whatever is known of his life or of the date and circumstances of his martyrdom.

genesius.name: Genesius
genesius.description: See SS. ANASTASIUS, PLACIDUS, Ac. (5th cent.) GENEVIEVE (GENOVEFA) (St.) V. (Jan. 3) Born at Nanterre near Paris (A.d. 422), and, when only seven years old, blessed in a special manner by St. Germanus of Auxerre, who foretold her sanctity and the vow of virginity by which she would bind herself. At fifteen she received the veil of the Spouses of Christ, and thenceforth led a life of penance, bearing with heroic patience the calumnies and persecutions which became her She greatly helped the Parisians during lot. the siege of their city by the Franks. Later, she again saved it from destruction, as, through her prayers, Attila the Hun suddenly changed Gaul and his turned aside his army, while still south of Paris. St. Genevieve died a.d. 512. Her relics were at once venerated ; and to a church in which she was buried her name was given. She is Her relics honoured as Patron Saint of Paris. were burned during the great Revolution at the end of the eighteenth century, and her stately church has now been turned into the so-called Pantheon.

gennadius.description: A Benedictine Bishop of Astorga in Spain, which See he resigned to return and prepare for death in his monastery. (May 16)

gennaro.description: GENNYS (GENEWYS) (St.) Bp. Otherwise St. JANUARIUS, which see. (July 26) Otherwise St. GERMANUS of AUXERRE, (Sept. 19) (April 18) (Jan. 3) which see.

george of antioch.name: George Of Antioch
george of antioch.description: A zealous Bishop of Antioch in Pisidia (Asia Minor), previously a monk, one of the Fathers of the Second Council of Nicaea (a.d. 787), and a strenuous champion of the Banished by Faith against the Iconoclasts. the Emperor Leo V the Armenian, he died in exile a.d. 814, and is honoured as a Saint by Greeks and Latins alike.

george the martyr.name: George The Martyr
george the martyr.description: St. George, whom the Greeks style " the great Martyr," though honoured alike in the East and in the West, is one of those Saints of whom we know least. He was an officer in the army of Diocletian, the persecuting Emperor, and for refusing to sacrifice was tortured and beheaded at Nicomedia, a town of Asia Minor on an inlet of the Sea of Marmora (a.d. 303). Some say that St. George was the young Christian who, as Eusebius relates, tore down the Imperial edict of persecution. But of this there is no proof. St. George is usually represented on horseback vanquishing a dragon. This is merely symbolic of the Martyr's victory over the devil ; and in the East is not an unusual emblem of Christian sanctity. The popular legend of St. George and the Dragon Equally baseless are the is of course fabulous. now discredited assertions once common among Non-Catholics, that St. George is a myth ; that he Cappadocia, is murdered The to Western Crusaders gave George, though venerated devotion From about the in the West long before. thirteenth century, he came to be regarded as Patron of England, partially displacing St. Edward the Confessor. One of the English monks who accompanied St. Colman on his retirement (A.D. 664) from Northumbria to Ireland, on occasion of the dispute about the date of Easter. St. Gerald at the head of the English House founded by him, which is said to have been the nursery of over one hundred Saints, a.d. 732 is given as the year of St. Gerald's death, at a very advanced age. In Mayo, St. Colman placed (11th

gerald of aurillac.name: Gerald Of Aurillac
gerald of aurillac.description: A Count of Aurillac, who led a life of great virtue and practised in the world the penitential exercises of the cloister. He denied himself every comfort in order to relieve the distress of the poor. He was scrupulously just and at the same time most considerate in his dealings with his numerous vassals. He died a.d. 909, and many miracles attested his sanctity.

gerald of beziers.name: Gerald Of Beziers
gerald of beziers.description: Saint (Nov. 5) (called by the French St. Guiraud) was a Canon Regular, who became Bishop of Beziers in the South of France. He spent all his revenues in relieving the distress of the poor of his Diocese. He died A.d. 1123. (12th cent.) This

gerard of toul.name: Gerard Of Toul
gerard of toul.description: A native of Cologne who, in his youth, having seen his own mother struck dead by lightning, embraced a life of penance. Made Bishop of Toul (a.d. 963), he rebuilt his Cathedral and otherwise benefited his Diocese. A learned man himself, he gathered Greek and other scholars around him. He died a.d. 994, in the odour of sanctity, and was canonised by Pope St. Leo IX, who had been one of his successors in the See of Toul. (April 28) (Probably 7th cent.) An English pilgrim, a companion of St. Ardwine. He died at Gallinaro in the South of Italy while on the pilgrimage to Palestine, and is there liturgically honoured as a Saint and Patron of the district. The century in which he flourished is a matter of controversy.

gerard of hungary.name: Gerard Of Hungary
gerard of hungary.description: A Benedictine monk of Venice, invited to Hungary by St. Stephen, First St. Gerard Christian King of that country. became one of its Apostles. Made Bishop of Chunad, he converted two-thirds of the populaIn the disorders which tion to Christianity. followed on the death of St. Stephen, he was set upon by the Pagans and cruelly done to His relics were afterwards death (a.d. 1046). Venice, where they are now translated to honoured.

gerard.name: Gerard
gerard.description: An Official of noble birth at the Court of the Prince-Counts of Namur, who relinquished prospects of high advancement in the world to become a simple monk at Sent back after five years St. Denis near Paris. to Namur, he spent the rest of his life in reforming the discipline of the Flemish monasteries, Having eighteen of which received his Rule. obtained the Papal approbation of his Reform, he passed to his reward A.D. 959.

gerard majella.name: Gerard Majella
gerard majella.description: A Redemptorist Saint, born A.D. 1725, in the South of Italy, who to the customary vows of the Religious life added that of ever doing that which was most perfect. His life of prayer and humble obedience drew down to him marvellous supernatural graces. He worked many miracles in his life, and they have been multiplied since his holy death THE BOOK OF SAINTS GERMANUS cent.) (12th (a.d. 1755). He is now the object of much popular devotion throughout the world.

gerard of potenza.name: Gerard Of Potenza
gerard of potenza.description: Piacenza, Born at (Oct. 30) he was enrolled among the clergy of Potenza in the South of Italy, and, on account of his virtues, elected Bishop of that city, although already advanced in age. He died in the ninth year of his Episcopate (a.d. 1119). Several miracles having borne witness to his sanctity, Pope Callistus II canonised him a few years later.

gerasimus.name: Gerasimus
gerasimus.description: A monk at first in Lycia (Asia Minor) and afterwards in Palestine, where, in a monastery which he had founded on the banks of the Jordan, in the neighbourhood of Jericho, He died a.d. he trained numerous disciples. In his youth, for some time a follower of 475. the heretic Eutychcs, he for all the rest of his life did severe penance for his fault. GEREBERN (GEREBRAND) (St.) M. (May 15) St. Gerebern or Gerebrand was the Irish priest who accompanied St. Dympna in her flight to Belgium, and who was privileged to share with her her crown of Martyrdom at Gheel in that country. They suffered some time in the seventh century, but the records are St. Gerebern is Patron Saint very imperfect. of a village in Rhenish Prussia, where his relics are enshrined. (7th cent.)

geremarus.name: Geremarus
geremarus.description: Born A.D. 608, of rich and noble parents, the Merovingian King Dagobert I made him (with his friends Eloi and Ouen) Royal Councillors. By his saintly wife, Domana, he had three children, of whom the youngest, Amalberga, is honoured as a Saint. When free to do so, he entered a monastery, and later became its Abbot ; but, after an attempt on his life, he retired for five years to a hermit's Finally, he founded another monastery cell. near Beauvais, and a few years afterwards died a holy death as Abbot of the same (a.d. 658).

gereon and others.name: Gereon And Others
gereon and others.description: These heroic Christians, three hundred and nineteen in number, appear to have formed part of the famous Theban Legion, massacred by order of the Emperor Maximian St. Gereon would therefore be the (a.d. 286). officer in command of the detachment. St. Hanno of Cologne discovered and enshrined their remains in the eleventh century.

gerinus.name: Gerinus
gerinus.description: The brother of St. Leger (Leodegarius) and, like him, persecuted by Ebroin, Mayor of the Palace to the Merovingian " roi faineant," Thierry III. Stoned to death near 676), he was honoured by the Arras (a.d. people as a Saint and a Martyr.

gerlach.name: Gerlach
gerlach.description: A holy hermit in great veneration at Liege and Aix-la-Chapelle. He lived a life of singular austerity and seclusion, but did wonders for the winning of souls to God and was much esteemed and honoured by the Popes of his time. He died a.d. 1170.

german gardiner.name: German Gardiner
german gardiner.description: Of German (Jermyn) Gardiner, Secretary of the Bishops of Winchester, it is not known whether he was a priest or a layman. He won the Crown of Martyrdom about a.d. 1544. (16th cent.)

germana.name: Germana
germana.description: GERMANA (GERMAINE) COUSIN Spe SS. PAUL, GERONTIUS, &c. (Jan. 19) (June 15) (St.) V. (17th cent.) A poor girl, daughter of a farm labourer in the neighbourhood of Toulouse (South of France), who passed her short and innocent life in minding sheep and other out-ofBoth from ill-health and from door rural work. ill-treatment at the hands of a stepmother, her days passed in suffering patiently borne, comforted only by Almighty God, who privileged her by close union with Himself in high prayer, until He called her to a better life, a.d. 1601, when she had entered on the twenty-second Forty years after her death year of her age. her body was found incorrupt. Passing into Gaul, he did much Apostolic work, and in the end was put to death for the Faith in Normandy, about A.D. 460. GERMANUS of CONSTANTINOPLE (May 12) he resisted (6th cent.) (St.) Bp. With undaunted courage the Monothelites and the Iconoclasts, even refusing to publish the Imperial Edict (a.d. 725), by which the honouring of Holy Pictures was In consequence, he was banished, interdicted. and died in exile (a.d. 733).

germanus of paris.description: Born near Autun (a.d. 496), he was there ordained priest, and became Abbot of Happening to be in Paris when a monastery. the See was vacant, he was elected (a.d. 554) Bishop of that city. On account of his charity styled the " Father of the Poor," he by his zeal and example wrought a wonderful change in the morals of the people, converting even the careless King Childebert to the living of a The latter founded the monaChristian life. stery of St. Vincent (now known as S. Germain des Prte), in which he was buried (a.d. 561), and after him (a.d. 576) the holy Bishop, his truest friend, to whose sanctity many miracles St. Germanus' account have borne witness. of the Gallican Rite is liturgically of great value.

germanus and randoald.name: Germanus And Randoald
germanus and randoald.description: St. Germanus was a citizen of Treves and disciple of St. Arnulph of Metz. He became a monk of Luxeuil under the Irish Rule of St. Columbanus ; and later was appointed Abbot of a monastery in Switzerland. In his struggles with the neighbouring Barons, undertaken in order to save the villagers of the district from spoliation and murder, he was put to death by the marauding soldiery about a.d. 666. A fellow-monk, by name Randaut or Randoald, shared with him the crown of martvrdom.

germanus of auxerre.name: Germanus Of Auxerre
germanus of auxerre.description: Born at Auxerre, about A.D. 378, of noble parents, he studied Civil Law in Rome, married a lady of rank equal to his own, and by the Emperor Honorius, was made Governor {Dux) of his native Province. From a.d. 418, his manner of life, up to then far from edifying, underwent a complete change. He received (7th cent.) (5th cent.) Saxons. Later, he again priest's orders, and very soon became "Rishop of Auxerre, which Diocese he governed with wonderful gain to souls for thirty years. His successful mission with St. Lupus of Troyes, to Britain against the Pelagians, has made him famous there, where several churches have been dedicated to him. It was then that he led the islanders to their famous Alleluia victory over the visited Britain, and is said to have ordained the great Welsh Saints, Dubritius and Illtyd. Engaged in an errand of mercy to the Court of the Eraperer Valentinian III, he died at Ravenna in His body at his Italy (July 31, a.d. 448). dying request was brought back to Auxerre. His remains were destroyed during the French Revolution. Among the striking miracles he wrought, his raising up from the dead the son of Volusian, Secretary to Sigisvult the Patrician, is the most famous.

germanus of besancon.name: Germanus Of Besancon
germanus of besancon.description: The successor of St. Desideratus in the See of Besancjon. Particulars of his life have been lost, but it appears certain that he met his death at the hands of heretics (probably Allans) about the end of the fourth century. (4th cent.)

gerold.name: Gerold
gerold.description: An Irish chieftain, brother of St. Breaca, who settled in Cornwall, near Mount's Bay. Outside St. Germoc's church, a stone called St. Germoc's Chair may still be seen. (April 19) (10th cent.) A member of the Ducal House of Saxony who embraced the life of a Solitary in the Tyrol and attained to high sanctity. His grave is still a place of pilgrimage, and his memory is especially honoured in the Abbey Church of Einsiedeln in Switzerland.

gerontius.name: Gerontius
gerontius.description: A Bishop of Cervia, near Ravenna, who attended a Synod held in Rome by Pope Symmachus (a.d. 501) and who was attacked and murdered on his return journey, at Cagli on the Flaminian Way, under circumstances which led to his being honoured as a Martyr. *GERONTIUS (GERAINT) (St.) Son of Erbin, and (Aug. 10) King of King, M. (6th cent.) of (7th cent.) (7th cent.) Damnonia (Devon). He fell in battle against the Saxons (a.d. 508). Much romantic legend has been woven about his life and that of his Another St. Gerontius, King of wife, Enid. Cornwall, died A.D. 596. St. Gerrans in Cornwall and St. Geran in Brittany have the one or the other for Patron Saint.

gertrude of hamage.name: Gertrude Of Hamage
gertrude of hamage.description: The widow of a nobleman in the present Belgium, who retired into a solitary place in order to live the life of an Anchoress ; but soon found herself at the head of a numerous community of nuns who had gathered round her. She died about A.D. 655.

gertrude of nivelles.name: Gertrude Of Nivelles
gertrude of nivelles.description: The daughter Pepin of Landen, Mayor of the Palace to King Clotaire II and to two of his successors. When only twenty-one years old, Gertrude was placed at the head of the Abbey of Nivelles, in which her own mother, Itta, its foundress thenceforth St. Gertrude lived as her daughter's subject. was distinguished for her care of the poor and for culture of mind remarkable in that age, though far from uncommon in the monasteries She is said to have known nearly of the time. the whole Bible by heart. In art, she is usually depicted so absorbed in contemplation that a mouse quietly climbs up the Pastoral Staff at She passed the three last years of her her side. life almost entirely in exercises of devotion and penance, falling asleep in Christ some time between a.d. 659 and a.d. 664, at the early age of thirty-three.

gertrude.name: Gertrude
gertrude.description: The holy nun of singular learning and endued with high gifts of mystic prayer, who has left us the " Insinuationes Divinse Pietatis," a work comparable to the writings of St. Teresa, and enriched with sublime imagery. Tradition assigns Eisleben in Saxony as her birthplace, and makes her Abbess successively But modern of Rudersdorff and of Heldelfs. research distinguishes the Abbess St. Gertrude from her contemporary the mystic Saint of the same name, a nun in the monastery of the former. They flourished in the latter half of the thirteenth century, and Nov. 17, A.D. 1334, is assigned as the date of the death of the surThat St. Mechtildis, another celebrated vivor. mystic writer, was sister of either St. Gertrude is also now controverted. The Church keeps the Feast of St. Gertrude on Nov. 15, though is found noted on in certain Kalendars it The confusing together April 12 or Nov. 12. of two or more Saints of the same name has The works evidently led to this discrepancy. of SS. Gertrude and Mechtelde, edited by the Solesmes, may be usefully Benedictines consulted. of

gerulph.name: Gerulph
gerulph.description: A youth in Flanders, heir to a great estate and distinguished for the holiness of his life, who on his way back from the church where he had received the Sacrament of Confirmation was treacherously murdered by a relative in hopes of succeeding to his inheritance. St. Gerulph died (about a.d. 746) pardoning his murderer, and is venerated as a Martyr at Tronchiennes. (5th cent.)

geruntius of milan.name: Geruntius Of Milan
geruntius of milan.description: The successor at Milan in the fifth century of St. Eusebius. He appears to have governed the Diocese for about five years, 470, though no reliable account dying a.d. of his Episcopate has reached us. St. Charles Borromeo enshrined his Relics in the church of St. Svmphorian in the city of Milan. (1st cent.)

geruntius.name: Geruntius
geruntius.description: A Missionary in Spain in the Apostolic Age, reckoned as Bishop of Talco (Seville). A special Hymn in the old Mozarabic Breviary commemorates him. *GERVADIUS (GERNAD, GARNAT) (St.) (Nov. 8) (10th cent.) An Irish Saint, who crossed over THE BOOK OF SAINTS GLYCERIA (1st cent.) to Moray and afterwards retired as a recluse to near Elgin.

gervase and protase.name: Gervase And Protase
gervase and protase.description: Two brothers, sons (June 19) the Martyr, St. Vitalis, were Christian heroes who have ever been held in high honour in the St. Ambrose styled them the Western Church. Proto-Martyrs of Milan, where they suffered in the first century of our era, either under Domitian. Many miracles Nero or illustrated the discovery and Translation of their relics by St. Ambrose, towards the close of the fourth century. They now repose at Milan in the Ambrosian Basilica. under of

primitivus.name: Primitivus
primitivus.description: Roman Martyrs who suffered 117-138). They were under Hadrian (a.d. scourged and tied to the stake to be burned But miraculously spared by the flames, alive. they were in fine clubbed to death. St. Getulius is said to have been a man distinguished both by birth and by learning. (May 8) (5th and 6th cent.) An Irish Saint who, with his five brothers and three sisters, crossed over to France and led a life of penance and conHis relics templation near Chfilons-sur-Marne. were enshrined in Rheims Cathedral, many miracles worked both during his life and after his death attesting his great sanctity. at cent.) Born Sempringham (Feb. 4) in Lincolnshire and ordained priest by the Bishop of Lincoln, he became Parish Priest of his native village, distributing yearly to the poor the revenues of his benefice. He founded a convent of nuns and afterwards an Order of men, which he himself joined, the Rule having been approved by Pope Eugene III. He lived the life of penance and zeal he had thus professed till his holy death (Feb. 3, 1190), having, it is said, reached the age of one hundred and six years. He was canonised His Order, once widespread in England, has been long extinct. 1202. a.d.

gilbert.name: Gilbert
gilbert.description: For twenty years Bishop of Caithness, of which Diocese he built the Cathedral. He was a zealous Pastor of souls, and also a valued servant of the Scottish Kings of his time. He died a.d. 1240. Many miracles are recorded of him.

gilbert of hexham.name: Gilbert Of Hexham
gilbert of hexham.description: GILBERT (St.) Bp. See SS. ALCHMUND and GILBERT. Otherwise St. TILBERT, which see. (Sept. 7) (Oct. 2) GILDARD (GODARD) (St.) Bp. (June 18) (6th cent.) A Bishop of Rouen, once erroneously supposed to have been the brother of St. Medard of Soissons. He assisted at the Council of Orleans (a.d. 511), and governed his own Church with great zeal for about fifteen years, dying probably early in the same century. Buried at Rouen, his remains were afterwards removed to Soissons.

gildas the elder.name: Gildas The Elder
gildas the elder.description: He appears to have been associated with St. Cadoc at Llancarvan and to have afterwards lived as a hermit in an island off Glastonbury Abbey the South coast of Wales. claimed to have been the scene of his death, and to have possessed his relics. He is often confused with his namesake, the more famous Gildas the Wise.

gilbert of auvergne.name: Gilbert Of Auvergne
gilbert of auvergne.description: A Saint of the Order of PraeNorbertine Canons. He monstratensians or founded the Abbey of Neuffontaines, where he died a.d. 1152. In his early life he had fought as a Crusader in Palestine.

gildas the wise.name: Gildas The Wise
gildas the wise.description: Often cent.) (6th (Jan. 29) called BADONICUS, GILES (/EGIDIUS) (St.) because born in the year the Britons defeated the Saxons at Bath. He was brought up with SS. Samson, Paul de Leon, and other holy men, by the famous St. Illtyd. He crossed over into Brittany and there wrote the works on The Ruin of his Fatherland, which have perpetuated his memory in the British Isles. He established in Brittany the monastery of Rhuys, but appears to have passed the last years of his life (which ended about a.d. 570) in a hermitage. He is liturgicallv honoured throughout Brittany. (7th cent.) (Sept. 1) Said to have been by birth a Greek. He passed his life as a hermit in the France. The many miracles he South of wrought made him famous in the West of Europe, as is evidenced by popular devotion and by the many churches which bear his name. He died early in the eighth century. Butler notes the very common confusing of this St. Giles with another Saint of the same name who was Abbot near Aries about two hundred vears earlier. GISLAIN (GHISLAIN, GUISLAIN) (St.) Bp. (Oct. 9) (7th cent.) A Bishop (or possibly only an Abbot) in Hannonia (Belgium), who flourished in the seventh century, and, being himself by birth a Greek, introduced into the monastery he founded the Oriental Rule of St. Basil. He died a.d. 681, leaving his name to the town which rose up round his monastery.

gislain.name: Gislain
gislain.description: A holy hermit in Luxemburg, much venerated in Belgium.

gistilian.name: Gistilian
gistilian.description: The uncle of St. David and a monk of the present Menevia or St. David's, to which place the monastery was transferred from its old site in the Roman Settlement now obliterated in the sands of Whitsand Bay.

gladys.name: Gladys
gladys.description: A Welsh Saint, daughter of the famous Brychan of Brecknock, wife of St. Gundleus, and mother of St. Cadoc.

glaphyra.name: Glaphyra
glaphyra.description: A Christian maiden in (Jan. 13) the service of Constantia, wife of the Emperor Licinius, who, to escape the unlawful attentions of her master, fled to the Bishop of the place (St. Basil of Amasea in Pontus), was pursued, captured and sentenced to death. Some say that the sentence was executed, others that she again escaped and passed away in peace, about A.D. 324. to

glastianus.name: Glastianus
glastianus.description: The Patron Saint of Kinglassie As mediator between the Picts and in Fife. Scots, he did much to. alleviate the lot of the former when subjugated by their enemies. He died A.D. 830. (July 24) Betrothed a young noble,

gleb.name: Gleb
gleb.description: GLODESIND (St.) V. See SS. ROMANUS and DAVID. (July 25) (7th cent.) A French Saint of Merovingian her times. promised husband was arrested on their wedding day and afterwards condemned and executed. Glodesind took refuge in the cloister, and died Abbess of a convent at Metz (a.d. 608) in great fame of sanctity.

glunshalaich.name: Glunshalaich
glunshalaich.description: A famous Irish penitent, converted by St. Kevin and buried in the same grave with him at Glendalough. GLUVIAS (GLYWYS) (St.) cent.) A brother of (May 2) St. Cadoc of Llancarvan, and possibly sent by him into Cornwall, where he made a monastic foundation. A parish in Cornwall perpetuates his name.

glyceria.name: Glyceria
glyceria.description: A Roman by birth, this Christian maiden, who was living with her father at Trajanopolis in Greece, suffered there for the Faith, being thrown to the wild beasts in the enduring many cruel Amphitheatre, after (6th The date of her martyrdom, under torments. one of the Antonines, probably Marcus Aurelius, in the last half of the second century, cannot precisely be fixed. A magnificent church was dedicated to her at Heraclea of Thessaly,

glycerius.name: Glycerius
glycerius.description: A priest of Nicomedia in Asia Minor, who in the persecution under Diocletian, after bravely enduring the torture, bore witness to the Faith at the stake, A.D. 303. (May 2)

goban.name: Goban
goban.description: *GOBAN (GOBHNENA) (St.) (6th and 7th cent.) (May 23) Supposed to be the Goban mentioned in the Life of St. Laserian as governing the monastery of Old-Leighlin, retirement, he from which seeking greater betook himself to Tascafnn, a solitude in the present countv of Limerick. *GOBNATA (GOBNET) (St.) V. (6th cent, probably.) (Feb. 11) St. Abban is said to Ballyvourney have founded a convent (Cork), and to have placed St. Gobnet over it as Abbess. A well still exists there called* in

gobrian.name: Gobrian
gobrian.description: A Breton monk who became Bishop of Vannes, and at the age of eighty-seven resigned his See to retire to a hermit's cell, where he died a.d. 725.

godric.name: Godric
godric.description: after enduring much cruel treatment at the hands of her inhuman husband, was at length (a.d. 1070) murdered by him. She has ever since been venerated in Belgium, and especially at Ghent, as a Martyr. (12th cent.) A native of (May 21) Norfolk, who, after having passed some years in trade, resolved upon embracing a higher life. He made several pilgrimages, and finally settled in a hermitage in the neighbourhood of Durham. Almighty God favoured him with the power of working miracles and with other supernatural gifts. He died a.d. 1170, and is the Title Saint of many churches.

goeznoveus.name: Goeznoveus
goeznoveus.description: A Cornish Saint, brother of St. Maughan, who passing over into Brittany, became Bishop of Leon. A.D. 675 is given as the date of his death.

gofor.name: Gofor
gofor.description: A Welsh Saint, Patron of Llano ver in Monmouthshire. *GOLLEN (COLAN, COLLEN) (St.) (May 21) (7th cent, probably). The Saint who has given his name to Llangollen in Denbighshire. There are legendary Lives connecting him with Wales, Rome and Glastonbury ; but nothing is known for certain about him, though from the Dedication of a church to him in Brittany it may be conjectured that he resided for some time in that country. *GOLVINUS (GOLWEN) (St.) Bp. (July 9) (7th cent, probably.) A Breton Saint but of British origin, whose fame for sanctity led to his appointment as Bishop of St. Paul de Leon. After a useful pastorate he passed away at Rennes where his relics were enslirined.

goneri.name: Goneri
goneri.description: An exile from Great Britain to Brittany, where he led a holy life as a hermit near Treguier.

gonsalvo.name: Gonsalvo
gonsalvo.description: A Portuguese priest of eminent sanctity, who, after suffering much for justice's sake, entered the Dominican Order, and of whom many miracles are related. He died about A.D. 1259. GONTRAM (GUNTRAMNUS) King. Clotilde. He became King of (March 28) (6th cent.) A grandson of Clovis and of Orleans St. in the partition of the Frankish monarchy and governed his people in justice and mercy, going so far as to pardon two of his would-be assassins. His sin in divorcing his wife and over-hastily ordering the execution of his physician, like David, he wept over till the day of his death, which happened A.D. 593, when he was in his Beloved by his subjects, he sixty-ninth year. was at once by them acclaimed as a Saint. Miracles as well in life as after death are attributed to him. Feast, though kept on various days, is put in the Roman Martyrology. as by the Greeks, on March 25, from an old belief that Our Lord's Crucifixion, and therefore the Good Thief's confession, fell on that day in the year of the T^ocsioti *GORAN (WORANUS) (St.) (April 7) Several Cornish churches are dedicated in honour of this Saint, a contemporary and friend of St. Petrock. (6th cent.) GORCUM (MARTYRS OF) (SS.) (July 9) Nineteen Catholics of holy life (16th cent.) ; THE BOOK OF SAINTS GREGORY

gordian.name: Gordian
gordian.description: cruelly put to death (A.d. 1572) by the Protestants at Gorcum, near Dordrecht in Holland. Ten of them were Franciscan Friars, two Pre-monstratensiaDS, one a Dominican, one a Canon Regular, four Secular priests, and one a layman. The savagery of the Dutch Calvinists is notorious ; but one is appalled in reading the tortures, physical and moral, to which these nineteen Martyrs were subjected, before being hanged, the one charge against them being that they were faithful Catholics. They were canonised by Pope Pius IX (a.d. 1867). (May 10) (4th cent.) A Roman judge, who being still a Pagan, undertook to carry out the persecuting Edict of the Emperor Julian the Apostate. Converted at length himself to Christianity by witnessing the fortitude of the Martyrs, he was baptised with his wife, Maxima, and fifty-two Arrested and tried of his household retainers. in his turn, he was beheaded, after torture, in Rome, A.D. 362. His relics, with those of St. Epimachus of Alexandria (who suffered under Decius a.d. 250), are now venerated at Kempten in Bavaria. St. Epimachus is again honoured with a St. Alexander on Dec. 12.

gordius.name: Gordius
gordius.description: Later, returning to the city, (Jan. 3) A Christian soldier of Csesarea in Cappadocia, who in the time of the Emperor Licinius, with other Christians, was dismissed from the army and thereupon retired into a solitude. he, moved by his zeal in the cause of Christ, addressed the crowd, seeking to make converts. He was seized and, after trial, beheaded in some year between a.d. 314 and a.d. 320. An eloquent Panegyric preached by St. Basil, in which he reminds his hearers that some among them had seen St. Gordius die, has perpetuated his memory.

gorgonia.name: Gorgonia
gorgonia.description: A holy woman, sister of St. Gregory N azianzen who has left us a Panegyric dwelling upon the eminence in virtue and holiness of his dead sister. Before her death (A.D. 375, about), she saw her husband, children and grandchildren, received into the Church by the Sacrament of Baptism. Her own aged parents seem to have survived her. GORGONIUS and FIRMUS (FIRMINUS) (SS.) MM. (3rd cent.) Some say that (March 11) holy these at Nicaea in Bithynia Confessors suffered others at Antioch in Syria ; but nothing precise is known about them, save that they were victims of one of the third century persecutions. (Sept. 9) See SS. DOROTHEUS and GORGONIUS.

gormgall.name: Gormgall
gormgall.description: An Irish Saint, head of the monastery of Ardoilen and famous as a spiritual guide. He died A.d. 1016.

gothard.name: Gothard
gothard.description: A holy hermit, whose cell was situated high up in the Alps, and who has left his name to the neighbouring Mons Adulas, now the St. Gothard.

gotteschalk.name: Gotteschalk
gotteschalk.description: The son of the chief of one of the Sclavonic tribes who distinguished himself greatly in battle, and becoming a Christian . devoted himself to the spreading of the Faith among the heathens on the shores of the Baltic. He was murdered in a church by the Pagans, A.D. 1066. GOTTFRIED (GODFREY) (Bl.) (Jan. 15) (12th cent.) A Premonstratensian Canon, disciple and trusted friend of St. Norbert, Founder of the Order. He was remarkable for the austere sanctity of his life, and his devoted (May 4) service of all in suffering or distress. He died A.D. 1127 ; and his relics were enshrined at Cappenberg. *GOWAN (GOVAN, GOVEN, COFEN) (St.) (Dec. 28) (5th cent.) The wife of King Tewdrig of Glamorgan. The parish of Llangoven takes its name from her ; and a chapel in Pembrokeshire is likewise dedicated in her honour.

grace and probus.name: Grace And Probus
grace and probus.description: Two Cornish Saints, it is said, husband and wife ; but nothing is now known about them. They are Patron Saints of the Parish of Tresilian. GRACILIANUS and FELICISSIMA (Aug. 12) (SS.) MM. (4th a cent.) Christian Gracilianus, of Faleria, an old Tuscan town, since destroyed, suffered in the great persecution in the first It is related how, years of the fourth century. whilst in prison, a widow brought to him her to whom he blind Felicissima, miraculously restored her sight and gave Holy Gracilianus and his convert were Baptism. beheaded on the same day. daughter, (May 1) (4th cent.) A holy woman of Bergamo in the North of Italy who, having had the consolation of bringing to the true Faith her husband and her parents, after the death of the former, devoted herself to the doing of good works. She was especially zealous in securing Christian She passed burial for the bodies of the Martyrs. away Aug. 27, a.d. 305.

grata.name: Grata
grata.description: GRATINIANUS (GRATIANUS) (St.) M. (June 1) See SS. FELINUS and GRATINIANUS. GRATIAN (GATIEN) (St.) Bp. (Dec. 18) (Date uncertain.) The first Bishop of Tours in France. The tradition was that he was a disciple of the Apostles, sent by them to France in the first century of our era. But Baronius and the moderns post-date his mission to the time of Pope St. Fabian, in the middle of the In one of the troubled years of third century. his Episcopate he is said for a time to have lain concealed in a cave on the banks of the Loire, &t a spot where later rose the great Abbey of Marmoutier. in 1793, during the French Revolution. His relics destroyed were

gratus.name: Gratus
gratus.description: *GREDIFAEL (St.) (Dec.5) (Nov. 13) (7th cent.) A Breton or Welsh Saint who accompanied St. Padarn from Brittany to Wales. He is said to have been Abbot of Whitland in Pembrokeshire. (May 4) (May 4) See SS. JULIUS, POTAMIA, <fcc. *GREEN (THOMAS) (Bl.) M. See CARTHUSIAN MARTYRS. GREENWOOD (WILLIAM) (Bl.) M. See CARTHUSIAN MARTYRS.

gregory of langres.name: Gregory Of Langres
gregory of langres.description: A principal citizen of Autun, who, having lost his wife, became a priest, and ultimately Bishop of Langres (North-East of France). He converted many of the inhabitants of the surrounding villages who were as yet heathens, and drew a still greater number of lax Christians to the leading of a better life. He died a.d. 541, in the thirty-third year of his Episcopate, and was succeeded by his own son, Tetricus.

gregory x.name: Gregory X
gregory x.description: One of the Visconti, an illustrious Italian family, and born at Piacenza. Theobald, the future Pope Gregory X, had given himself up to a life of study when he was appointed Archdeacon of (Belgium), and charged with the preaching of the last In the Holy Land, whither he had Crusade. betaken himself, he received (a.d. 1271) the The five news of his election to the Papacy. years of his Pontificate were made memorable by the celebration of the great Oecumenical Council of Lyons, attended by over five hundred Bishops. A solemn, though unhappily not lasting, Union of the Greek and Latin Churches Liege of was there effected. The holy Pontiff died Feb. 16, A.D. 1276, at Arezzo in Tuscany, on his way back to Rome.

gregory ii.name: Gregory Ii
gregory ii.description: years, sixteen initiated (Feb. 13) (8th cent.) Roman-born and educated at the Papal Court, St. Gregory II became a Benedictine monk, and was made Librarian or Archivist of the Roman Church. He succeeded Pope Constantine (a.d. 715) and, during his the Pontificate conversion of Germany, by despatching thither as missionaries SS. Boniface and Corbinian. He boldly opposed the outbreak of Iconoclasm and successfully under Leo the Isaurian, resisted the aggression of King Luitprand and his Lombards, restoring likewise many churches and monasteries (among them the Abbey of Monte Cassino) destroyed by these Barbarians. St. Gregory frustrated several attempts of the Eastern Emperor to seize or even murder him, and passed away in peace, Feb. 10, a.d. 731. He was (writes Anastasius Bibliothecarius) " a man, pure in life, learned in Holy Scripture, eloquent of speech, and of resolute will."

gregory of nyssa.name: Gregory Of Nyssa
gregory of nyssa.description: The brother of St. Basil the Having received a good education and Great. married a virtuous lady, he afterwards renounced the world and went to assist his holy brother and to be later consecrated Bishop of Nyssa Banished by the in Cappadocia (A.D. 372). intrigues of the Arian faction, he was restored to his See in 378, and died at Nyssa some time between A.D. 395 and a.d. 400. St. Gregory was one of the most prominent of the Fathers who attended the Second General Council, His copious that of Constantinople (a.d. 381). writings are remarkable for eloquence of diction, and are most valuable on account of the powerful and accurate exposition of Orthodox doctrine they embodv.

gregory the great.name: Gregory The Great
gregory the great.description: Doctor of the Church. (7th cent.) The most commanding figure Born in Rome in the world history of his age. (a.d. 540) of patrician parents (the Senator Sylvia), and a collateral Gordian and St. descendant of Pope St. Felix (whether II, III, or IV, is uncertain), he was early in life made Praetor or Governor of Rome by the Emperor Relinquishing, however, his prosJustin II. pects of a brilliant future in the world, he retired to the monastery into which he had converted his family mansion on the Ccelian Hill (San Gregorio). But Pope Benedict I soon appointed him his Apocrisiarius or Legate to Constantinople, where he remained for seven years. At the death of Pope Pelagius (a.d. 590), Gregory, after vainly trying by flight to avoid the dignity, was elected his successor. During his thirteen years of Pontificate, his untiring energy (despite continuous ill-health) enabled him to accomplish a very thorough Reform of Church discipline, both among the Secular clergy and in Religious Houses. His work in Liturgy and Church music has proved lasting. He dealt successfully with the yet existing debris of the old heresies, as is proved by his voluminous correspondence with Spain, Gaul, Ireland, and with the Eastern Patriarchates. He strenuously upheld the rights of the Roman See against the pretensions of the Patriarchs of Constantinople ; but treated so wisely with the Byzantine Emperor and other Christian Princes as to avoid all conflict with His sending of St. Augustine with his them. forty monks, as first missionaries to the AngloSaxons, has earned him the title of Apostle of England. He saved Rome from oppression by the Lombards, who at that time were devastating Italy, and showed himself a most sagacious administrator of the Patrimony of His loving-kindness to the poor, St. Peter. whom he delighted in ministering to with his own hands, His has remained proverbial. Homilies, Exegetical and Ascetical letters, works take up several folio volumes. He rested from his labours, March 12, a.d. 604, and was buried in St. Peter's.

gregory of elvira.name: Gregory Of Elvira
gregory of elvira.description: One of the champions of the Faith against Arianism, and one of the few Bishops who at Rimini (A.D. 359) consistently refused to palter with the heretics. There is no proof at all, as alleged by some Non-Catholics, that St. Gregory took part in the Schism of His Episcopal city of Elvira, Lucifer of Cagliari. from which the See has since been transferred to Granada, was the scene of several Spanish Councils. St. Gregory died before A.D. 400.

gregory of nazianzen.name: Gregory Of Nazianzen
gregory of nazianzen.description: Doctor of the Church. (4th cent.) St. Gregory the Elder, himself later Bishop of Nazianzus, a small town of Cappadocia in Asia Minor, and St. Nonna, were the parents of Gregory, who during his brilliant course of studies at Caesarea, Alexandria and Athens (the fourth century centres of learning), had for fellow-student, St. Basil the Great, his compatriot, and contracted with him It was not till after an intimate friendship. this that, in accordance with the imperfect Church discipline of his age, he was even baptised. He then retired with St. Basil for a time to live a monastic life in a secluded spot Recalled by his in Pontus on the Black Sea. father, who ordained him priest (a.d. 361), he was by St. Basil, his Metropolitan, eleven years later, consecrated Bishop of Sasima, a mere village, but in reality became Coadjutor to his own father at Nazianzus, the government of which See he however persistently refused to The troubled Church of Constantinople accept. St. Basil was was to be his chief field of work. dead, when St. Gregory was called there (A.d. 379 about). The Arian intruder was expelled, and Gregory, raised to the Patriarchate, was recognised as legitimate holder of the See in the Second CEcumenical Council, then (a.d. 381) sitting. He spent himself in toiling for peace and sound doctrine, but was soon forced to retire ; and ended his days, in company with other Solitaries at Arianzum, not far from his native place. He died in A.d. 389, at an With SS. Athanasius, Basil advanced age. and John Chrysostom, St. Gregory Nazianzen His is reputed a pillar of the Eastern Church. works in poetry and in prose are voluminous, and apart from their theological significance, show that his was a literary genius of the first His relics were translated to Rome in order. the Middle Ages.

gregory vii.name: Gregory Vii
gregory vii.description: Said to have been an AngloSaxon prince, who returning from a pilgrimage to Rome, became a monk at Einsiedeln in Switzerland, and later Abbot of that monastery. He died a.d. 996. state Religious (11th cent.) (May 25) One of the most famous of the Born before a.d. 1020 successors of St. Peter. of poor parents in Tuscany, and educated in Rome, Hildebrand (for so he was named at his Baptism) embraced the at Pope St. Leo IX, who knew Cluny in France. him there, recalled him to Rome to become Abbot of St. Paul's and his own councillor ; and as such he continued to act under St. Leo's successors. He was Archdeacon of Rome when elected (a.d. 1073) to succeed Pope Alexander II. The great evils of his time were the prevalent vice of simony, and the usurpation of authority in spirituals by temporal rulers. Gregory's firmness in withstanding the one and the other, his battling with Henry IV of Germany, the humiliation of the latter at Canossa, the renewed conflict leading to the disastrous intervention of Robert Guiscard and the Normans, form an important episode in the history of Mediaeval THE BOOK OF SAINTS GUARINUS end, the Church emerged Europe. Tn the But St. Gregory victorious from the struggle. himself passed away a fugitive at Salerno near Naples with on his lips the words : " Forasmuch as I have loved justice and hated iniquity, therefore do I die in exile." (May 25, A.D. 1085.)

gregory barbadigo.name: Gregory Barbadigo
gregory barbadigo.description: A Cardinal Bishop of Padua, distinguished equally as a statesman and as an Ecclesiastic, but still more illustrious on account of his piety and heroic patience. He died a.d. 1697, and miracles quickly bore witness to his sanctitv.

gregory of utrecht.name: Gregory Of Utrecht
gregory of utrecht.description: disciple and companion of (Aug. 25) (8th cent.) A Frank of Royal Blood, born at Treves, at the beginning of the eighth century, the faithful St. Boniface, both in his missionary travels in Germany and in one of his journeys to Rome. From the time of the martyrdom of St. Boniface (A.D. 754) St. Gregory governed the Church of Utrecht, and, though it seems he never received Episcopal Consecration, he is always styled Bishop of that city. Paralysed during the last years of Ms life, he continued to the end to teach and encourage his numerous disciples. He died A.D. 781.

gregory the illuminator.name: Gregory The Illuminator
gregory the illuminator.description: to Christianity conversions Bishop. (4th cent.) An Armenian, and reckoned the Apostle of his native country because of the numberless he The extant Acts of the Saint there effected. are of doubtful authority ; but it seems certain that he was consecrated First Patriarch or Archbishop of the Armenians, that he succeeded in converting Tiridates, the King of Christianity, and that he the suffered many persecutions from the heathen. To the place from which the title of his See is taken he gave the name of Etchmiadzin (now Vallarshabad), "The Descent of OnlyBegotten." a.d. 332 is a probable date of his death. country, the to

gregory thaumaturgus.name: Gregory Thaumaturgus
gregory thaumaturgus.description: Bishop. (3rd cent.) A Saint of exceeding celebrity both in the East and in the West, who is still annually commemorated in the Liturgy. Born at Neo-Caosarea, a then Pagan city of Pontus near the Black Sea, and a disciple of the famous Origen, he became Bishop of his birthplace about a.d. 240. At his accession there were no more than seventeen Christians in the town ; and it is related that on his deathbed (about A.D. 270) he thanked God that only that same number of idolaters remained in it. His title of Thaumaturgus, or Wonder-worker, he earned by the marvellous miracles his faith privileged him to work, among them the literal moving of mountains and drying up of lakes. He took part in the Council of Antioch (A.D. 264;, against Paul of Samosata. His literary remains are of value though fragmentary.

gregory of tours.name: Gregory Of Tours
gregory of tours.description: Born in Auvergne (a.d. 539) and of noble parentage, he was educated by his uncle the Bishop of Clermont. Threatened with a dangerous malady, he went as a pilgrim to the shrine of St. Martin of Tours, and was there by the people who were struck by his piety elected to fdl the then vacant See (A.D. 573). He built several churches, and assisted at the local French Councils of the period. In learning and culture he was far in advance of his contemporaries, and attracted the favourable notice of Pope St. Gregory the Great. His historical writings are even in our own day continually referred to as throwing great light on Merovingian times. He died Nov. 17, A.n. 590.

gregory decapolites.name: Gregory Decapolites
gregory decapolites.description: So-called from his birthplace in Asia Minor. A fervent ninth century Catholic, who suffered much in the Iconoclastic persecution. He himself ministered, so far as he was (6th cent.) (9th cent.) (6th

gregory of agrigentum.name: Gregory Of Agrigentum
gregory of agrigentum.description: cent.) A Sicilian His pupil allowed, to the imprisoned Faithful. Joseph, the Hymnographer, built a monastery over the spot where his body had been interred. (Nov. 23) of Pope St. Gregory the Great who raised him, on his return from a protracted sojourn in the monasteries of the East, to the See of Agrigentum (Girgenti), his native town, and vindicated his character when attacked by the evil-livers he corrected. The dates concerning him are much disputed ; but it would seem fairly certain that he did not pass away until after a.d. 600. contemporary

gregory hi.name: Gregory Hi
gregory hi.description: Like his predecessor, St. Gregory II, St. Gregory III was distinguished for learning and piety. He was a Syrian by birth and his election was the last for which the Emperor's leave was asked, the practice of doing so having years. The struggle lasted for nearly fifty with the Iconoclasts of the East continued through the eleven years of his Pontificate. Against Luitprand and the Lombards still overrunning Italy St. Gregory sought the aid of Charles Martel, the Frankish leader, who had just overthrown the Saracen invaders of Western After a stormy Pontificate, he died Europe. Nov. 27, A.D. 741.

gregory of auxerre.name: Gregory Of Auxerre
gregory of auxerre.description: The twelfth Bishop of Auxerre. He flourished in the first half of the sixth century, and died at the age of eighty-five, in the thirteenth year of his Episcopate.

gregory of spoleto.name: Gregory Of Spoleto
gregory of spoleto.description: A priest of Spoleto in Umbria, tortured and beheaded at the beginning of the fourth century, under Maximian Herculeus. The tradition is that, the Prefect having ordered his remains to be thrown to the wild beasts kept for the public games, a Christian woman bought them back at a great price and honourably interred them.

grignon de montfort.name: Grignon De Montfort
grignon de montfort.description: Bl. LOUIS-MARIE GRIGNON DE See MONTFORT.

grimbald.name: Grimbald
grimbald.description: A monk, native of Flanders, well-versed in all the learning of his age, and England by King Alfred. He invited presided for some time over the Schools at but afterwards was called by the Oxford ; King to Winchester, where he died (a.d. 903). to

grimoaldus.name: Grimoaldus
grimoaldus.description: An Archpriest of Pontecorvo, in Southern Italy, near Aquino, where towards a.d. 1137, he built a church to commemorate an Apparition of St. John the Baptist. He died in odour of sanctity after a life of austere piety and of works of mercy. He is said by some to have been born in England and to have been a brother of SS. Fulk and Eleutherius. *GRIMONIA (GERMANA) (St.) V.M. (4th cent.) An Irish (Sept. 7) Saint, martyred in Picardy (France), in defence of her virtue.

grwst.name: Grwst
grwst.description: The Welsh Saint, whose memory is perpetuated by the place-name Llanrwst (Denbighshire). GUAINERTH (WEONARD) (St.) (April 7) Patron of a chapel in Hereford (6th cent.) shire.

guarinus.name: Guarinus
guarinus.description: Born at Bologna (Italy) (Feb. 6) of noble family, he entered the Order of Canons Regular. After forty years of Religious life, during which his fame of sanctity became widespread, he was elected Bishop of Pavia ; but nothing could induce him to accept the post. However, his reluctance, created him Cardinal Bishop of Palestrina, where his great charity made him Great miracles followed universally beloved. his holy death (a.d. 1159) and led to his being canonised by Alexander III. Pope Lucius overruling II, *GUASACHT (St.) Bp. (5th cent.) (Jan. 24) St. Patrick being made captive in Ireland by Maelchu, Guasacht's father, the great Apostle converted the latter, who afterwards became one of his fellow-workers, and was by him consecrated Bishop of Granard (Longford).

gudelia.name: Gudelia
gudelia.description: A holy Christian woman who, after enduring exquisite tortures, was savagely done to death in Persia, under Sapor II (a.d. 330-A.D. 375).

gudula.name: Gudula
gudula.description: The daughter of St. Amalberga, and trained by St. Gertrude of Nivelle. She passed a holy life in watchings, fasts and prayer, and in toiling for the poor and distressed. She died a.d. 712 ; and three hundred years later her relics were translated to Brussels, of which city she is the Patron Saint. *GUDWALL (CURVAL) (St.) Bp. (June 6) (7th cent.) A Welsh Saint and Bishop who founded monasteries in Devon and Cornwall. By many he is supposed to be the St. Gurval who succeeded St. Malo at Aleth in Brittany. Ghent in Belgium claims to possess his relics.

guenhael.name: Guenhael
guenhael.description: The name Guenhael (" White Angel ") was given to the son of a Breton noble who consented that his child should be brought up in the monastery of Landevenec by St. In due course St. Guenhael sucWenwaloe. ceeded the latter as Abbot. He introduced the severe discipline followed in general by the Celtic Saints whom he passed over into Britain It is impossible to fix the exact to consult. date of his death, which happened in some year between A.D. 530 and A.D. 580.

guenninus.name: Guenninus
guenninus.description: A Bishop of Vannes in Brittany whose relics are enshrined in his Cathedral. *GUESNOVEUS (GOUERNOU, GUINOU) (Oct. 25) (St.) Bp. (7th cent.) A Bishop of Quimper in Brittany and founder of a famous monastery near Brest, where he died A.D. 675. (Feb. 6)

guinoc.name: Guinoc
guinoc.description: A saintly prelate in Scotland, Breviary. Aberdeen commemorated in He passed away about A.D. 838. the (Dec. 14) (March 3)

guislain.name: Guislain
guislain.description: Otherwise St. GISLAIN, which see. *GULSTAN (GUSTAN, CONSTANS) (St.) (Nov. 27) (11th cent.) A holy monk of the Benedictine Abbey of St. Gildas de Rhuys, in the Diocese of Vannes in Brittany. He died about A.D. 1009.

gumesindus and servusdeus.name: Gumesindus And Servusdeus
gumesindus and servusdeus.description: MM. (9th cent.) Two Spanish Martyrs, one a Parish Priest, the other a monk, who suffered death for the Christian Faith at Cordova, under the Mohammedan Caliph Abdurrahman II, about A.D. 850. GUMMA RUS (GOMER) (St.) (Oct. 11) (8th. cent.) A native of Brabant and relative of Pepin (the founder of the Carolingian dynasty in France) who called him to his Court and entrusted him with important offices. Late in life, on his return from the warlike expeditions in which he had accompanied his master, Gummarus with his wife's consent, betook himself

gundebert.name: Gundebert
gundebert.description: to a hermit's cell and passed the last years of his stay upon earth in prayer and penance. The Flemish town of Lierre has grown up around the hermitage where he died (a.d. 774). (April 29) (8th cent.) A French nobleman, brother of St. Niorad, Bishop of Reims. He was the husband of St. Bertha, and late in life retired to a monastery in Ireland, in the spoliation of which bv marauders he met his death.

gundenes.name: Gundenes
gundenes.description: A Christian woman traditionally described in the Martyrologies as a virgin, who bore witness to the Faith with her blood at Carthage in the persecution under Septimus Severus (A.D. 203).

gundleus.name: Gundleus
gundleus.description: A Welsh Prince, husband of St. Gladys and father of the famous St. Cadoc. In his old age he betook himself to a hermit's cell where he passed some years in austere penance. On his deathbed (about A.D. 500) he was assisted by his son St. Cadoc, and by the equally well-known Bishop St. Dubritius, the predecessor of St. David. A church at Newport is dedicated to St. Gundleus under the name of St. Woolloos.

gundulphus.name: Gundulphus
gundulphus.description: A holy man who seems to have lived in the sixth century and to have died at Bourges in France, where his tomb had been Nothing is now known the scene of miracles. of his career, nor even the name of the See over which he presided.

gunifort.name: Gunifort
gunifort.description: A native of Scotland or Ireland who left his country in company with his brother St. Gunibald, and of his two sisters. The two latter suffered martyrdom in Germany ; and his brother at Como on the confines of St. Gunifort, hit by arrows, succeeded Italy. in escaping the same fate, and in reaching Pavia, where he however died of the wounds still venerated at are received. It is conjectured that these martyrdoms Pavia. took place under Maximian Herculeus, the ferocious colleague of the persecuting Emperor Diocletian, that is, about A.D. 300. His relics

gunthiern.name: Gunthiern
gunthiern.description: (5th cent.'* A Welsh Prince who led the life of a hermit in Brittany, where he passed away about a.d. 500.

gurias and samonas.name: Gurias And Samonas
gurias and samonas.description: at Edessa in Syria, where, after torture, they were beheaded as Christians (a.d. 299). Martyrs under Diocletian cent.) (3rd (March 28)

gurval.name: Gurval
gurval.description: *GUTHAGON (St.) Otherwise St. GUDWALL, which see. (July 3) (8th cent.) An Irish Saint, who crossed over into Belgium, and there lived the life of a hermit. Many miracles have been wrought at his tomb.

guthlac.name: Guthlac
guthlac.description: A Mercian prince who, after some years of military life, passed to that of a hermit, and established himself in the Island of Croyland in the desolate marshes of LincolnAfter fifteen years, during which the shire. repute of his sanctity and miraculous gifts had drawn many Bishops and Princes, as well as thousands of others of inferior degree, to seek his counsel, he passed away A.D. 714 ; and in later ages the great Abbey of Croyland, erected on the site of his poor cell, befittingly enshrined his sacred remains. *GUY (WITEN) (St.) (March 31) (11th cent.) A holy Abbot of a monastery near Ferrara in Italy. He is chief Patron Saint of Spires in Germany, whither his relics were translated.

guy.name: Guy
guy.description: Otherwise St. VITUS, which see. (June 6) ; THE BOOK OF SAINTS HEDDA GUY (GUIDO) (St.) (Uth cent.) A poor man of (Sept. 12) Brabant, Sacristan to the Sanctuary of Our Lady at Laken, and afterwards for seven years a pilgrim in the Holy Land. On his return, he was hospitably received at Anderlecht (Belgium), where The precise he passed away a few years later. date (some year between a.d. 1012 and a.d. 1033) is uncertain. The miracles wrought at his tomb led to his being honoured as a Saint. *GWEN (BLANCHE) (St.) See SS. FRAGAN and GWEN. (5th cent.) *GWEN (BLANCHE) (St.) Widow. (Oct. 18) Said to have been the sister of St. Nonna. and therefore aunt to St. David of St. Gwen is alleged to have been the Wales. But the whole mother of SS. Cuby and Cadfan. tradition is altogether uncertain. Another St. Gwen, of the family of the great chieftain Brychan of Brecknock, suffered death at the hands of the heathen Saxons about a.d. 492. GWENDOLINE (GUNDELINDA) (St.) (March 28) (July 5) V. (8th cent.) A saintly Abbess in Alsace, She was sister of SS. Attala and Eugenia. brought up by her aunt St. Odilia, whom she She died about a.d. 750. succeeded as Abbess.

gwenhael.name: Gwenhael
gwenhael.description: GWERIR (St.) See SS. BROTHEN and GWENDOLINE. Otherwise St. GUENHAEL, which see. (April 4) (Date uncertain.) A hermit near Liskeard in Cornwall, over whose grave King Alfred was cured of a serious malady. St. Gwerir's cell was after his death occupied by St. Neot. (Nov. 3)

hadelin.name: Hadelin
hadelin.description: (7th cent.) A disciple of St. Remaclus of Tongres. He lived as a hermit in a cell near Dinant, on the river Mouse. He died there about A.D. 690.

hadrian and eubulus.name: Hadrian And Eubulus
hadrian and eubulus.description: A lion to which St. Hadrian was thrown in the Amphitheatre having refused to touch him, he was put to the sword, by order of the Prefect Firmilian, under Diocletian, St. Eubulus, at Caesarea in Palestine (A. D. 308). suffered with another Palestinian him.

hadrian.name: Hadrian
hadrian.description: Said to have been a son of the Emperor Probus, and, having embraced Christianity, to have been put to death (a.d. 320), at Nicomedia in Asia Minor, by the Emperor But no reliable information concernLicinius. ing him is extant. Christian,

hadrian iii.name: Hadrian Iii
hadrian iii.description: A Roman by birth, elected Pope (A.D. 884). He ruled the Church during one of the most troubled periods of her history. He laboured hard to alleviate the misery of the people of Italy, in prey to famine and to continuous war ; and he firmly withstood Photius, author of the still persisting Eastern Schism. Unhappily, in the second year of his Pontificate, while travelling to Germany to induce the Emperor Charles to support the cause of the Church and to help Italy in its distress, he died a.d. 885, near Modena. He was buried in the Abbey Church of Nonantula, where his tomb at once became a popular place of pilgrimage. (May 4) *HAILE (JOHN) (Bl.) M. See Bl. JOHN HAILE.

hallvard.name: Hallvard
hallvard.description: A Scandinavian Saint of the Royal Family of Norway, who met his death (A.d. 1043), while defending from ill-usage a poor stranger who had appealed to him for help. (July 31) *HANSE (EVERARD) (Bl.) M. See Bl. EVERARD HANSE.

hardoin.name: Hardoin
hardoin.description: The name is variously written, OUARDON, WARDON, HOARZON, HUARDO, etc. He was Bishop of St. Paul de Leon in Brittany, in succession to St. Tennenanus.

hardulph.name: Hardulph
hardulph.description: A church (Aug. 21) Bredon (Worcestershire) was dedicated to this Saint, of whom nothing besides is known. His name does not appear in the Mediaeval Kalendars. The English Menology surmises that he may be the hermit of Bredon mentioned in the Life of St. Modwenna (9th cent.). at

harmon.name: Harmon
harmon.description: Otherwise St. GERMANUS of AUXERRE, tihich sef.

harold.name: Harold
harold.description: A Christian child, said to have been put to death by Jews infuriated against This Christianity, at Gloucester (a.d. 1168). strange outbreak in the twelfth century is also held responsible for the martyrdoms of St. William of Norwich and St. Robert of Bury.

hegesippus.name: Hegesippus
hegesippus.description: HEDWIG (HEDWIGIS) (St.) Widow. (8th (July 7) cent.) An Anglo-Saxon monk and Abbot in the North of England, who became Bishop of the West Saxons (A.D. 676) by permission of Pope St. Hadrian I. He transferred his See from Dorchester in Oxfordshire to Winchester, and governed his Diocese to the advantage of both Church and State (he being a chief Councillor of King Ina of Wessex) until 705. Many miracles his attested his sanctity. death, holy A.D. (13th cent.) (Oct. 17) Of princely race and daughter of a Duke of Dalmatia, St. Hedwig was married, when only a child, to Henry, Duke of Silesia, to whom she bore six children. Later, by mutual consent, they separated to lead lives of greater religious perfection, though St. Hedwig never ceased to aid and comfort her husband in the many political troubles which beset him. She survived him for fifteen years, which she passed in the practice of the severest penance in the monastery of Treibnitz, near Cracow, her only solace being her devoted ministering to the She passed away Oct. 15, poor and afflicted. A.D. 1243, at the age of sixty-nine, and was canonised A.D. 1267 by Pope Clement IV. (April 7) (2nd cent.) A Jew by birth, who flourished in the second century of our era and lived for many years in Rome, dying about A.D. 180, after his return to Jerusalem. He is reputed the father of Church History, from his having compiled an account of happenings in it, tracing the succession of Popes from St. Peter to his own day. The work is unfortunately lost, but it is warmly commended by St. Jerome and by Eusebius, who knew it. There is no proof at all that St. Hegesippus was (as is sometimes advanced) a Judaizing Christian. (Oct. 7) (6th cent.) The tradition at Reims, where his festival is kept, is that St. Helanus came to France in the sixth century, with his six brothers and three sisters, who thenceforth lived separately, the one from the other, an Eremitical life, on the banks of the River Marne. St. Helanus, who was a priest, presided over them and ministered to the people of the neighbourhood. He appears to have survived till after a.d. 600. (May 22) Mentioned in the Acts of St. Amator, Bishop of Auxerre, as a saintly maiden, endued with the grace of working miracles. She assisted at the deathbed of the holy Bishop (A.D. 418). More is not known of her. (5th cent.)

helena.name: Helena
helena.description: Otherwise St. ALENA or St. ALANA, which see.HELENA (St.) Widow. M. (July 31) (11th cent.) A noble Swedish lady, given up to the practice of good works, who in the final struggles of heathenism against advancing Christianity, in Scandinavia, was barbarously She was canonised by Pope put to death. Alexander III (A.D. 1164).

heliconides.name: Heliconides
heliconides.description: Holy Places of Jerusalem. Part of her relics are in France, part have been retained in Rome. (May 28) (3rd cent.) A Christian woman, native of Thessalonica, who was arrested at Corinth and beheaded after excruciating torture (a.d. 244) under Gordian, or more probably (a.d. 250) in the Decian persecution.

helier.name: Helier
helier.description: A native of Tongres (Limburg), who lived as a hermit in the Island of Jersey, and was put to death by a band of heathen pirates, whom he was endeavouring to convert to Christianity.

helimenas.name: Helimenas
helimenas.description: See SS. PARMENIAS, HELIMENAS, &c. HELIODORUS, VENUSTUS and OTHERS (May 6) (SS.) MM. (3rd cent.)

heliodorus.name: Heliodorus
heliodorus.description: Martyrs of the great persecution at the close of the third century. They are reckoned to have been seventy-seven in number. St. Heliodorus, with seven others, appears to but St. Ambrose have suffered in Africa ; claims the greater part of the rest for his own city of Milan. (4th cent.) (July 3) Born in Dalmatia, probably at the same place and about the same time (A.D. 332-A.D. 342) as St. Jerome, he was through life the intimate friend and confidant of the famous Doctor of the Church. He helped him, financially and otherwise, in the preparing of the Vulgate. He made two pilgrimages to the East in company with St. Jerome, and on his second return to Italy was made Bishop of Altinum, a small town (since destroyed), not far from Venice. He assisted at the Council of Aquileia (A.D. letter addressed to him by St. Jerome, written in the year 396 ; but the exact date of his death is unknown. 381). We have a (Sept. 28)

heliodorus and others.name: Heliodorus And Others
heliodorus and others.description: Christian Martyrs who suffered under Aurelian (A.D. 270-A.d. 274, in Pamphylia (Asia Minor). Some of their executioners, converted at the sight of their patience in the torture chamber, are said to have declared themselves Cliristians, and there and then to have shared their glorious lot.

helladius.name: Helladius
helladius.description: A distinguished minister of the Visigothic Kings of Spain, at the Court of Toledo, who embraced the Religious life in a neighbouring monastery. He afterwards (A.D. 614) was made Archbishop of Toledo. He died, full of years and virtues, a.d. 632. St. Ildephonsus, his successor, has written a noble Panegyric of St. Helladius.

helladius of auxerre.name: Helladius Of Auxerre
helladius of auxerre.description: The predecessor in the See of Auxerre in France of St. Amator, whom he He died a.d. 387, converted to a devout life. in the twenty-fourth year of his Episcopate.

hemeterius and celidonius.name: Hemeterius And Celidonius
hemeterius and celidonius.description: MM. (Date uncertain.) Two famous Spanish Martyrs, believed to have been soldiers in the Roman Imperial army. They were put to the torture and beheaded as Christians at Calahorra in Old Castile, but in which persecution is Prudentius wrote a Hymn in their unknown. honour, in which he deplores the destruction by the Pagans of the Acts of their Martyrdom. St. Gregory of Tours has preserved for us the few particulars we have. HEMMA (EMMA) (St.) Widow. (11th cent.) A relation (June 29) of the Emperor St. Henry of Germany, who, after the death of her husband, became a nun in Carinthia. Having attained to great sanctity, she died A.D. 1045. THE BOOK OF SAINTS HERMAS (May 14)

henry.name: Henry
henry.description: Descended on both his father's and his mother's side from Charlemagne, Henry, son of the Duke of Bavaria, was born A.D. 972, and educated by St. Wolfgang of Ratisbon. Elected Emperor (A.D. 1002) and crowned in Rome by Pope Benedict VIII (a.d. 1015), Henry married St. Chunegunda, making however with her a pact of life-long continence. St. Henry was a sagacious ruler and contrived more or less to maintain peace in Germany and in Italy. He however strenuously and successfully asserted his rights against the powerful rebel Ardoin. He fostered the commerce of his country, giving privileges and charters to the cities, and overawing the feudal justice tempered with mercy barons. made him universally popular. He respected the rights and possessions of the Church and aided the Bishops in their work of reform. After a long and prosperous reign, he passed away, July 15, a.d. 1024, and was buried in the Cathedral at Bamberg, a church and Bishopric he had himself founded. arrogant His (Oct. 25) (14th cent.) A Dominican Saint of Flemish descent who died at Ulm in Germany (a.d. 1365). He was remarkable for his gifts of supernatural prayer, and his works on the Contemplative Life, much used in our own day, have been translated into many languages and often reprinted.

henry of treviso.name: Henry Of Treviso
