A Martyr of Marcianopolis in Thrace who suffered under the Emperor Marcus Aurelius, the Philosopher, about the middle She appears to have of the second century. previously been zealous in doing her best to spread Christianity, and so to have attracted She was severely scourged special attention. and beheaded. Her remains were taken for burial to the Isle of Lemnos in the JEgean Sea by a devout Christian, who, falling ill during the voyage, was shortly afterwards interred at her side.

melito.name: Melito
melito.description: A Bishop of Sardis in Lydia (Asia Minor), author of an Apology or work in defence of Christianity, addressed to the Emperor Marcus Aurelius.

mella.name: Mella
mella.description: Born in Connaught, St. Mella became the mother of two Saints, Cannech and After the death of her husband Tigernach. she embraced the Religious life and died Abbess of Lough-Melvin.

mellanius.name: Mellanius
mellanius.description: Otherwise St. MELLONUS, which see. MELLION (MELLON, MULLION, MELANIUS)

mellitus.name: Mellitus
mellitus.description: Bp. Otherwise St. MELLONIUS, which see. (Jan. 6) (April 24) (7th cent.) A Roman monk, one of the band of missionaries sent by St. Gregory to aid St. Augustine in the work he had begun some years before in Kent, and to further spread the Gospel among the Anglo-Saxons. St. Augustine consecrated him Bishop of the East Saxons, with his See in London. Trouble with the Pagan Princes of Essex drove him into exile into France ; but he soon forced his way back to liis work, and on the death of St. Laurence, succeeded him in the Archbishopric of Canterbury. He governed the nascent English Church with wonderful success, despite grave bodily infirmities. He passed away a.d. 624. MELLO (MELLON) (St.) Bp. Oct. 22nd Otherwise St. MELLONIUS, which see.

mellonius.name: Mellonius
mellonius.description: This Saint, whose name the Roman Martyrology renders as " Melanius," is supposed to have been a native of Great The churches of St. Mellon and St. Britain. Mullion in Wales and Cornwall may possibly commemorate him, though other Patron Saints with similar names have been by some assigned to them. St. Mellonius is stated to have gone to Rome and to have been sent thence as a missionary by Pope St. Stephen, about the middle of the third century. He stayed in Northern Gaul, and is venerated as the Founder and first Bishop of the See of Rouen. After a long Episcopate he retired to a hermit's cell at a place called Hericourt, where he died a.d. 314.

melorius.name: Melorius
melorius.description: cent.) A Saint venerated both in Catholic England, chiefly at Amcsbury, and in Brittany. He is said to have been the son of a chieftain in Cornwall and a convert to Christianity, done to death on that account early But no source of authentic in the fifth century. information is now available. (Aug. 5 (2nd cent.) The Saint popularly known in France as St. Menge. The tradition is that he was one of the zealous men sent by St. Peter The raising of the as Apostles into Gaul. dead to life and many other miracles are said to have borne witness to the truth of his preaching. He made numberless conversions

memmius.name: Memmius
memmius.description: among the population. He is also credited with having systematically divided his Diocese into parishes and thoroughly organised it. A visit to Rome led to his extending the sphere His of his labours into the adjoining districts. Episcopate is said to have been a very long one, the date of his death being put as late as A.D. As in similar cases regarding the planting 126. of Christianity in Gaul, the time of his Apostolate is challenged by modern investigators.

memorius and others.name: Memorius And Others
memorius and others.description: ; (Sept. 7) (5th cent.) The Roman Martyrology registers this Saint as " Nemorius " popularly he is known as St. Mesmin. He was a deacon of the Church of Troyes in France, sent by the Bishop, St. Lupus, with several companions, to the camp of Attila the Hun, who was threatening the city, to beg of him to spare it. The Barbarian leader, however, seized them and put them all to death. There are various accounts extant of the circumstances of this martyrdom, and not all of them are trustworthy. The fact of the cultus of the victims from the earliest ages is at least undoubted. The Relics of St. Memorius escaped the fury of the Revolutionists of 1792, and are still in popular veneration.

menedemus.name: Menedemus
menedemus.description: MENEFRIDA (St.) V. (5th cent.) Brecknock. (Cornwall). (July 24) Of the family of Brychan of She is the Patron Saint of Menver (Sept. 2) (April 28) (Aug. 1) (Sept. 5)

menehould.name: Menehould
menehould.description: The Patron Saint of the French town in the Argonne called after her. With her five sisters, likewise honoured as Saints, she illustrated by her holy life the Diocese of Chiaons-sur-Marne. MENELEUS (MENEVE) (St.) Abbot. (8th cent.) (July 22) In French the name is rendered Menele or Mauvier. He was a native of the West of France, but entered a monastery in Later, he founded a great Abbey Auvergne. at Menat near Clermont. In his declining years he appointed as his successor St. Savinien, a companion of his youth, and died a.d. 720.

meneus and capito.name: Meneus And Capito
meneus and capito.description: Beyond the fact that these Martyrs are commemorated in the Greek Menologies, and thence notices of them copied into the Western Martyrologies, nothing is now known of them. often written " Hymenseus." Meneus is

menevius.name: Menevius
menevius.description: A French Abbot in Auvergne, in which Province and in that of Anjou, in which he was born, he is in great veneration.

menignus.name: Menignus
menignus.description: A Count of Huy on the Meuse, where he is venerated as Patron Saint. He met his death while struggling with evildoers in the cause of Christian morality. (March 15) (3rd cent.) An Asiatic, by trade a fuller. He, in times of persecution, ministered to the suffering Christians to the utmost of his power. It is related that in a.d. 250, when the Decian persecution broke out, Menignus received a Divine inspiration to go before the judge and to confess the Christian Faith. and was sentenced with the rest. After the usual scourging, the tradition is that his fingers and toes were cut off before he was beheaded. Many miracles wrought at his tomb in the This he did N (5th neighbourhood of Constantinople attracted to it in Christian times numerous pilgrims. *MENNA (MANNA) (St.) V. (Oct. 3) cent.) A Christian maiden in the country now called Lorraine, related by blood to St. Eucharius and other Saints. The traditions concerning the details of her life are unfortunately very unreliable.

mennas.name: Mennas
mennas.description: cent.) An Egyptian officer in the Imperial army, serving in Asia Minor. On quitting military service he retired for a time into the Desert, intending to embrace the life Nevertheless, on the breaking of the Solitaries. out of the great persecution under Diocletian, Mennas felt himself moved to share the lot of his fellow-believers and, returning to the town of Kutahia in Phrygia, publicly declared himself a Christian. He was scourged, put to other His body torture, and beheaded (a.d. 296). was cast into a fire, but thence rescued by a fellow-countryman of the Martyr and taken back to the Egyptian desert, where it was interred and later a church erected over the grave.

mercurialis.name: Mercurialis
mercurialis.description: The first Bishop of Forll in Central Italy. He attended the Council of Rimini summoned in the heat of the struggle of the Church with the Arians. He died about a.d. 406. The records of Forli have been again and again destroyed ; and there is consequently great uncertainty as to the trustworthiness of the traditional accounts of its early Bishops. It seems, too, that more than one of these bore the name Mercurialis.

mercurius.name: Mercurius
mercurius.description: An Armenian soldier (Nov. 25) in the Imperial army, who by his bravery had secured advancement to a post of importance. His refusing to take part in an idolatrous ceremony betrayed him to the authorities charged to carry out the edict of persecution promulgated by Decius. Mercurius was consequently put to the torture and beheaded a.d. 250. Some of his relics are venerated in churches in the South of Italy.

mercurius and others.name: Mercurius And Others
mercurius and others.description: cent.) escort sent to (Dec. 10) Sicilian Martyrs. They were (4th prisoners, Christian soldiers Mercurius being the officer commanding the detachment. The prisoners so impressed the soldiers that they too on arrival at Leontium, whither they were bound, declared themselves to be of the same religion as their charges. All alike were put to the torture and beheaded, The date appears to require about a.d. 320. reconsideration, as it is not clear how Licinius, who is named in the Roman Martyrology as the persecuting Emperor, could have been Sicily so long after pursuing Christians in Constantine had guaranteed toleration and protection to the Christians in the West.

merewenna.name: Merewenna
merewenna.description: The Patron (Aug. 12) Saint of Marham Church, near Bude. She is said to have been one of the daughters of Brychan of Brecknock, and again, is reputed by some identical with St. Morwenna, also a daughter of the famous Welsh chieftain.

meriadec.name: Meriadec
meriadec.description: A Bishop of Vannes in Brittany, famous for the austerity of his life and for his a.d. 1302 is the accepted charity to the poor. date of his death.

merinus.name: Merinus
merinus.description: A disciple of Dunawd of Bangor and Patron Saint of churches in Wales and also of others in Brittany. MERINUS (MERRYN, MEADHRAN) (St.) Bp. (Sept. 15) (7th cent.) A disciple of St. Congall at Benchor, venerated as a Saint both in Scotland and in Ireland. He passed away about a.d. 620. *MERLILAUN (MEROLILAUN) (St.) M. (May 18) (8th cent.) A British Saint who met his death by violence near Rheims in France while on a pilgrimage to Rome, and has since been popularly venerated as a Martyr. " THE BOOK OF SAINTS MIDDLEMORE (Aug. 29) MERRI (MERRY) (St.) Abbot. (Sept. 15) Otherwise St. MEDERICUS, which see. *MERRYN (MEADHRAN) (St.) Otherwise St. MERINUS, which see.

merulus.name: Merulus
merulus.description: St. Gregory the Great says of St. Merulus that he was always in prayer, except for the few moments he was constrained to set aside for sleep and for the taking of The same holy Pope mentions nourishment. the fact that St. Merulus with his fellow monks, SS. Antony and John, received from Almighty God a revelation of the day and hour in which each would be called out of this world to a better life.MERWENNA (St.) V. (10th cent.) (May 13) The first Abbess of Rumsey Under her rule, it is stated that (Hampshire). the monastery was a " veritable school of Probably identical with religious perfection." St. Merewenna, which see.

mesmin.name: Mesmin
mesmin.description: Otherwise St. MAXIMINUS, which see. (4th MESOPOTAMIA (MARTYRS of) (May 23) Christians put to death on account of their religion in Mesopotamia, under the Emperor Maximian Galerius, one of the colleagues of Diocletian, about A.D. 307. cent.)

methodius.name: Methodius
methodius.description: According to St. Jerome, St. Methodius was a Bishop of Olympus in Lycia (Asia Minor), and thence translated to the more He is important See of Tyre in Phoenicia. generally supposed to have suffered martyrdom at Chaleis in Greece about A.D. 311. He was a profound Theologian and a polished writer His " Symposium " after the style of Plato. is avowedly an imitation of the " Banquet of the latter. In the controversies of his time he showed himself a vigorous opponent of the theories of Origen. METRANUS (METRAS) (St.) M. (Jan. 31) (3rd cent.) One of the victims of the persecu250). He was an tion under Decius (a.d. Egyptian of Alexandria, and St. Dionysius, his Bishop and contemporary, describes in vivid terms the ghastly tortures which preceded his execution.

metrobius.name: Metrobius
metrobius.description: METRODORA (St.) V.M. See SS. LUCIAN, METROBIUS, <fcc. See SS. MENODORA, METRODORA, Ac. (Sept. 10) (Dec. 24)

metrophanes.name: Metrophanes
metrophanes.description: Believed to have become Bishop of Byzantium about A.D. 313. There is a tradition that the admiration cherished by Constantine for his virtues and merits had not a little to do with the choice made by that Emperor of Byzantium, henceforth Constantinople, as the seat of his government. St. Metrophanes had suffered imprisonment during the his Episcopate at Constantinople was a peaceful one. He was unable on account of his infirmities to take part in the great Council of Nicaea (a.d. 325), and died in that same year. persecution under Diocletian, but *MEUGANT (MAWGHAN, MORGAN) (Sept. 26) (St.) (6th cent.) A Saint to whom several churches in Wales and Cornwall are dedicated. He appears to have been a disciple of St. Ultyd, to have lived as a hermit in several places in the West of Britain, and to have retired before his holy death to the Isle of Bardsey. He is sometimes found represented as a Bishop with mitre and crozier. (4th MEURIS and TH/EA (SS.) MM. (Dec. 19) cent.) Two Christian maidens who suffered martyrdom at Gaza in Palestine about It is not clear that these Saints a.d. 307. are other than the St. Valentina and her anonymous fellow-sufferer, commemorated on July 25. (June 21)

mevenna.name: Mevenna
mevenna.description: *MEWAN (St.) Abbot. Otherwise St. MAINE, which see. (June 21) The Cornish form of the name of St. MAINE, MEVENNA, MEEN, which see.

mewrog.name: Mewrog
mewrog.description: Saint, (Date uncertain.) A Denbighshire concerning whom no particulars are extant. MICHjEAS (MICAH) (St.) Prophet. (Jan. 15) B.C.) A contemporary of the (8th cent. One of the Twelve Minor Prophet Isaias. His inspired Book contains the Prophets. prophecy that Christ should be born in the town His prophecy is a short one. of Bethlehem. He inveighs both against Samaria and Jerusalem, but in magnificent imagery foretells the glory of the Church of the New Testament. His tomb, according to the historian Sozomen, was in the fourth century discovered in the neighbourhood of Jerusalem. MICHAEL CARVALHO and OTHERS (March 1) (Bl.) MM. (17th cent.)

michael.name: Michael
michael.description: Portuguese Jesuits, missionaries in Japan, burned to death there at the stake (A.D. 1624). of St. (9th cent.) A disciple (May 23) Tarasius, Patriarch of Constantinople, by whom he was consecrated Bishop of Synnada in Phrygia. St. Tarasius also chose Michael as the bearer of his Synodal Letter to Pope St. Leo III in Rome. St. Michael was distinguished by his fearless opposition to the Iconoclast Emperor Leo the Armenian. He was banished into Galatia, where he went from place to place spreading everywhere the light of the Faith, in spite of continuous persecution. He died about a.d. 820.

michael the archangel.name: Michael The Archangel
michael the archangel.description: One of the three Angels (Michael, Gabriel, Raphael) liturgically venerated by Holy Church. Holy Scripture describes St. Michael as " one of the chief princes " (Dan. x. 13) ; and again as the leader of the Heavenly Host in their battle and triumph over the forces of hell 7). He is mentioned also in the (Apoc. xii. Epistle of St. Jude as " rebuking the devil." He has always been specially invoked by the Catholic Church both in the East and in the West. A second Feast is kept in his honour, that of his Apparition (May 8) on Monte Gargano Another in the South of Italy (fifth century). Apparition in France (eighth century) led to the foundation of Mont St. Michel in Brittany. (Sept. 30) (7th cent.) An Anglesey Saint who flourished early in the seventh century. We have no reliable particulars concerning him. MIDDLEMORE (HUMPHREY) (Bl.) M. (June 8) *MIDAN (NIDAN) (St.) See CARTHUSIAN MARTYRS. (Nov. 18)

migdonius and mardonius.name: Migdonius And Mardonius
migdonius and mardonius.description: They were high officials in the Imperial Court, either in that of Maximian Herculeus or in that of Diocletian. In the persecution (A.D. 300 about), as Christians who refused to return to heathenism, they were Migdonius sentenced to the death penalty. was burned at the stake and Mardonius drowned in a well. A Christian, by name Anthimus, was discovered conveying a letter to them while awaiting trial in their prison For this he was stoned to at Nicomedia. death.

milburga.name: Milburga
milburga.description: A sister of St. Mildred of Thanet, she became Abbess of Wenlock in Shropshire. The old English historians attribute the working of many miracles to St. Milburga. She is said to have survived till about A.D. 722. Her Abbey, destroyed by the Danes, afterwards passed into the possession of Cluniac monks. (Jan. 17) (7th cent.) The youngest and least known of the three holy sisters, Milburga, Mildred and Mildgith was trained by her saintly Mildgith. mother, Ermenburga, at Minster in Thanet, and afterwards pursued the Religious life in She passed away the North of England. towards the close of the seventh century. (July 13) (7th cent.) One of the three daughters of St. Ermenburga (Ebba, Domneva). Mildred was sent by her mother to be educated in the convent of Chelles in France, and on her return received the Religious habit from St. Theodore, Archbishop of Canterbury, in St. Ebba's monastery of Minster in Thanet, of which at her She mother's attended a Provincial Council in that capacity She died towards the end of the (A.D. 694). century. Her relics were translated to Canterbury (A.D. 1030). became Abbess. death she

mirocles.name: Mirocles
mirocles.description: A famous Florentine Martyr, one of the victims of the Decian persecution (a.d. 250). He was a soldier, and had done his best to spread the Christian Faith among his comrades. The extant Acts of his Passion describe the many tortures to which he was subjected before execution. The Italian form of his name, San Miniato, is the more usual. (Dec. 3) (4th cent.) The successor of St. Maternus in the See of Milan, which in his time became an Archbishopric. He is said to have been the originator of the Ambrosian Liturgy and Chant, afterwards improved and defined by the holy Doctor whose name it bears. St. Mirocles died Both St. Ambrose and St. Ennodius a.d. 318. of Pavia speak in terms of admiration of his life and works. MISACH (MISAEL) (St.) (Dec. 16) One of the three Hebrew youths cast into the fiery furnace by King Nabuchodonosor, and miraculously delivered unscathed therefrom (Dan. iii.).

mitrius.name: Mitrius
mitrius.description: A Greek by birth, slave of a hard master in the South of Gaul. The latter, a Pagan and a hater of Christianity, ill-used Mitrius savagely on account of his religion. The cruelty was lifelong for both, since Mitrius quickly followed his persecutor to the tomb St. Mitrius is in especial honour at (a.d. 314). The French call him SaintAix in Provence. Mitre, also Merre or Metre.

mnason.name: Mnason
mnason.description: Otherwise St. JASON, which see. *MOCH^EMHOG (MOCHCEMOC, VULCANIUS, PULCHERIUS) (St.) Abbot. (March 13) (7th cent.) He was born in Munster and brought up by his aunt, St. Ita. He then became a disciple of St. Comgall. Later he built cells for his own monks at Anatrim, and finally established himself as head of a community at Liath. Great miracles are recorded of him, especially his having raised the dead The precise year of his death is unto life. certain. *MOCHELLOC (CELLOG, MOTTELOG, MOTALOGUS) (St.) (7th cent.) (March 26) The Patron Saint of Kilmallock Authentic particulars of his life (Limerick). are lacking.

mochteus.name: Mochteus
mochteus.description: The first Bishop of Louth, to which See he is said to have been appointed by St. Patrick himself, which would give the fifth century as his date, though by some he is placed a century later. He would appear to have been born either in England or in Scotland. St. Adamnan styles him a " Briton."

mochua.name: Mochua
mochua.description: 0«terwi*e, ettfter St. CLUANUS or St.CRONAN, which see.

mochuda.name: Mochuda
mochuda.description: Otherwise St. CARTHAGE THE YOUNGER, which see.

modan.name: Modan
modan.description: An Abbot of Mailros who preached the Faith in Stirling and at Falkirk, retiring in his old age to a solitude near Dumbarton.

modanic.name: Modanic
modanic.description: A Scottish Bishop whose Feast as a Saint was kept at Aberdeen, but of whom we have no reliable particulars. MODERAN (MORAN) (St.) (Oct. 22) (8th cent.) A saintly Bishop of Rennes in Brittany who renounced Ms See and, passing into Italy, finished his life as a hermit in the Apennines (a.d. 730).

modesta.name: Modesta
modesta.description: A great deal of controversy exists about the identity of this holy Abbess, (March 13) ; THE BOOK OF SAINTS MONICA but the most probable opinion is that she was closely allied with St. Gertrude of Nivelle, and that she was the first Abbess of (Ereo (Horren) at Treves, the monastery founded by St. MoThe name of St. Modesta appears in doald. numerous Litanies, local Martyrologies, &c, and she is specially venerated in the Diocese She seems to have died about of Treves. a.d. 680 and to have been succeeded at Horren by St. Erminia, daughter of King Dagobert. (Jan. 12)

modestus.name: Modestus
modestus.description: MODOALD (St.) Bp. See SS. TIBERIUS, MODESTUS, &c. of (7th cent.) Archbishop (May 12) Treves from a.d. 622 to a.d. 640. He had previously been at the Court of the Merovingian King Dagobert and, as Archbishop, one of his achievements was the conversion of the monarch from a life of dissipation to one conformable to Christian His Diocese prospered greatly under principles. his administration. When he died (a.d. 640) his remains were laid by the side of those of his sister, St. Severa (an Abbess at Autun) in the Abbey Church of the latter.

modestus and julian.name: Modestus And Julian
modestus and julian.description: St. Modestus is described as a Carthaginian Martyr. He has been chosen as the Patron Saint of Cartagena in Spain. St. Julian, according to the best authorities, suffered at Alexandria in Egypt. Why they in the Martyrologies is not are apparent. (Date unknown.)

modestus and ammonius.name: Modestus And Ammonius
modestus and ammonius.description: Martyrs at Alexandria in Egypt. They are said to have been mere Nothing is really now known about children. them. associated

modoc.name: Modoc
modoc.description: •MODOMNOCK (DOMNOC) (St.) Otherwise St. ^EDAN of FERNS, which see. (Feb. 13) (6th cent.) An Irish Saint who, with others, became a disciple of St. David in Wales. Returning to his own country, he lived a holy life as a hermit in the neighbourhood of Kilkenny. He fell asleep in Christ a.d. 550. (Jan. 31)

modwenna.name: Modwenna
modwenna.description: An Irish Saint who, coming to England, founded the Abbey of Polesworth in Warwickshire. Most probably she flourished but there is much in confusion in Ecclesiastical history between her and other holy women of the same or similar name. the ninth century, *MOZLIAI (M03LRAY) (St.) Abbot. (5th cent.) An Irish (June 23) Saint, baptised by St. Patrick, and by him set over the newly founded monastery of Nendrum, where he had SS. Finnian and Colman among his disciples. He died about a.d. 493. •MOGUE (St.) Abbot. (April 11) Otherwise St. MACDOGH-^EDAN, ivhich see. *MOLAGGA (LAICIN) (St.) Abbot. (Jan. 20) (7th cent.) An Irish Saint, brought up in Wales under the discipline of St. David. He founded a monastery at Fulachmhin (Fermoy). He was distinguished for his exceptional learning as well as for his piety and for his Christian charity. He seems to have survived the great pestilence of a.d. 664. He is much venerated There are several in the South of Ireland. Saints of the same name (Irish Hagiologists enumerate no less than twelve), and it is often difficult to disentangle their Acts. (April 18)

moloc.name: Moloc
moloc.description: An Irish Saint, disciple of St. Brendan, who passed over to Scotland, the field of his labours for Christ. He lived chiefly His memory is also associated in the Hebrides. with that of St. Boniface of Ross. He was consecrated Bishop, but to what See is not clear. Throughout his life, he was famous for his a.d. 592 is given as the probmissionary zeal. able date of his death.

molonachus.name: Molonachus
molonachus.description: A disciple of St. Brendan who Little became Bishop of Lismore in Argyle. or nothing is now known about him.

monan.name: Monan
monan.description: A Saint trained up by St. Adrian of St. Andrews, and a missionary in the country With six thousand about the Firth of Forth. other Christians he was slain by the heathen His shrine was famous for Danes (a.d. 874). the miracles wrought there.

monas.name: Monas
monas.description: A native of Milan who in his youth attracted the attention of the Archbishop St. Callimerus. The latter trained him for the priesthood, with the hope that Monas might one day succeed to his own See. This wish was realised, it is said, by a miraculous intervention at the moment of the election. Monas gathered together his flock, scattered by the persecutions so frequent and so ruthless of the third century, organised parishes, and conThe verted numberless Pagans to Christianity. conjectural conversion of the Emperor Philip is affirmed by the biographers of St. Monas, and attributed to his prayers and wholesome influence. He died after fifty-nine years of Episcopate, March 25, A.D. 249. (July 2) (6th cent.) A pious woman of Chartres (France), who on the death of her two children, with the consent of her husband, betook herself to a hermitage, where she spent the rest of her life in the practices of prayer, self-denial and others. Round her work for the good of deathbed (a.d. 570) were gathered several pious women who had adopted her mode of Mention is made of her as a Saint by her life. contemporary, St. Gregory of Tours.

monessa.name: Monessa
monessa.description: The daughter of an Irish chieftain, converted by St. Patrick. The tradition is that on coming out of the Baptismal Font she straightway winged her way to Heaven (A.D. 456).

monica.name: Monica
monica.description: St. Augustine of Hippo, who owed his conversion cent.) The saintly mother of (4th from a life of error and dissipation to Christianity and high sanctity to her prayers and tears. She was of Christian parentage in Africa, though married to a Pagan, whom, however, she had She accomthe comfort to see die a Christian. panied her son and his fellow-converts to Italy, where she superintended their quasi-monastic In her old age she was seized establishment. with a longing to return to her native Africa. On the way, at the port of Ostia, she fell mortally ill and expired there May 4, a.d. 387, in the Most people will remember presence of her son. the pathetic words in which St. Augustine in his " Confessions " enlarges on his mother's virtues and describes the manner of her passing away. (July 6) (6th cent.) An Irish Saint of Sliabh Cuillin, where she closed a saintly life with a happy death, a.d. 518.

monitor.name: Monitor
monitor.description: The twelfth Bishop of Orleans. He flourished towards the end of the fifth century. He is always described as a Saint in the Orleans documents, but nothing further His relics were transferred is recorded of him. to the Abbey of St. Aignan, under King Robert of France, a.d. 1029.

monon.name: Monon
monon.description: A Scottish (Oct. 18) Saint who crossed over to the Continent and lived as a hermit in the Forest of the Ardennes, where he was done to death by men of evil life. He is famous for miracles. MONTANUS, LUCIUS, JULIAN, VICTORIOUS,

flavian and others.name: Flavian And Others
flavian and others.description: Some of the many Christians, disciples of St. Cyprian of Carthage, who were put to death during the fierce persecution of Christianity under the Emperor Valerian (a.d. 259). The story of their imprisonment is told by themselves, and that of their martyrdom by eye-witnesses.

montanus.name: Montanus
montanus.description: Some have thought that this suffered under Martyr, a Christian soldier, Hadrian in the second century, but the opinion now prevails that he was one of the victims of the fury of Diocletian. He was, after a period of imprisonment, taken over to the Island of Ponza, and there thrown into the sea, with a heavy stone tied round his neck. The Christians recovered his body and enshrined it at Gaeta. MORE (THOMAS) (Bl.) M.

morwenna.name: Morwenna
morwenna.description: A Bishop of Dunblane in Scotland who appears to have left his name to several churches, and who was venerated with a solemn Office in the old Scottish Rite. (July 8) (5th cent.) A Cornish Saint to whom we owe some place-names. She is often confused with St. Modwenna, who flourished two centuries There is also an Irish Saint Monynna, later. and in her case also the similarity of names has led to mistakes.

moses.name: Moses
moses.description: A Roman priest, of such worldwide renown as a champion of the Faith that even from Carthage St. Cyprian addressed to him a letter full of praise and encouragement, which he received while in prison on the charge of leading Romans astray from the worship of the gods. On this occasion he was after a time released, and soon after we find Pope St. Cornelius commending him for his zeal in converting idolaters and in confuting the crafty subtleties the Novatian heretics. He was again of arrested and imprisoned, and in fine gained the crown of martyrdom. He was beheaded a.d. 251. (Jan. 18) (3rd cent.) Two Christian soldiers arrested as Christians in the Province of Pontus in the Their sentence Decian persecution (a.d. 250). was at first only to forced labour for life in the mines ; but it appears to have been revised by the Imperial authorities, and they were adjudged to undergo capital punishment, like the greater part of their co-religionists. They were burned alive in the following year.

moseus and ammonius.name: Moseus And Ammonius
moseus and ammonius.description: MOUNT ARARAT (MARTYRS of) (SS.) MM. (Date uncertain.) The tradition exists that In one of the old persecutions under the Roman Emperors, ten thousand of the Faithful won the Crown of Martyrdom in a general massacre of Christians in the country round Mount Ararat But no reliable record of their in Armenia. sufferings now exists.

moysetes.name: Moysetes
moysetes.description: An African Martyr. He probably was one of the victims of the persecution under Decius (a.d. 250). (July 3)

mucius.name: Mucius
mucius.description: A Martyr at Constantinople, where the Emperor Constantine built a church over his tomb. He was a native of that city, born of Christian parents who had come thither to settle from Rome. He became a priest, and in his zeal is said to have overturned a Pagan altar, scattering the offerings on the This, it appears, whether the accusaground. tion was true or false, occurred at Heraclea, and entailed the death penalty. He was put to the torture and beheaded in Constantinople Several Odes and Canticles itself (a.d. 311). in honour of St. Mucius were composed by the Greeks, and some of them are still sung in their churches. : THE BOOK OF SAINTS NARCISSUS (Jan. 6)

myrope.name: Myrope
myrope.description: *MUIRCHU (MACCUTINUS) (St.) (June 8) (7th cent.) An Irish Saint, son of Cogitosus, who wrote the Life of St. Bridget and one of those of St. Patrick. He appears to have been time, but an important personage materials for even sketching out his own Life are altogether lacking. his in

mummolin.name: Mummolin
mummolin.description: A French Saint, successor of He St. Eligius or Eloy as Bishop of Noyon. died a.d. 680 about.

mun.name: Mun
mun.description: One of the four nephews of St. Patrick, who consecrated him Bishop over his converts in the present County of Longford. He ended his days as a hermit in an island in Lough Bee.

munchin.name: Munchin
munchin.description: A Prince of the Blood of the chieftains of North Munster. As Abbot of Mungret he ruled over a community of fifteen Of these, five hundred were hundred monks. five hundred to the devoted to preaching ; chanting of the Psalmody, which it was sought to make unceasing through the day and the night and five hundred to the doing of other good works to the Glory of God and advantage of man. St. Munchin is the Patron Saint of Limerick City and Diocese, of which he is venerated as the first Bishop. He died late in the fifth century.

munde.name: Munde
munde.description: A Scottish Saint, head of a great monastery in zealous missionary and a man of prayerful and austere life. He died a.d. 962. The dedications of various churches perpetuate his holy memory. (Jan. 13) Argyle. He was a

muredach.name: Muredach
muredach.description: A disciple of St. Patrick, who consecrated him first Bishop of Killala. St. Muredach ended his holy life as a hermit in the island of Innismurray.

mustiola.name: Mustiola
mustiola.description: MYLLIN (St.) Bp. (June 17) The Welsh form of the name MOLLING or (July 3) MOLINGUS, which see.

myron.name: Myron
myron.description: A priest in charge of a church in Greece. At the coming of Imperial officers, under Decius (a.d. 250), to wreck the sacred building and arrest such Christians as they might find about it, Myron boldly faced them and made his protest against the iniquitous law of the Pagan Emperor. The Saint was subjected to torture on the spot, but was sent for execution to Cyzicus on the Sea of Marmora. (July 13) (3rd cent.) A Christian woman, native of the Island of Chio in the Grecian Archipelago, whence she used to make pilgrimages to the shrines of the Martyrs and other holy places. Accused of having hidden the body of the Martyr St. Isidore, she admitted the having She was scourged and died in prison done so. from the effects of the punishment (a.d. 251). (April 24) (6th cent.) A child in Rome, much favoured by Almighty God with visions and supernatural She is spoken of by St. Gregory contemplation. the Great, her contemporary, and locally was honoured as a Saint from soon after her holy death.

nabor and felix.name: Nabor And Felix
nabor and felix.description: Martyrs under Diocletian (July 12) at Milan, about A.D. 304. They owe their celebrity in the Universal Church to their solemn Translation and enshrinement by the great St. Ambrose, nearly a century later.

nahum.name: Nahum
nahum.description: One of the Minor Prophets, supposed to have been a native of Northern His short prophecy of three chapters Palestine. is directed against Ninive, the great city of the Assyrians, by whom his compatriots of the Ten Tribes were shortly after led into captivity. He lived to see come to pass the destruction of Ninive, which he had foretold. (2nd cent.)

nampharion and others.name: Nampharion And Others
nampharion and others.description: African Martyrs, so celebrated in ancient times that St. Nampharion (the name is of Punic or Carthaginian derivation) was styled the Arch-Martyr, and reputed one of the first who suffered for the Faith in Africa (perhaps Mention is made of him in the a.d. 180). Letters of St. Augustine.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.description: One of the victims of the persecution under Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. He appears to have been an Egyptian, and to have suffered at Alexandria. He was put to the torture, and so horribly maimed thereby that he expired while being carried back to his dungeon. See SS. ARGEUS, NARCISSUS, &c.

narcissus and felix.name: Narcissus And Felix
narcissus and felix.description: A holy Bishop and his deacon, who were put to death together as Christians at Gerona in Catalonia (Spain), in the persecution under Diocletian, about a.d. 303. St. Narcissus is also famous at Augsburg (Germany) and in Switzerland, as having, while preaching in those parts, brought about the conversion of the celebrated penitent St. Afra. (3rd cent.)

narcissus and crescentio.name: Narcissus And Crescentio
narcissus and crescentio.description: These Saints were among the victims of the Decian persecution continued under the Emperor Valerian (a.d. 254-261). Narcissus was a Christian in whose house many of the Faithful had found a refuge, and one of those charged by St. Laurence with the distribution of the moneys of the Church to the (July 13)

narcissus.name: Narcissus
narcissus.description: NARCISSUS (St.) Bp. (3rd Crescentio was a blind man, to whom poor. by a miracle St. Laurence gave back his sight. The little we know of either is drawn from the Acts of St. Laurence compiled from oral tradition. (Oct. 29) cent.) A Bishop of Jerusalem, an account of some of whose miracles is given by the historian Eusebius. St. Narcissus is said to have been considerably more than one hundred years old when he died. Though already in his eightieth year when made Bishop, he was energetic as a Pastor of souls, and even (a.d. 195) presided over a Council of the Bishops of Palestine. (Oct. 31)

narnus.name: Narnus
narnus.description: The tradition concerning St. Narnus is that he was consecrated first Bishop of Bergamo in the North of Italy by St. Barnabas the Apostle, that he governed his Church ably and holily, and in his extreme old age committed the charge of it to St. Victor of

natalia.name: Natalia
natalia.description: A devout Christian woman of Nicomedia, the residence of the Emperor Diocletian, who bravely ministered to the Martyrs imprisoned during the persecutions, the worst of which she survived, dying peacefully at She had been Constantinople about a.d. 311. a servant in the household of the Martyr St. Hadrian (Sept. 8), and the loyal service she rendered him in prison and in the torture chamber is touchingly narrated in his Acts.

natalis.name: Natalis
natalis.description: The Founder of monasticism in the Northern parts of Ireland, and associated St. Natalis ruled the Abbeys with St. Columba. of Cill, Naile and Daunhinis. His holy well is still venerated.

nathalan.name: Nathalan
nathalan.description: A celebrated Bishop of Aberdeen, famous for his learning, zeal in spreading the Faith and charity to the poor. He died Jan. 8, A.D. 679.

nathanael.name: Nathanael
nathanael.description: Otherwise probably St. BARTHOLOMEW, which see.

nathy.name: Nathy
nathy.description: Son of a chieftain in Connaught and disciple of St. Finnian of Clonard. He founded a monastery at Achonry and was consecrated Bishop. He was famous for his austerity of life but much more for his loving kindness to the poor. He died at a great age about a.d. 600.

nazarius.name: Nazarius
nazarius.description: See SS. BASILIDES, CYRINUS, &c. St. (1st cent.)

nazarius and celsus.name: Nazarius And Celsus
nazarius and celsus.description: Nazarius's (July 28) father was a heathen ; but his Christian mother, Perpetua was probably a disciple of St. Peter. Leaving Rome, the Saint went to Milan, where, under Nero, he was beheaded with his companion, the youth Celsus, about a.d. 60. Their bodies, separately buried, were discovered by St. Ambrose (a.d. 395), and in the tomb of St. Nazarius, a vial of blood, fresh as if recently shed.

neachtain.name: Neachtain
neachtain.description: A near kinsman of St. Patrick, at whose holy death, according to tradition, the Saint was present. The memory of St. Neachtain has always been held in much veneration.

nectan.name: Nectan
nectan.description: The Patron Saint of Hartland in Devonshire. He was one of the descendants of the famous prince, Brychan of Brecknock. The circumstances of his death, which have justified his being accounted a Martyr, are not now known. (Feb. 3) *NELSON (JOHN) (Bl.) M. See Bl. JOHN NELSON. NEMESIANUS, MM. (3rd cent.) FELIX, ANOTHER POLYANUS, LUCIUS, LITTEUS, JADER, DATIVUS &

nemesis.name: Nemesis
nemesis.description: An Egyptian, one of the Martyrs at Alexandria under Decius (a.d. 250). He suffered about the same time as St. Macarius (Dec. 8), and, to make his Passion more humiliating, he was burned at the stake between two Eusebius the historian had these and thieves. other particulars from an account written by St. Dionysius, Patriarch of Alexandria, contemporary of the Martyrs. (3rd

nemesius.name: Nemesius
nemesius.description: A Saint venerated near Lisieux in the North jof France, but of whose life we have no reliable account.

nemesius and lucilla.name: Nemesius And Lucilla
nemesius and lucilla.description: Nemesius, a Roman deacon, with his daughter Lucilla, was among the Christians put to death in Rome by the Emperor Various Popes interValerian (a.d. 254-260). ested themselves in the fitting enshrinement Hence, separate remains. of commemoration is made of them in the Martyrologies. their sacred cent.) NEMORIUS (MEMORIUS, MESMIN) and

nennius.name: Nennius
nennius.description: An Irish Saint, disciple of St. Finnian of Clonard, reckoned as one of the " Twelve Apostles of Ireland." The particulars of his life are lost. *NENNOC (NENNOCHA, NINNOC) (St.) V. (June 4) (5th cent.) A British Saint, one of the children of Brychan of Brecknock, said to have followed St. Germanus of Auxerre back to France and to have become Abbess of one or in Armorica (Brittany). more monasteries a.d. 467 is given as the date of her holy death. *NENNUS (NENUS, NEHEMIAS) (St.) (June 14) Abbot. (7th cent.) An Irish Saint, the successor of Saint Eudeus in the government of the monasteries of the Isles of Arran and Bute.

neophytus.name: Neophytus
neophytus.description: A Christian youth, not yet years of age, who was put to the fifteen torture, and in the end executed at Nicaea (Asia Minor), in the persecution under Diocletian (A.D. 310). (May 2)

neopolus.name: Neopolus
neopolus.description: •NEOT (St.) See SS. SATURNINUS, NEOPOLUS, &c. (9th cent.) (July 31) Tradition tells us that St. Neot was a monk at Glastonbury Abbey who lived in the ninth century ; that he was a councillor of King Alfred, and that he retired to a hermitage in Cornwall, where he gathered round him a small band of disciples. His remains, it is further said, were afterwards translated to the place called St. Neots in Huntingdonshire. (Sept. 8)

nereus and achilleus.name: Nereus And Achilleus
nereus and achilleus.description: Two famous Roman Martyrs, baptised by St. Peter the Apostle, and household servants of the noble lady St. Flavia Domitilla. With her they were banished as Christians to were the Isle they Unbeheaded under Trajan, about a.d. 100. fortunately, the extant Acts of these Saints are far from reliable. Ultimately of Ponza.

nersas and others.name: Nersas And Others
nersas and others.description: Both Latins and Greeks agree that this band of Martyrs were Persians, and that St. Nersas was a Bishop. Nothing else is known for certain about them. (Oct. 16)

nestor.name: Nestor
nestor.description: One of the Martyrs at Gaza in Palestine under the apostate Emperor Julian. He was quite a youth and showed himself a While veritable hero in the torture-chamber. being dragged half-dead with the others to the place of execution, outside the city walls, the crowd, moved by a sort of pity, insisted rather on his being left to die by the wayside. There, he was found by Christians and given shelter. But while being tended he expired (a.d. 362). (Oct. 8) (4th cent.) A youthful Martyr at Thessalonica, at the beginning of the fourth century, under Diocletian. A singular tale concerning his voluntarily undertaking a gladiatorial fight in the Arena is given in the Greek Acts, but there is no need to accept it. His cult was from the outset far spread in the East, and it was only much later that it was extended to the Western Church.

nicander.name: Nicander
nicander.description: An Egyptian Martyr at the beginning of the fourth century under Diocletian. He distinguished himself by his charity in ministering to his previously had (Aug. 29) Syrian Nothing brethren in prison and by his diligence in collecting and honourably interring the remains of those who had died for Christ. He was, according to custom, put to frightful torture before being beheaded. (2nd cent.)

nicander and marcian.name: Nicander And Marcian
nicander and marcian.description: Martyrs in the South of Italy. They appear to have been officers in the Imperial army, or, as others say, high civil functionaries. The date of their death is also much disputed. Some put it as late as the reign of Diocletian With the Bollandists (a.d. 300 or thereabouts). we give a.d. 173 as the more likely year of (Date uncertain.)

nicander and hermas.name: Nicander And Hermas
nicander and hermas.description: St. Nicander was a Bishop and St. Hermas a priest. They were put to death at Myra in Lycia (Asia Minor). Nothing certain is now known about them.

nicanor.name: Nicanor
nicanor.description: A Jew by birth, one of the seven deacons chosen by the Apostles (Acts vi. 5). The tradition is that after the stoning of St. Stephen, their chief, they dispersed and went as St. Nicanor came to Cyprus, where, years afterwards, under Vespasian (a.d. 76 about), he suffered death for Christ. among the missionaries Gentiles. (Nov. 7) (June 5)

pientia.name: Pientia
pientia.description: St. Nicasius, a Bishop, is said to have been one of the first missionaries sent from Rome to the Pagans of the North of France, where he, with the others enumerated above, As in many was put to death as a Christian. other cases, there is a great doubt as to whether the old tradition that these and other holy missionaries came into Gaul in the Apostolic Age or centuries later can be maintained. The Bollandists prefer a.d. 286 as the date of the martyrdom of St. Nicasius. NICASIUS, EUTROPIA and OTHERS (Dec. 14) (SS.) MM. (5th cent.)

nicephorus.name: Nicephorus
nicephorus.description: St. Nicasius was a Bishop of Rheims and had with him his sister Eutropia. All agree that they, with a multitude of other Christians, suffered death at the hands of Barbarian invaders of Gaul ; but some would date their martyrdom as early as a.d. 407, while others, with greater probability, maintain that it took place nearly half a century later at the time of the inroad of the Huns. (Feb. 9) (3rd cent.) A Syrian Christian put to death for his Faith at Antioch under the Emperor This is the holy Martyr Valerian, a.d. 260. of whom it is related in an official account by contemporaries that he took the place of Sapricius, who, through unwillingness to forgive Nicephorus some injury, lost the grace of fortitude and apostatised before the heathen Judge who was trying him as a Christian. St. Nicephorus then of his own accord came forward and received Martyr's crown forfeited by the other. the

niceras.name: Niceras
niceras.description: A devout woman of Constantinople, so intent on good works that the historian Sozomen writes of her that he knew of no woman of his time who surpassed her in Loyal to St. John Chrysostom, she virtue. left Constantinople when he was banished from his See, and seems to have died in exile early in the fifth century.

niceta and aquilina.name: Niceta And Aquilina
niceta and aquilina.description: All that we know of these sufferers for Christ is drawn from the traditional account of St. Christopher. They were two women in Lycia (Asia Minor) converted from an evil life as heathens to Christianity by the holy Martyr, and were soon themselves privileged to die for their Faith.

nicetas.name: Nicetas
nicetas.description: A Goth, one of the victims of the fury of King Athanaric, who ruled towards the end of the fourth century over those of the nation then settled about the Danube. He had been converted to Christianity by the celebrated Ulphilas, translator of the Bible into St. Nicetas was burned the Gothic language. to death about a.d. 378. NICETIUS (NIZIER) (St.) Bp. (April 2) For twenty years Archbishop of Lyons. He died a.d. 577, and many miracles worked at his tomb have borne witness to his eminent sanctity.

nicetius.name: Nicetius
nicetius.description: A French Benedictine monk who became Archbishop of Treves and distinguished himself by his courage in rebuking the semibarbarous princes of his time for their crimes and cruelty. He died a.d. 570. (6th cent.) in Gaul.

nicholas of flue.name: Nicholas Of Flue
nicholas of flue.description: The fifteenth Bishop of Vienne Little or nothing is now known of him. (March 21) (15th cent.) A holy man in Switzerland who at the death of his wife retired to a hermit's cell and passed the last twenty years of his life in solitude. He died March 21, a.d. 1487, at the age of seventy, and many miracles were wrought at his tomb.

nicholas albergati.name: Nicholas Albergati
nicholas albergati.description: Born at Bologna in Italy, and afterwards Cardinal Archbishop of that city, who by his skill in negotiations between the Holy See and Christian princes rendered great services to the Church, and by his successful Episcopate did much good to souls. In his old age he resigned all his dignities to perfect his sanctity by becoming a Carthusian monk. He passed away May 10, A.D; 1443.

nicholas.name: Nicholas
nicholas.description: One of the most remarkable men of his age. He ably governed the Church during nine dark years of the ninth century. Many of his letters are extant and testify to his learning and holiness. Missionaries sent by him effected the conversion of the Bulgarians. He died A.D. 867. (Dec. 6) (4th cent.) An Archbishop of Myra in Asia Minor who from the innocence of his own life and the devotedness with which he, as a Bishop, watched over the young, has come to be regarded as the Patron Saint of children. He died in the middle of the fourth century, and some hundred years later his holy relics were transThe familiar " Santa lated to Bari in Italy. Klaus " is a corrupt form of his name. (1st (Aug. 3) cent.) The Saint whom Our Lord styled " a Master in Israel," and who shared with St. Joseph of Arimathsea the privilege of laying Him in the tomb. On August 3, the Feast of the Finding of his Body with that of St. Stephen is kept. He is also in some places commemorated on March 27.

nicomedes.name: Nicomedes
nicomedes.description: (1st cent.) A Roman priest associated with SS. Nereus and Achilleus (May 12), and St. Petronilla (May 31), to the last of whom he administered the Sacraments of the Dying. St. Nicomedes was scourged to death under Domitian about A.D. 90. NICOMEDIA (MARTYRS of) (March 18) Nicomedia on the Hellespont, the residence of the Emperor Diocletian, had a It was there he large Christian population. initiated his fierce persecution. The number of Martyrs at that place is variously estimated from ten thousand to twenty-three thousand. They were for the most part put to death in the first years of the fourth century, though from other entries in the Martyrology it may be reasonably inferred that the commemoration of March 13 refers specially to those who under went capital punishment previously to a.d. 300. Again, among the Martyrs are rightly reckoned Christians, victims in massacres carried out by the Pagan multitude irrespectively of the Such massacres were encouraged Imperial Law. or at least tolerated by the authorities. NICOMEDIA (MARTYRS of) (June 23) (4th cent.) Numerous Christians of Nicomedia who, while the persecution under Diocletian was raging, had taken refuge in .the forests and mountain ravines in the neighbourhood. They were hunted out and in great numbers sealed their Faith with their blood (A.D. 303). NICOMEDIA (MARTYRS of) (Dec. 23) (4th cent.) The victims of an atrocious massacre of Christians perpetrated at Nicomedia, the Imperial residence on the Hellespont (a.d. 301), by order of the Emperor Diocletian. The Greeks estimate that some twenty thousand of the Faithful perished in the indiscriminate slaughter of men, women and children. NICOMEDIA (MARTYRS of) (Dec. 25) (4th cent.) Many hundreds of Christians who, assembled in a church, perished through the building being surrounded by soldiers and set on fire by order of the Emperor Diocletian.

nicon and others.name: Nicon And Others
nicon and others.description: A band of one hundred Italian Martyrs whom modern investigation has proved to have suffered in Sicily and not in Palestine, as registered by mistake in the Roman Martyrology. The record of St. Nicon is singular. THE BOOK OF SAINTS NOTHELM (Sept. 28)

nizier.name: Nizier
nizier.description: He was a Roman soldier of some distinction. Then, while travelling in the East, he became a Christian, and in company with others embraced the monastic life. Because of the persecution threatened in Palestine, they took refuge in Sicily, and were there, every one, put to death under Decius (a.d. 250).

nicon.name: Nicon
nicon.description: cent.) An Armenian monk who travelled (chiefly in Greece) as a missionary, preaching and converting many both by his eloquence and by the holiness of his life. He died in his own country, A.D. 998.

nicostratus, antiochus and others.name: Nicostratus, Antiochus And Others
nicostratus, antiochus and others.description: A cohort of Roman soldiers put to death at Caesarea Philippi (Palestine) in the persecution under Diocletian (a.d. 303). St. Nicostratus was their Tribune or commanding officer. They appear to have suffered at the same period as St. Procopius, Martyr.

nicostratus.name: Nicostratus
nicostratus.description: See SS. CLAUDIUS, NILCOSTRATUS, &c. (Nov. 8) See SS. CLAUDIUS, NICOSTRATUS, &c. ( This group includes the Saints of July 7, adding others to their number.)

nilammon.name: Nilammon
nilammon.description: An Egyptian monk of holy life whom the inhabitants of a neighbouring city Bishop. The insisted on having as Patriarch was asked by the reluctant Nilammon to consent to a delay while he prayed. Then, kneeling down and representing his reluctance to Almighty God, he suddenly passed from this life, a.d. 403.

nilus.name: Nilus
nilus.description: A Greek of Southern Italy, and the founder of the well-known Greek monastery of Grotta Ferrata near Rome. In his youth he had committed a sin he deemed so heinous as to call for a lifelong penance. First as a hermit and afterwards as the head of a Religious community, he faithfully carried this out. He died at the age of ninety-five, universally venerated, about a.d. 1000. (Nov. 12) (5th cent.) A learned Eastern monk, surnamed by his contemporaries " Sapiens " or the Wise. He made his home with the Solitaries of Mount Sinai and emerged into public life mainly as a supporter of the persecuted St. John Chrysostom. Most of his works, which are chiefly ascetic, are still extant. He died at Constantinople some time after a.d. 430.

nissen.name: Nissen
nissen.description: A convert in Ireland made by St. Patrick, who set him over a monastery at Montgarth (Mountgarret) in the present county of Wexford.

nithard.name: Nithard
nithard.description: One of the early (Feb. 3) Christian missionaries to Sweden. He was put to death by the Pagan inhabitants of that country A.D. 840.

nivard.name: Nivard
nivard.description: An Archbishop of Reims who died about a.d. 670, and is there venerated as a Saint. (April 2) (Dec. 31) Otherwise St. NICETIUS, which see.

nonna.name: Nonna
nonna.description: The mother of St. Gregory of Nazianzum, a matron of exemplary life, who obtained the conversion of her husband by her She was the model of a Christian prayers. mother, and a helper to all in poverty and distress. The touching Panegyric or Funeral Discourse pronounced over her remains by her son St. Gregory does equal credit to the heads St. Nonna lived to a great and hearts of both. age, dying at Nazianzum (Asia Minor) about A.D. 375. *NONNITA (NONNA) (St.) (March 3) (6th cent.) The mother of St. David and consequently a Saint of the first half of the She retired into a Convent sixth century. and came into such repute of sanctity that churches were dedicated to her after her death. Some have it that she, like so many others of her fellow-countrymen of that age, ended her days in Brittany. There is a Cornish St. Nonna or Nonnita, venerated as a VirginMartyr, confused sometimes with the mother of St. David, but materials for unravelling the historical puzzle are altogether lacking.

nonnosus.name: Nonnosus
nonnosus.description: An Abbot of a monastery near Rome to whose virtues and miracles St. Gregory the Great bears witness. By his Faith he literally moved mountains. He appears to have lived somewhat earlier in the sixth century than the great Pope who has written concerning him.

norbert.name: Norbert
norbert.description: A Syrian Bishop of Edessa, best known for having by his eloquent preaching converted the famous St. Pelagia, the sinner of That he was a man of God is evident Antioch. from all that we read in the records left of his St. Pelagia died a.d. 457, and holy penitent. St. Nonnus probably about the same year. (June 6) (12th cent.) Born in Lorraine (a.d. 1080; of a noble family, St. Norbert for some years led a worldly life at the Court of the Emperor Henry IV. Miraculously converted to God, he founded the Order of Canons Regular, known from the name of their first monastery as Premonstratensians, and later became Archbishop of Magdeburg in Saxony. He revived popular devotion to the Blessed Sacrament of the Altar and strenuously resisted the heresies which in his age impugned the Catholic Doctrine of the Real Presence. He died A.D. 1134, famous throughout Europe for his zeal and holiness of life.

nostrianus.name: Nostrianus
nostrianus.description: A Bishop of Naples remarkable for his zeal and skill in defending Catholic doctrine against the subtle issues raised by the Arian heretics of his age. He probably died about A.D. 450.

nothburga.name: Nothburga
nothburga.description: A Tyrolese Saint, a poor servant girl, whose only delight upon earth was the helping, as she could, those even poorer than herself. Her shrine at Eben in the mountains is a much frequented place of pilgrimage.

nothelm.name: Nothelm
nothelm.description: A saintly Archbishop of Canterbury, friend and helper in his historical labours of Venerable Bede, and much esteemed by St. Nothelm St. Boniface, Apostle of Germany. died A.D. 740. (Sept. 19)

novatus.name: Novatus
novatus.description: The son of Pudens the Senator, he was the brother of SS. Praxedes and Pudentiana, and like them venerated from the earliest ages as a Saint. He is believed to have died about a.d. 151.

noyala.name: Noyala
noyala.description: A Saint greatly venerated in Brittany, said to have been of British birth. She suffered martyrdom at the hands of infidel robbers. NUMERIANUS (MEMORIANUS) (St.) Bp. (July 5) (7th cent.) A Bishop of Treves in Germany, Modwaldus. The where St. records of his Pastoral work have been lost. He died, according to some, a.d. 658, according to others, eight years later. succeeded

numidicus and others.name: Numidicus And Others
numidicus and others.description: The number of Martyrs included by the Roman Martyrology as fellow-sufferers with St. Numidicus is unknown. They were Africans, and perished at the stake, probably a.d. 252, as victims of the Decian persecution, though the Roman Martyrology attributes their Passion to the edicts of Valerian. Numidicus, it is stated, was dragged still breathing, out of the ashes of the funeral pyre, and lived for some years afterwards as one of the clergy of the Church of Carthage.

nunilo and alodia.name: Nunilo And Alodia
nunilo and alodia.description: Two sisters, Christian virgins, put to death because of their religion by the Moots while masters of Spain, at Huesca in that country (a.d. 851). We know of them through St. Eulogius of Cordova, their contemporary. See SS. TRYPHON, RESPICIUS, &c.

obdulia.name: Obdulia
obdulia.description: The Feast of this Saint is kept on Sept. 5 at Toledo in Spain, and is so registered in the Roman Martyrology, but it has been found impossible to identify her. The most probably conjecture is that St. Obdulia is really St. Odilia, one of the Christians put to death with St. Ursula, and that her relics were in early times translated into Spain.

octavius, solutor and adventor.name: Octavius, Solutor And Adventor
octavius, solutor and adventor.description: Patron Saints of the city of Turin. They were soldiers in the Theban Legion, massacred, as being formed of Christians, by order of Maximian Herculeus (a.d 297). Among those who succeeded in temporarily escaping were Octavius and his two comrades. They reached Turin, but were there seized and put to death. They are specially eulogised in Homilies of St. Ennodius of Pavia and of St. Maximus of Turin.

oda.name: Oda
oda.description: A French Princess, married to the Duke of Aquitaine. In her widowhood she devoted herself to the care of the poor and 723. Her She passed away a.d. suffering. shrine is at Amay, near Liege.

odger.name: Odger
odger.description: A disciple of St. Wiro and of St. Plechelm. He accompanied them from England to Holland, where the three Saints lived in retirement and gave themselves up to The relics of St. Odger penance and prayer. are enshrined at Ruremonde. *ODHRAM (ORAM) (St.) Abbot. (Oct. 27) (6th cent.) An Abbot of Iona and also of an Irish monastery in Meath, commended for his holiness by St. Columba. He died about A.D. 563, and has given his name to Oronsay.

odilo.name: Odilo
odilo.description: A French Saint, Abbot of the famous Benedictine monastery of Cluny, and distinguished for the exceeding gentleness of his rule and for the great holiness to which, taught and encouraged by him, his disciples attained. He introduced into the Kalendar of the Church the beautiful annual commemoration of the Faithful Departed, known as All Souls' Day. He passed away in the night of the New Year, a.d. 1049.

odo.name: Odo
odo.description: A Bishop of Urgel in Spain, distinguished for his love of the poor and for his care of the widows and orphans of his nock. He died a.d. 1122. (Nov. 18) (10th cent.) A Frenchman of noble birth who renounced a canonry at Tours in order to embrace the Religious Life among the Cluniac Benedictines, then in the first fervour of their Elected Abbot, he by his famous Reform. piety and wisdom shone as a bright and sinning light amid the darkness of the age in which he Having rendered priceless services both lived. to his Order and to the Church at large, he was called to his reward A.D. 940.

odran.name: Odran
odran.description: The chariot-driver of St. Patrick, who about a.d. 452 gave his life for that of the Apostle, taking his place when the latter was murderously attacked by Pagans.

odrian.name: Odrian
odrian.description: One of the early Bishops THE BOOK OF SAINTS . OPTATIAN

odulph.name: Odulph
odulph.description: of Waterford in Ireland, but no particulars concerning him are now extant. (June 12) (9th cent.) A native of Brabant who, after a long and fruitful missionary life in the first half of the ninth century, passed away at His relics were translated Utrecht in Holland. to Evesham Abbey (a.d. 1034), to which the fame of the many miracles wrought by the intercession of the Saint drew numerous pilgrims.

oduvald.name: Oduvald
oduvald.description: A Scottish nobleman, a monk , and afterwards Abbot of Melrose. He was a contemporary of St. Cuthbert. He died a.d. 698.

ogmund.name: Ogmund
ogmund.description: A Bishop in Iceland and disciple of St. Isleph, one of the Apostles of that island. St. Ogmund died a.d. 1121.

olalla.name: Olalla
olalla.description: Otherwise St. EULALIA of MERIDA, which see. OLAVE (OLAUS, TOOLEY) King, M. (July 29) (11th cent.) A famous King of Norway, distinguished as a successful leader in war, who, yet a Pagan, came to England (a.d. 1013), helped King Ethelred in his struggle with the Danes, and returned to Norway, a convert to Christianity, together with priests and monks In this they destined to evangelise his people. were successful ; but the Pagans rose against their noble monarch, drove him into exile, and in the end killed him in battle near Drontheim (a.d. 1030) in the sixteenth year of his reign. He was forthwith and rightly venerated as a Martyr to the Christian Faith.

olave of sweden.name: Olave Of Sweden
olave of sweden.description: A Saint other than the famous St. Olave, King of Norway. He lived a century earlier and was done to death by his rebellious heathen subjects for refusing to sacrifice to idols at the spot where since Stockholm has been built.

olcan.name: Olcan
olcan.description: OLCANUS (St.) Bp. Otherwise St. B OLCAN, which see. (April 18) (5th cent.) A Briton by birth who worked in Ireland under St. Patrick, and was by him made Bishop of Derkan in Antrim. OLIVA (OLIVE) (St.) V. (June 3) (Date uncertain.) A holy nun at Anagni, some miles South of Rome, famous for her life of prayer and penance. (Feb. 20)

oliver.name: Oliver
oliver.description: •OLIVER PLUNKET, Bp., M. (Feb. 3) (13th cent.) A holy man of whom little is known save that, while on a pilgrimage to Rome, he entered at Ancona a Religious Order, and died there A.d. 1273. (July 1) (17th cent.) Born in 1629 and ordained priest in 1654, this Irish Saint devoted himself Consecrated (a.d. 1669) to the saving of souls. Archbishop of Armagh, he laboured successfully in restoring the discipline of the Irish Church, laid waste by the continuous persecuting of Catholicism in that age. He was arrested on a charge of complicity in one of the sham plots of the time, and brought for trial to The notorious Jeffries, not yet a London. Judge, was the prosecuting counsel. Chief Justice Pemberton, "whose conducting of the trial (writes Lord Campbell) was a disgrace to himself and his country," in condemning " Your treason is the Martyr to death, said : of the highest nature. A greater crime cannot be committed against God than for a man to endeavour to propagate your religion." Blessed Oliver was hanged, drawn and quartered at Tyburn (a.d. 1681). The words : " I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ " are his His body is now last recorded utterance. He enshrined at Downside Abbey, near Bath. was beatified by Pope Benedict XV (a.d. 1920). (March 6) (12th cent.) An Archbishop of Tarragona in Spain, previously an Augustinian Canon Regular

ollegarius.name: Ollegarius
ollegarius.description: and Bishop of Barcelona. He literally restored the Church of Tarragona, neglected and decayed during the Moorish domination. He took part in the Lateran Council of a.d. 1123, and in that of Clermont (a.d. 1130). He passed away full of merits, a.d. 1137.

olympias.name: Olympias
olympias.description: A lady of noble birth at Constantinople who lost her husband after only twenty months of married life, and thenceforward devoted herself to works of religion She was appointed a deaconess and charity. of the Church at Constantinople, and, devotedly attached as she was to the cause of the exiled St. John Chrysostom, was herself persecuted on Several Greek Fathers of her his account. She passed away, time speak in her praise. as would seem, soon after a.d. 400.

olympius.name: Olympius
olympius.description: OMER (St.) Bp. *ONCHO (ONCHUO) (St.) (Feb. 8) (6th or 7th cent.) An Irish pilgrim and Saint, who was also a poet, a guardian of sacred traditions and a collector of holy relics in While pursuing his search for memoIreland. rials of the Saints, he died at Clonmore monastery, then governed by St. Maidoc, and his body was there enshrined together with the Relics he had gathered together in life.

onesimus.name: Onesimus
onesimus.description: The slave in behalf of whom AcSt. Paul wrote his Epistle to Philemon. cording to tradition, the Apostle afterwards appointed him Bishop of Ephesus in succession Accounts vary as to the to St. Timothy. length of his Episcopate, but agree that he was put to death in Rome as a Christian. This probably happened towards the end of the first century. ONESIPHORUS and PORPHYRIUS (Sept. 6) (SS.) MM. (1st cent.) What Holy Scripture tells us of Onesiphorus is to be read in St. Paul's Second Epistle to Timothy (ii. 16-18). St. Porphyrius was a member of his household. They laboured in the work of spreading the Gospel until towards the end of the first century. Then, tradition alleges that they were seized by agents of the persecuting Emperor Domitian somewhere on the Hellespont, tied to wild horses and so torn to pieces. ONUPHRIUS (HUMPHREY) (St.) (June 12) Hermit. (4th cent.) A famous Egyptian Solitary who lived alone for sixty years in the Desert St. Paphnutius, of the Thebais (Upper Egypt). Solitary, has left us a another celebrated detailed and graphic account of a visit he paid to St. Humphrey. He relates too how he assisted at the Saint's holy death and reverThis event must ently interred his remains. have happened late in the fourth or early in the fifth century.

opportuna.name: Opportuna
opportuna.description: A sister of St. Chrodegang and Abbess of a monastery near Seez. She died after a life of great piety and self-denial in The Translation of a part of her a.d. 770. relics to Paris has led to her being specially venerated in that city.

optatian.name: Optatian
optatian.description: A Bishop of Brescia in Lombardy His name appears as one of the signatories to a Synodical letter of the time. He died about A.D. 505.

optatus.name: Optatus
optatus.description: An African Bishop of Milevis, and one of the Fathers of the Church. He was especially zealous in crushing the Donatist heresy ; and the great Doctor St. Augustine reckons him, with St. Cyprian, Lactantius and as most excellent among Christian others, are often writers. referred to by Theologians, a.d. 372 is given as the probable date of his death. His works, still extant,

oran.name: Oran
oran.description: Otherwise St. ODHRAN, which see. (3rd cent.)

orentius and patientia.name: Orentius And Patientia
orentius and patientia.description: Saints venerated at Huescar in Aragon (Spain), but of whom we have little or It is a belief, common no reliable information. in Spain, that they were the father and mother of the great Martyr St. Laurence of Rome.

orestes.name: Orestes
orestes.description: A Cappadocian (Asia Minor) Saint, noted for his zeal in making converts to Christianity. He was arrested under Diocletian and literally tortured to death (a.d. 304).

oriculus and others.name: Oriculus And Others
oriculus and others.description: A group of African Catholics put to death by the Vandals about A.D. 430. Place, number and other particulars are wanting. (May 1) (5th cent.) A French hermit in the Pyrenees whom, on account of his sanctity, the people of Auch insisted on having for their Bishop. He ruled his Chinch with success for over forty years, and was famous alike for his virtues and for his miracles. He passed away about the middle of the fifth century.

oringa.name: Oringa
oringa.description: A poor servant girl, born in Tuscany, who passed her whole life as a domestic and reached a great height of sanctity. When she died (a.d. 1310) at the age of seventy, the bystanders were awed at seeing her face radiant with a supernatural light.

orontius.name: Orontius
orontius.description: OSANNA (St.) V. See SS. VINCENT, ORONTIUS, &c. (June 18) (7th or 8th cent.) A Princess of Northumbria, perhaps daughter of King Altfrid and St. She was buried at Hoveden or Cuthburga. Howden, in miracles were wrought at her tomb. Northumberland, and (Jan. 22)

osburga.name: Osburga
osburga.description: cent.) The Abbess, as some say, first set over his foundation at Coventry by King Canute, and after her death, about A.D. 1016, held in veneration as a Saint by the inhabitants of the district, who in the fifteenth century were authorised to keep her Feast liturgically. But she may be a Saint of much earlier date. No particulars about her are extant. (8th cent. B.C.) OSEE (HOSEA) (St.) Prophet. (July 4) Osee seems, among the Ten Tribes, to have been a contemporary of Isaias in His prophecy was directed Judaea. his compatriots of Samaria, of which he foretells the destruction.

osith.name: Osith
osith.description: An Anglo-Saxon Princess, Abbess to of the monastery of Chich in Essex, who suffered death for the Christian Faith in an incursion of heathen Danes or other pirates. This event is said to have taken place about the middle of the seventh century, but both the date and the particulars are open to controversy. It is also possible that two or more saintly personages of the same name have been confused into the one St. Osith, V.M.

osmanna.name: Osmanna
osmanna.description: An Irish Saint who, crossing to Brittany, lived a holy life in a solitude near Saint-Brieuc.

osmund.name: Osmund
osmund.description: A Norman noble attached to the Court of William the Conqueror. He was made Chancellor of England ; but even in the world, undistracted by business, he lived the Raised to the Bishopric of life of a Saint. Sarum or Salisbury, he showed himself a model Prelate until his holy death, Dec. 2, A.D. 1099, Thence, many years later, his at Old Sarum. relics and Episcopal See were translated to Salisbury. He is especially remembered on account of his skilful arrangement of the Roman Breviary and Missal, so as to include the traditional rites peculiar to the Norman and Anglo-Saxon Church.

ostianus.name: Ostianus
ostianus.description: uncertain.) A Saint venerated at to have (South of Viviers been a priest, but of whom nothing is now known. France), said

oswald.name: Oswald
oswald.description: The successor of King Edwin on the throne of Northumbria in the time of the Heptarchy. He was converted to Christianity during his exile among the Scots. He governed his people wisely and well, labouring above all to reclaim them from heathenism. He perished in the Battle of Maserfleld (A.D. 642) against The head Penda and his Pagans of Mercia. of St. Oswald was eventually recovered and placed in the same shrine at Durham with the body of St. Cuthbert.

oswin.name: Oswin
oswin.description: extraordinary holiness of life in which he had for his master St. Aidan. He succeeded St. Oswald on the In a throne of Deira (a part of Nothumbria). Bernicia he was war with King Oswy of traitorously slain (A.D 651) near Richmond in Yorkshire, and has since been honoured as a Martyr. A solemn Translation of his Relics took place A.D. 1065. cent.) A Prince (7th of Otherwise St. OSITH, which see. OTHILIA (ODILIA, ADILIA) (St.) V. (Dec. 13) (8th cent.) A maiden of noble birth in Alsace who, embracing the life of the cloister, gathered round her more than three hundred nuns. Most austere in her life, she may be said to have passed her days in continuous prayer. She died in her monastery of Hohenburg, about A.D. 720.

othmar.name: Othmar
othmar.description: Of Teutonic origin and already a priest, he was (A.D. 720) appointed Abbot of the monastery of St. Gall in Switzerland. In it he restored the observance of the Rule of St. Columban (later replaced by that of St. Benedict). He was remarkable for his charity to the poor and for his patience in suffering and persecution. He ended his holy life A.D. 759, as a hermit in an island of the Rhine. (Sept. 9)

otho.name: Otho
otho.description: Bishop of Bamberg and Apostle (12th cent.) Born of noble parents in South of Pomerania. Germany, he by his talents obtained great influence at the Court of the hapless Henry IV. and did much to stifle the schism which that Prince, by the appointment of Anti-Popes, sought successful Pastorate at Bamberg, he, invited by the King of Poland, who had conquered Pomerania, made two missionary journeys to that province, and practically converted its population to ChristianSt. Otho died at Bamberg, June 30, a.d. ity. 1139. Besides up. set his to

otteran.name: Otteran
otteran.description: A disciple of St. Columba at Iona, where he himself ended his labours for So great was the veneration in which Christ. he was held that in a later age, when the Bishopric of Waterford was established, St. Otteran was chosen by the people as its Patron Saint.

oudaceus.name: Oudaceus
oudaceus.description: Son of Budic, Prince of Brittany, but brought up in Wales by St. Teilo, whose successor as Bishop of Llandaff he became. He was remarkable as a pastor of souls for his zeal and charity. A.D. 564 is given as the date of his death. OUEN (OWEN) (St.) Bp.

owen.name: Owen
owen.description: (7th Otherwise St. AUDOENUS, which see. (March 3) cent.) An Anglo-Saxon monk who accompanied St. Chad from the North of England in his mission to the Mercians and served him at Lichfield. A man of most holy life, favoured by God with many heavenly visions and other supernatural favours. He passed away about a.d. 680. (Aug. 24)

pachomius.name: Pachomius
pachomius.description: Surnamed " Post-Prydain (Prop of North Britain) ". He was the son of a chieftain on the Scottish Border, and at first a Later he came to Wales and founded soldier. the monastery called after him, Llanbabon, in Anglesey. He died about A.D. 510. (4th cent.) (May 14) One of the most celebrated of the " Fathers of the Desert." He was a hermit in the Thebaid (Upper Egypt) from soon after his conversion to Christianity, and there became a disciple of the Abbot Palaemon. St. Pachomius founded several monasteries governed by a very austere Rule, which he himself had compiled. He seems to have been the first to group Religious Houses subject to one Rule under the jurisdiction of a Father General or Head Abbot. At the time of his holy death (a.d. 348) seven thousand monks were in this manner governed by him.

pacianus.name: Pacianus
pacianus.description: A Spaniard, Bishop of Barcelona, and one of the Fathers of the Church. St. Jerome speaks of him in terms of high praise. He lived to a great age, and appears to have written but unfortunately only three of his Epistles have survived to our age. many theological Treatises,

pacificus.name: Pacificus
pacificus.description: A Franciscan Friar in Italy, known from his native village as of San Severino. In prey all his life long to intense bodily pains, he sought for comfort and relief in God alone, and was by Him favoured with marvellous supernatural graces and with the gift of working miracles. He passed away at San Severino, near Ancona, Sept. 24, a.d. 1721. (April 16)

palffimon.name: Palffimon
palffimon.description: One of the earliest of the Egyptian hermits. He took refuge in Upper Egypt during the persecution under Diocletian, and there passed a long life in the practices of austerity and in the study of Holy Scripture. He died in the arms of St. Pachomius, the best beloved of his disciples, a.d. 325. (4th cent.)

palatias and laurentia.name: Palatias And Laurentia
palatias and laurentia.description: Palatias was a lady of Ancona in Italy, converted to Christianity by her slave Laurentia. They both fell victims to the fury of the persecution under Diocletian, and were executed (a.d. 302) at Fermo, a town not far It is at Fermo that their distant from Ancona. relics are enshrined. (May 30)

palladius.name: Palladius
palladius.description: A deacon of the Roman Church, consecrated by Pope St. Celestine I, first Bishop of the Scots. After founding several churches in Ireland, he laboured long and successfully in North Britain. He died about a.d. 450, and was buried at Fordun near Aberdeen.

palmatius and others.name: Palmatius And Others
palmatius and others.description: Martyrs at Treves under Maximian Herculeus, the Emperor Diocletian's savage colleague. They suffered just before the outbreak of the general persecution. They appear to have been very numerous and at (May 10) least in great part to have been Christian soldiers in the Imperial army. Possibly this massacre had some connection with that nearly simultaneous of St. Maurice and the Theban The date given for the Martyrdom of Legion. St. Palmatius is a.d. 287.

pambo.name: Pambo
