plautilla.description: cent.) (May 20) accepted anonymous Life of SS. Nereus, Achilleus and Domitilla, St. Plautilla was the mother of the She is described as a noble Roman last-named. matron, converted to Christianity by the Apostle She is said to have passed away St. Peter. A.D. 67, the same year in which SS. Peter and Paul suffered martyrdom. the (1st to

plechelm.name: Plechelm
plechelm.description: A Saxon Saint, born in the South of Scotland, who, accompanied by SS. Wiro and Otger, evangelised the still heathen provinces about the Lower Rhine and the mouths of the Meuse. St. Plechelm is said to have been Bishop of Ruremonde, where he died and was buried (A.D. 732).

plegmund.name: Plegmund
plegmund.description: The tutor of King Alfred, at consecrated ArchSt. that monarch's request, bishop of Canterbury by Pope Formosus. Plegmund died a.d. 914. *PLUMTREE (THOMAS) (Bl.) M. See Bl. THOMAS PLUMTREE. (Jan. 4) PLUTARCHUS, SERENUS, HERACLIDES, HERON, SERENUS, RHAIS, POTAMI03NA and

podius.name: Podius
podius.description: cent.) The of Florence. He was a Prelate of wonderful prudence and piety, and he did much during his twelve years of Episcopate for the Glory of God and for the well-being of the Church of a.d. 1002 is given as the date of his Florence, holy death.

poemon.name: Poemon
poemon.description: One of the Fathers of the Egyptian Desert. He died A.D. 450. The His name Greeks hold him in high veneration. is often written in its Latin form " Pastor," He does not seem to have dwelt all his life in the same part of Egypt. Hence, perhaps, the theory of some scholars that there were two Saints Poemon, of whom one flourished in the fourth and the other in the fifth centurv. cent.)

pollio.name: Pollio
pollio.description: A Martyr in Pannonia (Hungary), burned alive during the persecution under Diocletian (a.d. 304). He seems to have been a Lector or Reader (one of the minor clergy). POLY^NUS (St.) M. See SS. PATRITIUS, ACATIUS, &c. POLY^ENUS (St.) M. See SS. HERMES, SERAPION, &c. POLY^INUS (St.) Bp., M. See SS. NEMESIAN, FELIX, &c.

polycarp.name: Polycarp
polycarp.description: (Sept. 10) of famous Martyrs (2nd cent.) (Jan. 26) Converted to Christianity by St. John the Evangelist, about a.d. 80, he became Bishop of Smyrna, and was one of the antiquity. The most Circular Letter of the Church of Smyrna recounting the details of his death has happily been preserved. He was burned alive (a.d. 166) with twelve other Christians, under the His tomb at Emperor Smyrna is His Epistle to the Philippians is the only one of his writings that remains to us ; but he is frequently referred to by the Fathers, especially by St. Jerome and by St. Irenseus, the latter his disciple. still shown. Aurelius. Marcus

polycarp and theodore.name: Polycarp And Theodore
polycarp and theodore.description: Martyrs at Antioch in Nothing Registers. Syria. more is now known about them.

polychronius.name: Polychronius
polychronius.description: A priest, probably of Constantinople, who had attended at the Council of Nicsea (a.d. 325). He was put to death by the Arians in the time of the heretical Emperor It is said that he was struck Constantius. down at the Altar while saying Mass, and that with his blood were mixed the consecrated contents of his overturned chalice.

polyeucte.name: Polyeucte
polyeucte.description: A Roman officer (probably of Greek parentage) in Armenia. He became a convert to Christianity, and on that account was beheaded, either under Decius (a.d. 250), His Acts, as or under Velerian (a.d. 259). given by Metaphrastes, are as touching as any in early Christian literature. The personages introduced by the French poet, Corneille, into his tragedy of Polyeucte (Pauline, the Martyr's wife, Nearque, his friend, etc.) are historical.

polyeuctus, victorius and donatus.name: Polyeuctus, Victorius And Donatus
polyeuctus, victorius and donatus.description: Martyrs at Csesarea in Cappadocia (Asia Minor), of whom we have no more than the names (variously spelled), registered in the Martyrologies on May 21.

pompeius.name: Pompeius
pompeius.description: A Bishop of Pavia in Lombardy who died a.d. 120. He was the disciple and successor of St. Syrus, first Bishop of that See.

pomposa.name: Pomposa
pomposa.description: A Spanish maiden put to death as a Christian at Cordova by the Mohammedan masters of Spain (a.d. 853).

pontianus.name: Pontianus
pontianus.description: The successor of Pope St. Urban I (a.d. 230), in the reign of the mild Emperor, Alexander Sever us. After the murder of the latter (A.D. 235) by the usurper, Maximin, St. Pontianus was banished to the Island of Sardinia, and a few months later succumbed to the hardships he was compelled to endure. (3rd cent.)

pontianus and others.name: Pontianus And Others
pontianus and others.description: St. Pontianus was a Roman A.D. 259 who suffered with four Martyr of other Christians. He had been baptised as a child and miraculously healed of a palsy by the priest St. Eusebius, also commemorated on Dec. 2.

pontius.name: Pontius
pontius.description: See SS. PHOTINUS, SANCTUS, &c. (March 8) (3rd cent.) A deacon of the Church of Carthage. He was the faithful attendant of the Martyr St. Cyprian in his exile and at his trial and execution. St. Pontius has left us a graphic account of the Life and Passion of his illustrious master. He died after a.d. 260. (May 14) This Roman Saint, who died for the Faith in the North of Italy (A.D. 258) under the Emperor Valerian, must not be confused, as has been done by some writers, with St. Pontius of Carthage, the witness of the martyrdom of St. Cyprian. We must be cautious also in giving credit to the tradition that this Italian Pontius was instrumental in converting the Emperor Philip to Christianity. The conversion itself is far from having been proved, and in the writings of the subsequent period more than one Saint is made to claim the distinction of having been the human means by which it was brought about. The relics of St. Pontius, translated into Gaul, have given its name to the town of Saint-Pons, in Languedoc.

poppo.name: Poppo
poppo.description: A pious and fervent monk, born near Li6ge, who, on account of his virtue, was placed successively at the head of several monasteries in Belgium and the North of France. He had considerable influence with St. Henry, Emperor of Germany, and laboured successfully to do away with some of the barbarous customs of his Age. He died at Marchiennes (a.d. 1048). (Aug. 12) These Martyrs, five hundred in

porcarius and others.name: Porcarius And Others
porcarius and others.description: called pirates, Certain number, were the community of the famous Abbey of Lerins in the island of that name, off the coast of France, opposite Cannes in the by Mediterranean. contemporaries " Saracens," but more likely to have been Danes or Northmen, landed on the island (a.d. 731) and ravaged it, putting all to St. Porcarius, the Abbot, had fire and sword. contrived to send away to the mainland the boys that were being educated in his Abbey, Four with thirty-six of the younger monks. The others were carried away by the pirates. rest, mercilessly massacred, have ever since been honoured as Martyrs. (4th cent.)

porphyrius and seleucus.name: Porphyrius And Seleucus
porphyrius and seleucus.description: Palestinian Martyrs, put to death The historian Eusebius at Csesarea a.d. 308. sufferings when gives an account of narrating the martyrdom of St. Pamphilus, one Both of whose dependents was St. Porphyrius. he and St. Seleucus were burned to death at the their

porphyrius.name: Porphyrius
porphyrius.description: A Greek, a personage of wealth his goods and and consideration who, selling bestowing the proceeds on the poor, lived the life of a hermit, at first in Egypt, but afterwards Palestine on the banks of the Jordan. in Much against his will he was made Bishop of Gaza, and presided over that Church for twentyseven years. He worked hard and successfully at the conversion of the Pagans, in his time still a.d. 420 is numerous in Syria and Palestine, Mark, a disciple given as the date of his death. of St. Porphyrius, has left us an interesting and trustworthy life of his master.

portianus.name: Portianus
portianus.description: An Abbot in Auvergne, famous for his miracles and for the courage with which he faced the Merovingian King Thierry of Austrasia, who was ravaging the country, and obtained from him the release of those of the inhabitants he was carrying away into slavery. St. Portianus died about a.d. 540.

possidius.name: Possidius
possidius.description: An African by birth, a disciple of St. Augustine of Hippo and writer of the In contemporary literature Life of that Saint. St. Possidius is frequently mentioned, and he played a useful part in the controversies of his time. He was driven by the Vandals from the city in Africa in which he was Bishop, and ended his days (A.D. 450) in Apulia in the South of Italy. THE BOOK OF SAINTS PRISCUS

potamion.name: Potamion
potamion.description: A young girl, a Christian in Egypt, put to death as such at Alexandria in the persecution under Diocletian ( a.d. 304 about). (May 18) (4th cent.) An Egyptian Bishop who suffered imprisonment as a Christian under the Emperor Galerius, and who, after the Peace of the Church, assisted at the Council of Nicsea True to the Catholic Faith, he (a.d. 325). shared with St. Athanasius his exile. And it is St. Athanasius who relates how the Arians compassed the death of the holy Martyr, about A.D. 340. (Dec. 31)

pothamius and nemesius.name: Pothamius And Nemesius
pothamius and nemesius.description: Martyrs in the Island of (Date unknown.) Cyprus whose Acts have long since been lost.

potitus.name: Potitus
potitus.description: A native of the island of Sardinia who, when a boy, was converted to Christianity, and later, in his turn, succeeded in converting It is alleged that the Emperor his own father. Marcus Aurelius in person conducted the trial of St. Potitus, accused of the crime of professing the Christian religion, or rather, of that of rejecting the gods of Rome. It seems certain that he was put to the torture in Rome itself, but his execution appears to have taken place in some city of Southern Italy (a.d. 166). *POWEL (EDWARD) (Bl.) M. PR^EPEDIGNA (St.) M. See Bl. EDWARD POWEL. See SS. MAXIMUS, CLAUDIUS, &c. (July 30) (Feb. 18) (Sept. 6) PR^ESIDIUS (St.) M. See SS. DONATIAN, PR^SIDIUS, &c. PR^JTEXTATUS (St.) Bp., M. (Feb. 24) (6th cent.) A Bishop of Rouen (France) who, for his courage in denouncing the crimes of the notorious Queen Fredegonda, was sent into banishment and, after his recall, put to death by her orders on the steps of the Altar in his own church (A.d. 586).

pragmatius.name: Pragmatius
pragmatius.description: A Bishop of Autun (France), a correspondent of St. Sidonius Apollinaris. His signature is appended to the Acts of a CounBut nothing is now cil celebrated a.d. 490. really known of his life and merits.

praxedes.name: Praxedes
praxedes.description: A daughter of (July 21) the Roman Senator, Pudens, and sister of St. Pudentiana. She was a fervent Christian, and rendered great service to religion in the first half of the second She devoted her great wealth to the century. relieving of the poor. An ancient and notable church in Rome perpetuates her memory, and bears witness to the esteem of sanctity in which Praxedes was held by the early Christians.

prilidianus.name: Prilidianus
prilidianus.description: PRIMAEL (St.) See SS. BABILAS, URBAN, &c. (5th cent.) A Breton (May 16) to whom churches are dedicated in the Diocese of Quimper, and who is said to have been a native of Great Britain.

primitiva.name: Primitiva
primitiva.description: We have no particulars of this Saint, beyond the name as above and the note of place, " Rome." It is not even clear that she is not identical with the St. Primitiva of Feb. 24. Several ancient Registers write her name Primitia ; others, Privata.

primus and donatus.name: Primus And Donatus
primus and donatus.description: Two African deacons who were done to death by the Donatist heretics while striving to defend an Altar which the latter were bent on destroying out of hatred of the Catholic worship (A.D. 362). St. Optatus has left us a vivid account of their Passion.

primus and felician.name: Primus And Felician
primus and felician.description: cent.) Two aged brothers, Roman citizens, who in the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian bravely confessed their Faith Christ. They were thrown to the wild in the Amphitheatre, but Almighty beasts God repeated in their behalf the miracle He had They were worked for Daniel in the lions' den. therefore conducted outside the walls of Rome and there beheaded. This happened in one of the first years of the fourth century. SS. Primus and Felician have ever been in great veneration in the Western Church. PRIMUS, SECUNDARIUS and CYRIL (Oct. 2) in (SS.) MM. (Date unknown.) Martyrs at Antioch in Syria in one of the early persecutions. No particulars are now obtainable.

principius.name: Principius
principius.description: A Bishop of Soissons (France), and brother of St. Remigius of Rheims. The old chroniclers dwell upon his virtues and sanctity of life, but we have no details of his His body was reverently interred by career. St. Remigius, outside the walls of Soissons, about a.d. 500.

prior.name: Prior
prior.description: An Egyptian, one of the first disciples of St. Antony. He died at the end of the fourth century, being then nearly one hundred years old.

prisca.name: Prisca
prisca.description: A Roman maiden, a fervent Christian, put to the torture and at last beheaded, under the Emperor Claudius II, about A.D. 270. A church dedicated to St. Prisca exists in Rome, where she is held in very great She is, of course, other than the veneration. Priscilla mentioned in Holy Scripture (Rom. xvi. 3 ; Acts xviii. 2, 26), though relics of the latter are enshrined in the Roman church of

priscilla.name: Priscilla
priscilla.description: A noble Roman matron, mother of the Senator Pudens and grandmother of SS. Praxedes and Pudentiana. The tradition is that she was the hostess in Rome of St. Peter the Apostle, by whom she had been converted She appears to have survived to Christianity. the Apostle. A celebrated church in Rome She must not be confused bears her name. with her contemporary, St. Priscilla, the wife of Aquila (Rom. xvi. 3).

priscus, priscillianus and benedicta.name: Priscus, Priscillianus And Benedicta
priscus, priscillianus and benedicta.description: A priest, a cleric and a Religious (July 8) (Jan. 4) woman who suffered death for the Faith in Rome during the reign of Julian the Apostate, about a.d. 362. All the Western Martyrologies commemorate them, though we have no longer any detailed Acts of their Passion.

priscus, malchus and alexander.name: Priscus, Malchus And Alexander
priscus, malchus and alexander.description: Palestinian Martyrs under the Emperor Valerian (a.d. 260). Eusebius mentions them by name in his Ecclesiastical History. They were thrown to the wild beasts during the Public Games at Caesarea. (3rd cent.)

priscus and others.name: Priscus And Others
priscus and others.description: Martyrs in Gaul, near Auxerre, in the time of the Emperor Aurelian. Priscus was an officer in the Imperial army, and of his fellow-sufferers, who appear to have been very numerous, many were soldiers under his command. The greater part of these Christians appear to have been massacred without trial. A formal sentence of death was, however, passed on St. Priscus previous to his execution (a.d. 271).

priscus.name: Priscus
priscus.description: unknown.) An Oriental a Saint, zealous preacher of Christianity, who was put to a death of slow torture when at length he fell into the hands of the idolaters. The little we know of him is taken from the Basilian Menology. PRISCUS, CRESCENS and EVAGRIUS (Oct. 1) (SS.) MM. (Date unknown.) Martyrs whose Acts have been lost. They suffered somewhere on the Danube. Many of the old Registers add the Christians who names of other Confessors, shared their fate at the same time and place.

privatus.name: Privatus
privatus.description: A Bishop in Gaul, whose See of Gevaudan is now that of Mende. He was a man of prayer and of very austere life. In an irruption of Barbarians from Germany he was his life on seized by them, but was offered condition of his revealing the hiding-place of his flock. On his refusal, he was beaten to death (A.D. 266).

probus.name: Probus
probus.description: See SS. ARCADIUS, PASCHASIUS, &c. PROCESSUS and MARTINIANUS (July 2) (SS.) MM. (1st cent.) Two of the warders of the Mamertine Prison in Rome in which SS. Peter and Paul were confined. A miracle, wrought by the two Apostles, converted them to Christianity and they were baptised by St. Peter. They met with tranquil constancy the cruel death to which on that account they were sentenced, and have ever been in great veneration, not only in Rome, but throughout Christendom. the (1st

probus and grace.name: Probus And Grace
probus and grace.description: tion husband and wife. Tressilian, or honour. (April 5) Cornish Saints, by tradiThe at Probus, is dedicated in their church

prochorus.name: Prochorus
prochorus.description: cent.) One of (April 9) Seven Deacons ordained by the Apostles. The tradition is that he afterwards became Bishop of Nicomedia and suffered martyrdom at Antioch. (2nd cent.)

proclus and hilarion.name: Proclus And Hilarion
proclus and hilarion.description: Christians of Ancyra in Galatia (Asia Minor), put to the torture and to death (a.d. 115) during the reign of the Emperor Trajan.

proclus.name: Proclus
proclus.description: A disciple of St. John Chrysostom, and, like him, a Patriarch of Constantinople. He died a.d. 446, in the thirteenth year of his Episcopate, endeared to his flock by his patience and gentleness. All the time left him by his Pastoral duties he spent in prayer and the reading of spiritual books.

procopius.name: Procopius
procopius.description: A Palestinian Christian, a Lector or Reader and Interpreter in the Church of Arrested during the persecution Scythopolis. under Diocletian, he was brought to Caesarea, where he boldly confessed the Faith before his judges and was sentenced and executed (a.d. 303).

proculus, ephebus and apollonius.name: Proculus, Ephebus And Apollonius
proculus, ephebus and apollonius.description: Christians who had crossed over into Italy and were residing at Terni when the holy Bishop Valentine was put to death for the Faith under the Emperor Aurelian. They had honourably interred the remains of St. Valentine, when they themselves were arrested, condemned and executed (a.d. 273).

proculus.name: Proculus
proculus.description: A Bishop in Central Italy, either of Terni or of Narni. He appears to have been a notable personage of his time. He came into contact with Totila, King of the Goths, when the latter was ravaging Italy, and it is generally admitted that he met his death at the hands of this despoiler of his flock.

projectus and marinus.name: Projectus And Marinus
projectus and marinus.description: Martyrs in Auvergne (France). St. Projectus, a zealous Bishop, faithful to his duty, failed not, when needed, to admonish even the great ones of the earth, and thereby made powerful enemies. Some of these murdered him (A.D. 674), together with his friend and confidant, Marinus or Amarinus, the Abbot of a monastery in the Diocese of St. Projectus. (Nov. 7) (1st cent.) The first Bishop of Padua in North Italy, sent thither by the Apostle St. Peter. He converted a multitude of Pagans to Christianity, and his memory has ever since remained in great veneration in the North-East Tradition has it that he lived till of Italy. near a.d. 100, but the various Lives written of him are not generally regarded as trustworthy.

prosper of aquitaine.name: Prosper Of Aquitaine
prosper of aquitaine.description: A native of Aquitaine, a man of great learning and piety, who attracted the notice of Pope St. Leo the Great, and was by him employed in the literary work connected with the subtle controversies then going on with the Nestorian and Eutychian heretics. His treatises, however, against Pelagianism, and his Chronicle, are the most noteworthy He, or as some think, another of his writings. Saint of the same name, became Bishop of St. Prosper is commonly Reggio in Calabria. believed to have died in a.d. 460.

prosper.name: Prosper
prosper.description: A Bishop of Orleans (France), who seems to have been the immediate successor of St. Anianus (a.d. 453). By the writers of the next few centuries this St. Prosper has so often been confused with his contemporary, or contemporaries, St. Prosper of Aquitaine and St. Prosper of Reggio, that nothing certain can be set down concerning his life. (June 19)

protasius.name: Protasius
protasius.description: Born at Milan, he was consecrated Bishop of that city by Pope St. Sylvester. He held the See for about twenty-five years, and passed away a.d. 352. He assisted at the Council of Sardica, where he strenuously defended St. Athanasius and the Catholic Belief in the Trinity. •PROTERIUS (St.) Bp., M. (6th cent.) A Patriarch of (Feb. 28) Alexandria, ordained priest by St. Cyril. He replaced in the See of Alexandria the heretic Dioscurus, and did his utmost to combat the plots of the Eutychians who were leading his flock astray. They, however, succeeded in murdering him on Good Friday, A.d. 557. St. Proterius is greatly venerated in the East.

protogenes.name: Protogenes
protogenes.description: A Bishop of Carrhse in Syria, who, together with St. Eulogius of Edessa, suffered banishment for the Faith in the reign In the end of the Arian Emperor Valens. both Bishops were restored to their flocks. Such particulars as we have of them are taken from the Ecclesiastical History of Theodoret, who wrote in the fifth century. (4th cent.)

protus and januarius.name: Protus And Januarius
protus and januarius.description: Two Sardinian Saints of great Ordained by Pope celebrity in their island. St. Caius, the one to the priesthood, the other to the deaconate, they laboured successfully In the persecution in spreading Christianity. under Diocletian they were put to the torture, and in the end beheaded at Porto Torres, not far from Sassari (A.D. 303).

protus and hyacinth.name: Protus And Hyacinth
protus and hyacinth.description: Two famous Roman Martyrs, probably brothers, servants or dependents of St. Eugenia. The weight of evidence is in favour of a.d. 262, in the reign of the Emperor Gallienus, being the year of their death, though some would defer it for about forty years and make SS. Protus and Hyacinth victims of the In any great persecution under Diocletian. case, arrested as Christians, they were scourged and beheaded. century Pope St. Damasus restored and embellished their shrine, over which verses written by him were inscribed. following the In

prudentius.name: Prudentius
prudentius.description: One of the most learned prelates of his age, zealous and successful in confuting the then threatening heresies of Gotteschalk, Scotus Erigena and others. Butler defends him well from the charge of having in certain his works advanced erroneous passages of doctrines in reference to abstruse points of His name, however, is not inserted theology. in the Roman Martyrology. As Bishop of Troyes he showed himself energetic in reforming Church discipline. He passed away a.d. 861. He is, of course, quite other than the Spanish Christian poet Prudentius.

psalmodius.name: Psalmodius
psalmodius.description: Of Irish or Scottish descent, and a disciple of St. Brendan. He passed into France and lived an austere life as a hermit near Limoges. He died in the closing years of That he is other than the seventh century. St. Saumay seems the most probable supposition in order to reconcile the various accounts given of St. Psalmodius, though the lives coincide in various details. PSALMODIUS (SAUMAY) (St.) (July 15) (6th cent.) A holy man whom the traditions of the Diocese of Limoges in France, where he passed his life, aver to have been a native of Great Britain. He lived as a hermit and became famous for his gifts of miracles and That he flourished in the sixth prophecy. century can hardly be controverted.

ptolemy.name: Ptolemy
ptolemy.description: A disciple of the Apostle St. Peter, sent by him to introduce Christianity into Tuscany. He suffered martyrdom in the town of Nepi, and his relics are venerated in the Cathedral there. (2nd

ptolemy and lucius.name: Ptolemy And Lucius
ptolemy and lucius.description: cent.) Roman Martyrs (Oct. 19) the Emperor Antoninus Pius. St. Justin Martyr, their contemporary, has left us a detailed account of their sufferings. under

publia.name: Publia
publia.description: A Syrian matron, head of a community of nuns near Antioch. While the Emperor Julian was passing on his way to his disastrous campaign against the Persians, she is said to have remonstrated publicly with him on his apostasy, and on that account, by his orders, to have been grievously ill-treated. It is alleged too that he had intended to have her put to death on his return, but his having perished during the war allowed of the holy woman's ending her days in peace.

publius.name: Publius
publius.description: A Saint in Mesopotamia, where he governed two communities of monks, the one of Greeks, the other of Asiatics. He was distinguished for his exceeding austerity of life. (SS.) MM. (Date unknown.) PUBLIUS, JULIAN, MARCELLUS and OTHERS (Feb. 19) African Martyrs, whose names are retained in the Roman Martyrology because registered in all the ancient but whose Acts have long since catalogues, been lost.

pudens.name: Pudens
pudens.description: nothing, save their names, is now known. (May 19) (2nd cent.) The Roman Senator, baptised by the Apostles, who was the of SS. Praxedes and Pudentiana. the He is by many identified with the Pudens mentioned in the New Testament (2 Tim. iv. 21). virgins father

pudentiana.name: Pudentiana
pudentiana.description: Otherwise called Potentiana. She was the daughter of St. Pudens, the Senator. St. Praxedes, she Together with her sister, helped greatly the Church in Rome during the first half of the second century. They buried the bodies of the Martyrs and spent their wealth on the poor. St. Pudentiana's church, built, it is believed, on the site of the mansion of St. Pudens, is one which attracts much attention on account of its association with early Christian history.

pulcheria augusta.name: Pulcheria Augusta
pulcheria augusta.description: The daughter of the Eastern Emperor Arcadius. She wisely governed the countries subject to Constantinople during the minority of her brother, Theodosius II. The latter, on attaining his majority, fell away from the Catholic Faith, and sadly mismanaged the affairs of the Empire. On his death, Pulcheria, becoming Empress, entered into a matrimonial contract with Marcion, an old soldier of valour and experience, altogether fitted for the task She survived only three years, of aiding her. passing away A.d. 453. The Universal Council of Chalcedon salutes Pulcheria as " Guardian of the Faith, Maker of Peace, pious, orthodox and a second St. Helena."

pyran.name: Pyran
pyran.description: (March 5) Otherwise St. PIRAN, which see. Q

quadragesimus.name: Quadragesimus
quadragesimus.description: A Sub-deacon in a church of Southern Italy, commended for his holiness by St. Gregory the Great. The learned Pope relates of him that he miraculously restored a dead man to life. as QUADRATUS (CODRATUS), THEODOSIUS, EM-

manuel and others.name: Manuel And Others
manuel and others.description: Asiatic Martyrs (fortythree in number) who were after torture put to death their leader, is said to have been a Bishop, but all particulars are lacking. Quadratus, Christians.

quadratus.name: Quadratus
quadratus.description: Registered in the old Martyrologies as a disciple of the Apostles and successor of St. Publius as Bishop of Athens, where he died some time before a.d. 130. He is famous as having written a work in defence of the Christian religion, so convincing that, according to St. Jerome, the reading it caused the Emperor Hadrian to put a stop to the persecution then raging. St.

quartus and quinctus.name: Quartus And Quinctus
quartus and quinctus.description: See SS. QUINCTILLUS, QUINTILLA, &c. (May 10) (Date uncertain.) Two Christian citizens of Capua condemned and executed in Rome for their religion, whose remains were taken back to Capua and there enshrined, but all particulars have been lost. (Aug. 6)

quinctian.name: Quinctian
quinctian.description: An African by birth, an account of whose holy life we have from the pen of St. Gregory of Tours. He appears to have been among the Catholics who, when the African Church was persecuted by the Vandals, took refuge in Gaul. He was appointed Bishop of Rodez in the South of France, but driven thence by the Goths, at that time in possession of the country. He retired into Auvergne, where St. Euphrasius made him his successor His sanctity in the See of Clermont-Ferrand. was witnessed to by many miracles, a.d. 527 is given by some as the date of his death. QUINCTIANUS and IREN/EUS (SS.) MM. (April 1) (Date uncertain.) Armenian Martyrs venerated both by the Greeks and by the Latins, but concerning whom no reliable particulars are extant. QUINCTIANUS, LUCIUS and JULIAN (May 23) uncertain.) A group African (Date There appear to have been sixteen, Martyrs. besides the three named, and among them women. The Roman Martyrology several marks them as having suffered under the Arian King Hunneric, that is, in the fifth century, but modern scholars insist that the date remains conjectural. of (Dec. 30)

quinctilis.name: Quinctilis
quinctilis.description: A Martyr of Nicomedia (Asia Minor). Most of the ancient records add as a fellow-sufferer with St. Quinctilis (variously <fec.) a St. written Quintillus, Capitolinus. Quintolinus, (April 13)

quinctus.name: Quinctus
quinctus.description: See SS. AQUILINUS, GEMINUS, &c. QUINCTUS, QUINCTILLA, QUARTILLA, MARK (March 19) at Sorrento, near Naples. The three first-named were probably a brother with his two sisters. It is stated that with them suffered ten other Christians, but no particulars are obtainable. and

quinidius.name: Quinidius
quinidius.description: A French Saint who, after some years of hermit life at Aix in Provence, was elected Bishop of Vaison. He was present at the Synods of Aries (a.d. 552) and of Paris Several remarkable miracles are (A.D. 572). recorded as having taken place in answer to his prayers. He died A.D. 579 or thereabouts. (Feb. 8)

quiriacus.name: Quiriacus
quiriacus.description: He was a Greek by birth, but travelled to Palestine and there embraced the monastic life. He lived in various monasteries and hermitages until, it is said, he had long passed his hundredth year, dying some time before a.d. 550. He had great influence in his time, and is praised for having always without hesitation defended the pure Catholic doctrine in the subtle disputes which troubled the Eastern Church. QUIRICUS (CYR) and

quirinus.name: Quirinus
quirinus.description: An Ulyrian who became Bishop of a town in Hungary now called Seseg. He died for the Faith after enduring many tortures, in one of the last years of the persecution under 310 about). When many Diocletian years later the inhabitants of Seseg had to forsake their homes, on account of the invasion of the Barbarians, and came as refugees in considerable numbers to Rome, they brought (a.d. f"

quiteria.name: Quiteria
quiteria.description: with them the relics of their Bishop-Martyr, St. Quirinus. The relics are still enshrined in one of the Roman churches. (Oct. 11) See SS. NICASIUS, QUIRINUS, &c. (May 22) (Date unknown.) A Spanish Saint concerning whom we have unfortunately no facts which we can assert for certain. Several cities in Spain and in Southern France put forward pretensions to the possession of her relics. Some writers date her martyrdom in the fifth century. The most we can say is that there certainly flourished a St. Quiteria in an early century on the borders of France and Spain, and that, if in time of persecution she in any way attracted attention, it is highly probable that she ended her life by martyrdom. Othenvise St. KEVOCA, which see. (March 13) Carthage (A.D. (Oct. 26) (5th cent.) An African Saint, a Bishop of Carthage. When the Arian Genseric, King of the Vandals, captured 439) he put Bishop and clergy on board ship and drove them away, destitute of everything. They landed at Naples, employed themselves to the best of their ability in ministering to the spiritual needs of the population, and so impressed all who witnessed their patient endurance of adversity that after they had passed away they were universally acclaimed as Saints.

quodvultdeus.name: Quodvultdeus
quodvultdeus.description: *QUIVOX (EVOX) (St.) R *RABANUS (RHABANUS), MAURUS (Feb. 4) (Bl.) Bp. (9th cent.) An Archbishop of Mainz, and one of the most erudite men of his century. His life, both as monk and Abbot of Fulda, and afterwards as the most prominent Prelate in Germany, was such as to attract to him the homage and veneration of all. He died a.d. 856, leaving us valuable Commentaries on the Scriptures and other learned works, the composition of which argues undeniable talent and perseverance in view of the semi-civilised surroundings in which he lived.

radbod.name: Radbod
radbod.description: An Archbishop of (Nov. 29) Utrecht, famous for piety and learning as well as for pastoral zeal. He died at Deventer, a.d. 918.

radegund.name: Radegund
radegund.description: A poor servant girl of Augsburg (Germany), pious and charitable to all to a degree that awakened the astonishment of all. In her intervals from work she busied herself in ministering to the lepers and outcasts in the While engaged on one occasion country lanes. in this holy service, she met with her death, being attacked and torn to pieces by wolves. (Aug. 13) (6th cent.) The daughter of a Pagan King or chieftain ruling in Thuringia, whose assassination was avenged by Clotaire I, King of Soissons. The latter had the child, then twelve years old, baptised and educated. Eventually he married her ; but much ill-usage, crowned by the King's murder of her brother and seizure of his domnions, compelled Radegund to leave him. After some hesitation, she was allowed to embrace the Religious Life, and founded the monastery of Holy Cross at Poitiers. Here she passed away, a.d. 587, venerated in life and after death as a Saint.

rainaldes and others.name: Rainaldes And Others
rainaldes and others.description: Rainaldes, (July 16) St. Amalberga, and sister of St. Gudula, was a nun at Saintes In Hainault, held in great She was put to death veneration by the people. by the Huns then ravaging the country (a.d. daughter cent.) of (Sept. 17)

rainerius.name: Rainerius
rainerius.description: A Bishop of Aquila in the South of Italy, the account of whose saintly life has been lost. *RAINOFLE (RAGNULPH) (St.) V. (July 24) (7th cent.) A holy virgin, related to the famous Pepin, Mayor of the Palace to King She fled from the Court to escape Dagobert. being forced into a marriage, and perished from want and cold. Her relics are venerated at Aincourt, near Louvain. RALPH (RADULPHUS) (St.) Bp. (June 21) (9th cent.) A monk of the Royal Blood of France who became Archbishop of Bourges and who was indefatigable in his Pastoral work. He was also a learned man, and some of his writings are yet extant and useful. He died A.D. 866.

ralph sherwin.name: Ralph Sherwin
ralph sherwin.description: A native of Derbyshire who gained a Fellowship at Oxford and was an After his conversion excellent classical scholar. to the Catholic Religion he gave up all his prospects, and in due time received the priesthood. He made a pilgrimage to Rome, and on his return to England was arrested. Queen Elizabeth offered him high preferment if he would turn Protestant ; but, on his indignant refusal, had him put to death (a.d. 1581) at the same time as Bl. Edmund Campion, whose blood, which stained the hangman's hand, Bl. Ralph reverently kissed before laying down his own life. of (7th cent.)

ramirus and others.name: Ramirus And Others
ramirus and others.description: the monastery of Leon in Spain, massacred by the Arians while chanting the Catholic Creed in the choir of their church (A.D. 630). Benedictine monks

ranulphus.name: Ranulphus
ranulphus.description: The father of (May 27) St. Hainulph, Abbot of Arras, near which city St. Ranulph is stated to have lost his life for the Faith, about A.D. 700.

raphael the archangel.name: Raphael The Archangel
raphael the archangel.description: One of the three Angels venerated by name St. Raphael (Tob. xii. 15) is in the Church. " One of the Seven who stand before the Lord." The Book of Tobias consists of the relation of one of his beneficent ministrations to men. Many churches are dedicated to him, and his Feast is celebrated very generally throughout the Church.

rasyphus.name: Rasyphus
rasyphus.description: A Martyr venerated from early ages in Rome, but of whom nothing is now known. He is whatever possibly identical with a St. Rasius whose relics are enshrined in the Pantheon in Rome. (5th cent.)

ravennus and rasyphus.name: Ravennus And Rasyphus
ravennus and rasyphus.description: Natives of Great Britain who took refuge in Normandy about the middle of the fifth century from the Anglo-Saxon invaders of their country. They lived there as hermits until put to death by order of the Governor (or subordinate magistrate) of Neustria, who The appears to have been still a Pagan. shrine of the Saints is in Baveux Cathedral.

raymund of pennafort.name: Raymund Of Pennafort
raymund of pennafort.description: A Spaniard of noble birth who in middle life entered the Dominican Order and eventually became General of the same. He co-operated with St. Peter Nolasco in the ' THE BOOK OF SAINTS RESTITUTA in Foundation of the Order of Our Lady of Ransom for the Redemption of Captives. He was remarkable as a zealous and eloquent his own life, but conpreacher, austere siderate and kindly with others. He was in great esteem at the Pontifical Court and the chief adviser of Pope Gregory IX. He was one of the most learned men of his time, and his " Collection of Canons known as the " Decretals remained the authoritative text-book of Church Law until the promulgation of the new "Codex ' St. Raymund died, a centenarian, in 1917. a.d. 1275.

raymund of fitera.name: Raymund Of Fitera
raymund of fitera.description: A Spanish Cistercian monk, founder and organiser of the famous Military Order of Calatrava. The object of its members was the recovery of Spain from the Moors, and originally they were Oblates of the Cistercian St. Raymund died A.D. 1163, and soon Order. afterwards his Military Order became secularised.

raymund nonnatus.name: Raymund Nonnatus
raymund nonnatus.description: A Spanish Saint, Religious of the then newly-founded Order of Our Lady of Ransom. He spent his all in the Moorish countries of North Africa in the purchase back end, gave of Christian slaves, and, in himself as a hostage to secure the liberty of one of their number. He thenceforth lived in slavery and endured terrible hardships until his Order succeeded in ransoming him in his Returning to Europe, he was received turn. with the utmost veneration and was even raised to the Cardinalate by Pope Gregory IX. Nevertheless, he persisted in living as a humble Religious until his holy death (A.D. 1240). the REATRIUS (RESTIUS) (St.) M. See SS. DATIVUS, REATRIUS, &c. (Jan. 27)

redemptus.name: Redemptus
redemptus.description: A holy Bishop of Ferentino, a town some distance to the South of Rome, and a friend of St. Gregory the Great, who bears witness to his sanctity. He died about a.d. 586. (May 4) *REDYNG (THOMAS) (Bl.) M. See CARTHUSIAN MARTYRS. *REGINA (REGNIA, REINE) (St.) V.M. (Sept. 7) (3rd cent.) A Christian maiden, put to death on account of her religion at Autun (France), most probably in the Decian persecution (a.d. 250). Some authors, however, number her among the victims of the Emperor Maximian HerciUeus, and give a.d. 286 as the date of her death.

regula.name: Regula
regula.description: REGULUS (RIEUL) (St.) Bp. See SS. FELIX and REGULA. REGULUS (RULE) (St.) Abbot. (March 30) (Date uncertain.) A Greek, the first Bishop of Senlis (North of France), also at one time venerated by the people of Aries (near MarThe old belief seilles) as one of their Bishops. was that St. Rieul was sent as a missionary to Gaul by the Apostles in the first century. But many moderns post-date him to the middle In either case, there can of the third century. be no doubt that he was a singularly holy and His shrine was succpssful missionary Bishop. at Senlis, where he died. (4th cent.) (March 30) According to Scottish tradition, St. Rule was a holy man to whom in the Dime of the Emperor Constantine it was by Divine direction committed to carry away to the ends of the earth a portion of the relics of St. Andrew, Hence, coming to Pagan Scotland, the Apostle. he enshrined them in the place since called St. Andrews, and there presided until his death over a community of fervent Christians. Other and more likely accounts of the Translation of the Relics of St. Andrew to Scotland put it at a much later date, and connect it with the name of the Scottish King Constantine, about the middle of the fifth century.

regulus.name: Regulus
regulus.description: An African (probably a Bishop) driven into exile by the Arian Vandals. He landed in Tuscany, in company with St. Cerbonius and others, and appears to have suffered martyrdom when the Barbarian Totila was ravaging Italv (about a.d. 545).

reine.name: Reine
reine.description: REMACLUS (St.) Bp. Otherwise St. REGINA, which see. (Sept. 3) (7th cent.) A native of Aquitaine, who was Bishop of Maestricht for twelve years, and who ended his life as a monk at Stavelo (a.d. 664). His memory is still in great local veneration.

rembert.name: Rembert
rembert.description: A native of Flanders, where he embraced the Religious life. At the persuasion St. Ansgar, he accompanied him in of his Apostolate of Scandinavia and succeeded him as Archbishop of Bremen. He seems to have been the first to preach the Gospel to the Pagans of Brandenburg. He died a.d. 888. To him we owe a well-written life of his leader, St. Ansgar. REMBERT (REGNOBERT) (St.) M. (June 13) (7th cent.) A pious youth of the Court of King Thierry of France, murdered (A.d. 675) because of his inflexibility in living a clean life, and hence honoured as a Martyr.

remedius.name: Remedius
remedius.description: A Bishop of Gap in the French Alps, the successor of St. Tyagris or Nothing reliable can be cited conTigis. cerning him. REMIGIUS (REMY) (St.) Bp. (6th cent.) (Oct. 1) Born in Gaul A.d. 439, he was consecrated Archbishop of Rheims when only twenty-two years of age, and governed that illustrious Church for over seventy years. He was looked up to as the most learned and most eloquent Prelate of his Age. He is the Apostle of the Franks, of whom he baptised over three thousand, together with their King Clovis. He died Jan. 13, a.d. 533, and has ever since been venerated as one of the greatest glories of the French Church. His Festival is generally kept on Oct. 1, anniversary of the Translation of his Relics.

remo.name: Remo
remo.description: San Remo is a corrupt form of the name of St. ROMULUS, which see.

reolus.name: Reolus
reolus.description: St. Nivard. (Nov. 25) (7th cent.) A Frankish monk, disciple of St. Philibert, and successor in the Archbishopric of Rheims of His relics were enshrined in the Abbey of Orbais, founded by him (A.D. 690 about).

reparata.name: Reparata
reparata.description: A Palestinian maiden of Csesarea who, when but twelve years old, was called upon to give testimony to Christ before the Officials of the Emperor Decius (a.d. 250 about). she was After beheaded as a Christian. Bystanders assert that at the moment of her death they saw a white dove fly upwards from her headless trunk. St. Reparata is venerated chiefly at Florence and at Nice. enduring tortures, terrible (Nov. 10)

restituta.name: Restituta
restituta.description: An African maiden, victim to heathen fury under Valerian (A.D. 255). She was put on board a boat loaded with combustibles, which, when afloat, was set on fire. God's Providence allowed what remained of the boat to drift to the Coast of Italy, the relics These of the Saint being still recognisable. relics are now enshrined in one of the churches of Naples.

tuosa and others.name: Tuosa And Others
tuosa and others.description: Martyrs (4th See SS. CRISPULUS and RESTITUTUS. RESTITUTUS, DONATUS, VALERIAN, FRUC(Aug. 23) in number), put to death at Antioch, probably at the beginning of the fourth century, but no particulars concerning them are extant. (sixteen Syrian All we know of

restitutus.name: Restitutus
restitutus.description: this African Martyr is that he was a Bishop of Carthage, and that St. Augustine (towards the end of the fourth century) preached a Sermon in his honour on his Feast Day. Unfortunately, the Sermon itself has been lost. REVERIANUS, PAUL and OTHERS (June 1) (SS.) MM. (3rd cent.) St. Reverianus, a Bishop, and St. Paul, a priest, Italians by birth, appear to have been sent into Gaul as missionaries by Pope St. Felix I, and to have been evangelising Autun and its neighbourhood at the time when the Emperor Aurelian vanquished the usurper Aurelian was a Tetricus at Chalons (a.d. 272). Christians, and by his fierce orders, Reverianus, Paul, and ten others of the Faithful were put to the torture and afterwards beheaded. persecutor of

reyne.name: Reyne
reyne.description: REYNOLDS (RICHARD) (Bl.) M. Otherwise St. REGINA, which see. See Bl. RICHARD REYNOLDS. See SS. PLUTARCH, SERENUS, &c. (Feb. 6) (Jan. 9) (March 7) (Sept. 7) (May 4) (June 28) (Sept. 22)

rhais.name: Rhais
rhais.description: RHEDIUS (St.) Otherwise St. IRAIS, which see.

rhudlad.name: Rhudlad
rhudlad.description: A Welsh Saint whose name is perpetuated by the Church Dedication in his honour of Llanflyfni in Carnarvon. (Sept. 4) (7th cent.) The Title Saint of the church of She is said to have Llanshudlad in Anglesey. been the daughter of a King of Leinster, and to have lived in the seventh century. But nothing certain is known about her. *RIAN (RHEANUS) (St.) Bp. (March 8) (Date unknown.) The Saint who has left his name to Pembrokeshire. Llanhrian in William of Worcester and Leland describe him as an Abbot, but no dates nor particulars concerning him are ascertainable.

richard.name: Richard
richard.description: cent.) (12th Possibly an English (June 9) Saint. We only meet him in the South of Italy, where he is venerated as the first Bishop of Andria. A document still in existence proves that in A.D. 1196 he, as Bishop of Andria, officiated at a Translation of Sacred Relics, and it is historically certain that from the time of his passing from this world he has been liturgically honoured as a Saint. her

richard of chicester.name: Richard Of Chicester
richard of chicester.description: Richard De Wiche, born near Worcester, distinguished himself from early (13th cent.) youth by his piety and intellectual ability. He studied at Paris and Bologna and, returning to England, was made Chancellor of the University of Oxford. He was a devoted friend of St. Edmund of Canterbury, chosen by him as his chief adviser, and attended him in his Consecrated Bishop of Chichester (A.d. exile. 1245), he bravely defended the rights of his See against the Royal usurpations, but was chiefly conspicuous for his devotedness to his flock and for his care of the poor. He died at Dover in the building still known as the Maison Dieu (A.d. 1253), and was canonised nine years later. (May 4) (16th cent.) A priest of the Bridgettine Order in their monastery of Sion at Isleworth on the Thames, and a man of deep learning and holy life. He was tried, sentenced and executed with the holy Carthusian Martyrs at Tyburn (A.D. 1535).

richard thirkill.name: Richard Thirkill
richard thirkill.description: A native of Durham who, when advanced in years, was ordained priest at His prayer had always been that he Douai. might die for Christ, and he won the Martyr's crown a few years after his coming on the On hearing his sentence he English mission. exclaimed : " This is the day which the Lord hath made : let us be glad and rejoice therein." He was executed with circumstances of great brutality at Tyburn (A.D. 1583).

richard fetherstone.name: Richard Fetherstone
richard fetherstone.description: One of the chaplains of Queen Catharine of Aragon, whose cause he defended husband. He was against hanged at Smithfield (a.d. 1540) for refusing to take the unlawful Oath of Supremacy exacted by King Henry. adulterous

richard kirkman.name: Richard Kirkman
richard kirkman.description: A native of Yorkshire, who Douai, having received laboured for four years on the English Mission. Arrested at York for preaching the Catholic Faith, sentence of death was pronounced upon him. He suffered, August 22, 1582, having passed his last moments in fervent prayer. Orders priests' A.D. at

richard whiting.name: Richard Whiting
richard whiting.description: The last Abbot of Glastonbury, where he presided over nearly one hundred Benedictine monks. They lived lives of such fervour and usefulness that even the Royal visitors sent by Henry VIII could find no fault with the community. But the holy Abbot steadfastly refused to subscribe the Oath of Royal Supremacy, and, on that account, washanged in view of his own monastery (Nov. 14,. a.d. 1539). With him suffered John Thorne and Robert James, monks of the Abbey. RICHARDSON (LAURENCE) (Bl.) M. (May 30> See Bl. LAURENCE RICHARDSON. RICHARIUS (RICARIUS, RIQUIER) (April 26) (St.) Abbot. (7th cent.) A French priest who appears to Favoured have passed some time in England. by King Dagobert, he founded the monastery of Centual (Saint- Riquier) near Amiens. He ended his days (a.d. 645) as a hermit in a neighbouring forest.

rictrudis.name: Rictrudis
rictrudis.description: A devout woman, four of whose children are venerated as Saints. On the death of her husband, she took the veil at the hands of St. Amandus, and for several years presided She, however,. over a monastery in Flanders. THE BOOK OF SAINTS ROGATUS resigned her charge some time before her happy death in A.D. 688. (March 30)

rigobert.name: Rigobert
rigobert.description: An Archbishop (Jan. 4) Rheims, persecuted and expelled from his See by Charles Martel, the father of Pepin and grandfather of St. Bigobert passed the closing Charlemagne. years of his life in a hermitage near Rheims. He died about A.D. 750. of

rioch.name: Rioch
rioch.description: An early (Aug. 1) convert made by Rioch was likewise by St. Patrick in Ireland. him consecrated Bishop, but from love of solitude and contemplation he soon resigned that office and retired to the island of InnisThere he founded a monastery over boffin. which he presided until his death. of (4th Martyrs

ripsimis and others.name: Ripsimis And Others
ripsimis and others.description: cent.) Armenian the Mention is beginning of the fourth century. made of them in the Acts of St. Gregory the Illuminator, Apostle of Armenia. But there is no really reliable account of these Martyrs in existence at the present day. RITA (MARGARITA) (St.) Widow. (May 22) (15th cent.) An Italian Saint who, after eighteen years of married life lost her husband and her two sons. Feeling herself then called to the Religious Life, she professed the Rule of St. Augustine at Cassia, her native place, near In a chronic and very Spoleto in Central Italy. painful malady, her patience, cheerfulness and union by continuous prayer with Almighty God She died May 22, A.D. 1456, never forsook her. and both in life and after death has worked many miracles.

robert.name: Robert
robert.description: The Founder of the Cistercian Order (so-called from its first monastery of Citeaux (Cistercium) in France. It is a branch of the Benedictine Order pledged to a literal and rigorous observance of the monastic Rule. Out of devotion to Our Blessed Lady, St. Bobert enjoined on his monks the wearing of a white habit, and directed that all the churches of his Order should be dedicated to her. The Cistercians are now most generally known as Trappists from a still later Reform which began in the monastery of La Trappe in the North After many times seeking to retire of France. from the government of his monastery, St. Robert died A.D. 1098. (13th cent.) •ROBERT of

robert johnson.name: Robert Johnson
robert johnson.description: A native of Shropshire, ordained priest at Doual, who, after four years of work on the English mission, was arrested, committed to the Tower, tried and hanged at Tyburn, a.d. 1582.

robert of newminster.name: Robert Of Newminster
robert of newminster.description: A Yorkshire priest who took the monastic habit in the Benedictine Abbey of York, but, with others of the brethren, passed to the Cistercian Beform already established at Rievaulx, and founded Fountains Abbey. Later that of Newminster near Morpeth was established, with St. Robert as Abbot. He was favoured with the gifts of prophecy and miracles, and was united in spiritual friendship with St. Bernard of Clairvaux, the great Saint of the Age, and with St. Godric, the holy hermit of Durham. St. Robert died a.d. 1159.

robustian.name: Robustian
robustian.description: A Milanese Martyr of early Christian times, possibly one and the same with St. Robustianus, venerated with a St. Mark on Aug. 31.

robustian and mark.name: Robustian And Mark
robustian and mark.description: unknown.) Martyrs (Aug. 31) at Milan from the early Ages and registered in the ancient Calendars of that Church, but of whom nothing whatever is now known. venerated ROCH (ROQUE, ROCK) (St.) (Aug. 16) (14th cent.) A citizen of Montpellier in the South of France, who devoted his life to the In their behalf serving of the plague-stricken. almighty God enabled His servant to work many miracles. He died a.d. 1337, and has since been venerated as the special advocate of the sick. (Date ROCHESTER (JOHN) (Bl.) M. See CARTHUSIAN MABTYRS. (9th cent.)

roderick and salomon.name: Roderick And Salomon
roderick and salomon.description: Spanish Christians, put to death at Cordova by the Moors during their occupation Roderick was a priest and of Spain (A.d. 857). Salomon a layman. They came to know one another as fellow-prisoners in the same dungeon. Of their trial, tortures and death we have some details from the pen of their contemporary, St. Eulogius. (May 4)

rogatus.name: Rogatus
rogatus.description: ROGER (St.) Abbot. See SS. LUCIUS, ROGATUS, &c. (Jan. 4) (12th cent.) A Saint of English birth who flourished in the twelfth century, and who entered the Cistercian Order in France, where he founded and governed the Abbey of Elan in the Diocese of Rheims. (Dec. 1)

roger.name: Roger
roger.description: A disciple of St. Francis of Assisi, received into his Order a.d. 1216. He was renowned for his gifts of prophecy and the working of miracles. He died in Spain A.D. 1236.

roger, james.name: Roger, James
roger, james.description: with Bl. (16th cent.) A fellow-sufferer Richard Whiting, his Abbot, at Glastonbury. ROLLOCK (ROLLOX) (St.) (Aug. 16) A Scottish corruption of the name of St. ROCH or ROQUE, which see. Forbes notes an even more grotesque variant of the same, SEEMIROOKIE, the title of a chapel at Dundee.

romana.name: Romana
romana.description: A Roman maiden, sister, it would seem, of St. Firmina (Nov. 24), baptised by Pope St. Sylvester. Forsaking her home, she took refuge with a band of Christian She embraced Solitaries near Todi in Umbria. with ardour their life of penance, but was soon called to a better world, dying at the age of eighteen (A.D. 324).

romanus.name: Romanus
romanus.description: A native of Gaul, and brother At the age of thirty-five he of St. Lupicinus. established himself as a hermit in the Jura mountains, between France aiid Switzerland. Many disciples soon gatheredVround the two brothers, who thereupon several St. Romanus (writes St. Gregory monasteries. of Tours) " persisted to the day of his death (a.d. 461) in simplicity of life and in the doing of good works, especially in charitably visiting and caring for the sick." founded

romanus and david.name: Romanus And David
romanus and david.description: Two Princes, sons of Vladimir, the first Christian Duke of Muscovy (Russia). Their zeal for the propagation of the Christian Faith led to their martyrdom at the hands of their heathen fellow-countrymen (a.d. 1010). St. Romanus is known in the East as St. Boris, a name very frequently given in Baptism, and St. David as Gleb.

romanus and barula.name: Romanus And Barula
romanus and barula.description: St. Romanus was a zealous Catholic of Antioch in Syria who, in the persecuEmperors Diocletian and tion Galerius, appears to have incited his fellowChristians to resist by force the Imperial desecrate and destroy Officials charged to For this, he paid with his life their churches. (a.d. 304). A little boy, Barula by name, for persisting that there is only One God, shared his happy lot. under the

romaric.name: Romaric
romaric.description: A priest in Gaul, ordained by St. Martin of Tours and sent by him to evangelise the South of France, where he worked many miracles. He died in St. Martin's arms about A.D. 385. (Dec. 8) (7th cent.) A Saint of the Royal Blood of the Merovingians who, forsaking the Court, retired to the monastery of St. Columbanus at Luxeuil, of which later he was appointed Abbot. He was zealous for Religious observance of the Rule among his monks. He is also said to have founded seven convents of nuns, close the one to the other, with the intent that each in turn should chant the Divine Praises, so that, neither by day nor by night, should their Psalmody be interrupted. ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (3rd cent.) (Jan. 13) Forty Christian soldiers put to death outside the walls of Rome, on account of their religion, under the Emperor Gallienus (a.d. 262). ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) for are the (4th cent.) (Jan. 21) Thirty soldiers put to death in Rome as Christians under Diocletian (a.d. The Martyrs in Rome in the greater 304). And the Antonines, notably Marcus Aurelius, the philosopher, condemned many citizens to death for despising the gods of Rome. From the time that the Emperors themselves insisted upon Divine Honours being paid to them personally, a political motive also Often too, in the first four cenintervened. turies of the Christian era, there were riots in which Christians were massacred by the heathen mob, with or without the connivance of the authorities. The Martyrologies mostly record the various martyrdoms under the head of the most prominent sufferer or sufferers. But here and there, we find entries like this of Jan. 21, in which no individual name is set down. A few of these are here indicated. (3rd ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (March 1) cent.) (3rd cent.) ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (March 4) Nine hundred Roman Christians of whose martyrdom no details are now extant. They appear to have been victims of a massacre Christians in the time of the Emperor of Valerian, about A.D. 260. THE BOOK OF SAINTS RUDERICUS ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (March 14) Forty-seven Christians, baptised by St. Peter, whom the Emperor Nero caused to be beheaded in one day. (1st cent.) ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (April 10) (2nd cent.) A number of Christians whom Pope St. Alexander baptised during his imprisonThey were taken to Ostia and put on ment. board of a ship which was then sunk at sea (a.d. 115 about). ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (June 17) (Date unknown.) Two hundred and sixtytwo Martyrs who suffered in Rome in one of the persecutions. The their martyrdom at the beginning of the fourth century ; but weighty authorities date it much Bollandists place (1st cent.) ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (June 24) These, many hundreds in number, are the Christians put to death by the Emperor Nero (A.D. 64) on the absurd charge that it was they who had caused the great Fire of Rome, probably his own work. The strange and horrible deaths they suffered are well known. Some, sewn up in the skins of animals, were thrown to the wild beasts in the Amphitheatre ; others, besmeared with oil, were used as torches to illuminate the Imperial Gardens ; others were crucified, &c, &c. ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (Aug. 5) Twenty-three Christians of the company of St. Abundantius (Sept. 16), put to Each one death while engaged in prayer. signed himself with the sign of the Cross in the They act of laying his head on the block. suffered under Diocletian about a.d. 303.
