One hundred and sixty-five Christian soldiers put to death under Aurelian (A.D. 274). ROME (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (3rd cent.) (Oct. 25) Forty-six Christian soldiers put to death under the Emperor Claudius II (a.d. 269). (3rd said

romuald.name: Romuald
romuald.description: at (11th cent.) A native (Feb. 7) of Ravenna and founder of the Order of the Camaldolese Hermits, a branch of that of St. Benedict, which had its head house Camaldoli near Arezzo, in Tuscany. Though most austere in his habits, St. Romuald was conspicuous for the cheerful kindliness and considerateness with which he dealt with others. He died June 19, a.d. 1027 ; but his Feast is kept on Feb. 7, the anniversary His Order of the Translation of his relics. has survived in Italy to our own time. ROMULA, REDEMPTA and HERUNDO (July 23) (SS.) vv. (6th cent.) Three devout maidens personally known in Rome to Pope St. Gregory the Great, whose edifying life of self-denial he made the text of one of his extant sermons.

romulus and secundus.name: Romulus And Secundus
romulus and secundus.description: African Martyrs, whose Acts, like so many others, have unhappily been lost. Many of the ancient Registers write Secundolus for Secundus.

romulus and others.name: Romulus And Others
romulus and others.description: St. Romulus was the missionary sent by St. Peter to evangelise the country round Florence, and is honoured as the first Bishop of Fiesole. With other Christians, he was put to death in the reign of the Emperor Domitian (a.d. 81-96). (1st cent.)

romulus.name: Romulus
romulus.description: A Bishop of Genoa, concerning whom we have now no reliable documents. His name, corrupted to San Bemo, has remained to a well-known coast town on the Mediterranean Riviera. contemporary,

romulus and conindrus.name: Romulus And Conindrus
romulus and conindrus.description: Two of the first preachers of Christianity in the Isle of Man, whither they may possibly have been sent by St. Patrick, the their conversion of Ireland. We have no particulars of their lives.

ronald.name: Ronald
ronald.description: An Earl or chieftain of Orkney, and a warlike prince, who, in discharge of a vow, built the Cathedral of St. Magnus at Kirkwall. He was murdered by rebels, a.d. 1158. Many and great miracles attested his sanctity. then engaged in

rosalia.name: Rosalia
rosalia.description: The Patron Saint of Palermo in Sicily, of which city she was a native. She passed her life as a recluse in a cave on a hillside, not far from Palermo, and died there at She was famous the age of thirty (a.d. 1160). for the austerity of her penitential life and for the many miracles wrought in answer to her prayers.

rose of lima.name: Rose Of Lima
rose of lima.description: The Patron Saint of Lima in Of Spanish origin, she, as a Sister of the Peru. Third Order of St. Dominic, lived a life of extraordinary austerity in South America, beai ing patiently the painful maladies to which she was subject. She died in her thirty-first year (a.d. 1617), and was canonised a.d. 1671.

rose of viterbo.name: Rose Of Viterbo
rose of viterbo.description: A virgin of Viterbo in Central Italy who, being unable to gain admittance to the then newly-founded Franciscan Order, lived a life of assiduous contemplation and penance in a solitary place near the convent She died about a.d. 1252. in her native town. (Sept. 1)

ruadhan.name: Ruadhan
ruadhan.description: A Leinster Saint who had under his Rule one hundred and fifty monks, and who is one of the number of the Saints styled the " Twelve Apostles of Ireland." *RUAN (RUADHAN, RUMON, RONAN) (June 1) (St.) Bp. (5th cent.) An Irish Saint (alleged to have been consecrated Bishop by St. Patrick) who came to labour for God in Cornwall. The particulars regarding him are vague and unProbably, this is one of the instances certain. in which the personalities of several of God's servants have been by accident confused into Various churches are dedicated to St. one. Ruan or Ronan. At one period, he lived in Brittany, where he is equally in honour as in the Perhaps it was in Brittany that British Isles. he ended his earthly pilgrimage.

ruellinus.name: Ruellinus
ruellinus.description: A successor of St. Tugwald in Brittany, and by him appointed his successor in the See of Leon.

ruffillus.name: Ruffillus
ruffillus.description: An Athenian sent by Pope St. Sylvester to preach Christianity at ForlimItaly. He is accounted popoli Apostle and first Bishop of that city. He died (a.d. 382) after forty-seven years of Episcopate. Forlimpopoli was destroyed in war (a.d. 1360), when the See was transferred to Bertinora, and the relics of the Saint were enshrined anew at Forli. Central

rufina and secunda.name: Rufina And Secunda
rufina and secunda.description: Two sisters, natives of Rome, whose promised husbands, terrified by the horrors of the persecution of Christianity then raging, had renounced the Christian Faith. In its profession, on the contrary, the two holy women persevered to the end, neither promises availing aught to shake their nor threats After being put to the torture, resolution. 257) under the they were beheaded (A.D. Emperors Valerian and Gallienus. Their relics are enshrined in the Baptistery of the Lateran Basilica. in (July 19) (Aug. 31) (Sept. 9) (Feb. 28) (April 7) (June 14)

rufinus and martia.name: Rufinus And Martia
rufinus and martia.description: Martyrs in one of the Noth early persecutions at Syracuse in Sicily. ing more is now known about them.

rufinus.name: Rufinus
rufinus.description: A Bishop of Capua, concerning whom we only know that he has always been venerated as a Saint, and that miracles have been wrought at his shrine. About a.d. 800, St. Decorosus, one of his successors, translated his relics to the Cathedral, and has left an account of the wonderful testimony given on that occasion by Heaven to his sanctity. RUFINUS, SILVANUS and VITELICUS (Sept. 4) (SS.) MM. (Date unknown.) Three children at Ancyra in Galatia (Asia Minor) who appear to have shared the fate of their Christian parents in one Together with them of the early persecutions. are associated in the old Martyrologies three other Saints, Magnus, Castus and Maximus ; but nothing has come down to us concerning any of the group.

rufinus and others.name: Rufinus And Others
rufinus and others.description: There is great difficulty in disentangling this Saint with his fellow-sufferers from others of the same name, and especially from St. Rufinus of Assisi (July 30). The St. Rufinus of Oct. 11 appears to have been a Bishop of the Diocese in Italy known as " Dei Marsi," and to have suffered at Rieti, under an Emperor, Maximin or Maximian ; but, whether under Maximin I (A.D. 235, about) or under the more Maximian the colleague of Diocletian (at the close of the third century or beginning of the fourth), is uncertain. (Sept. 9) (Date unknown.) Two brothers of whom we only know that they suffered death together because of their attachment to the Christian Faith. Herculeus, notorious

rufinus, valerius, mark and others.name: Rufinus, Valerius, Mark And Others
rufinus, valerius, mark and others.description: African Martyrs of whom we know nothing save the bare names.

rufus.name: Rufus
rufus.description: A Bishop of Capua, in the South is alleged, by St. of Italy, sent thither, it Apollinaris, the disciple of St. Peter. It is not known in what relation he stood to St. Priscus, who seems to have been the first Bishop of Capua. but again, the people venerate other local Martyrs bearing the same name of Rufus, and there is much confusion in the traditions regarding them respectively. St. Rufus was doubtless a Martyr (3rd cent.)

rufus and carpophorus.name: Rufus And Carpophorus
rufus and carpophorus.description: Martyrs at Capua, under DioThis St. Rufus was only a cletian (A.D. 295). deacon, and is clearly a distinct personage from the ancient Bishop St. Rufus, of Apostolic times, though some of the particulars alleged of the one evidently belong to the life of the other.

rufus and others.name: Rufus And Others
rufus and others.description: A Roman citizen with his entire All suffered death in the great household. persecution under Diocletian (a.d. 304). Some say that this family had been converted to Christianity by the better known Martyr, St. Chrysogonus. THE BOOK OF SAINTS SABINIANUS

rufus and zosimus.name: Rufus And Zosimus
rufus and zosimus.description: Two early Martyrs at Philippi in Macedonia, whom St. Polycarp, later in the same century and writing to the same Church, qualifies as " most happy men." They suffered about A.D. 109. *RUGG (JOHN) (Bl.) M. See Bl. HUGH FARINGDON. Otherwise St. REGULUS, tvhich see.

rule.name: Rule
rule.description: RUMOLD (RUMBOLD, ROMBAULD) (Nov. 14) (March 30) (July 1) (St.) Bp. M. (8th cent.) The Patron Saint of Malines in Belgium. An Irishman by birth, he journeyed to Rome, where he was consecrated Bishop and charged with the preaching of Christianity His mission there, eminently in successful, was extended from time to time to the neighbouring provinces. On one of his journeys, he was set upon and barbarously slain by evil-doers (A.D. 775). His shrine is in Malines Cathedral. Brabant. (Date unknown.) (June 1) Venerated at Tavistock in Devonshire and elsewhere in England. He may possibly be identical with one of the Saints, Rumon, or Iluan, or Ronan, assigned to other days in the year ; but such identity is purely conjectural.

rumon.name: Rumon
rumon.description: •RUMWOLD (St.) (Aug. 28) (7th cent.) An infant Prince of the Royal family of Northumbria, who is said miraculously to have spoken and to have made open profession of the Clrristian Faith immediately after being baptised, and to have died (A.D. 650) This led to his having the shortly afterwards. honour of a place in Catalogues of Saints. He was venerated chiefly in Northamptonshire and in Buckinghamshire. (March 27) (8th cent.) A Frenchman who was appointed Bishop of Worms in Germany, but was unjustly driven from his See. He then undertook the work of preaching Christianity in Bavaria, Styria and other parts of Upper Germany. He was eminently successful, finally fixing his See at the place which is now called Salzburg, where he passed away on Easter Sunday, A.D. 718.

rusticus.name: Rusticus
rusticus.description: The seventh Bishop of Clermont in Auvergne, concerning whose election St. Gregory of Tours relates that it was brought about by a special intervention of Divine Providence. He died A.D. 446, in the twentieth year of his Episcopate.

rutilius.name: Rutilius
rutilius.description: Christian, (Aug. 2) This steadfast an African, did all in his power to escape arrest under the persecuting edicts of his time. He wandered from place to place ; but nevertheless, was at last denounced and brought to trial. He bore himself bravely in the torture chamber, and was afterwards burned to death. His martyrdom cannot be dated later than the reign of Decius (a.d. 250). (Dec. 2) (April 12)

rutilus and others.name: Rutilus And Others
rutilus and others.description: unknown.) (June 4) Pannonia (Hungary), of whom nothing certain is now known. Martyrs (Date in *RUYSBROECK (JOHN) (Bl.) See Bl. JOHN 11UYSBROECK. S SABAS (SABBAS) and

sabbas and others.name: Sabbas And Others
sabbas and others.description: A Christian officer in the army of the Emperor Aurelian, and seventy other Christians who suffered death for their Faith in Rome (a.d. 272).

sabbas.name: Sabbas
sabbas.description: A Cappadocian by birth who became one of the most famous of the Palestinian monks, in whose discipline he established He himself was a much-needed Reform. remarkable for his austerity of life and for scrupulous exactitude in the observance of In various journeys to his monastic Rule. Constantinople he rendered great service to the Eastern Church, then much troubled by the Eutychian heretics. He died A.D. 532, at the age of ninety-four.

sabina.name: Sabina
sabina.description: See SS. MANUEL, SABEL, <&c. (Aug. 29) (2nd cent.) A rich widow of the Province of Umbria in Italy, converted to Christianity by the instrumentality of her slave or servant, St. Seraphia, later adopted by her as a daughter. Both suffered death for the Faith, St. Sabina in Rome, about A.D. 127, and St. Seraphia, five years previously. (Aug. 29) (3rd cent.) A Christian maiden, Greek by birth, and sister of St. Sabinian, the Martyr of Troyes (France), was, it is said, baptised in Rome by the priest St. Eusebius, afterwards Pope. Her parents were still heathens, and on this account she set forth to rejoin her As she neared the city of brother in Gaul. Troyes, she was informed of his glorious death for Christ, and prayed God that she might soon be with him in Heaven. The tradition is that, her prayer ended, she forthwith peaceably passed away (about A.D. 276).

sabinianus.name: Sabinianus
sabinianus.description: The brother of St. Sabina, a Greek, who, converted to Christianity, settled in Gaul, where he made many converts to the Faith. He was arrested, tortured and beheaded under the Emperor Aurelian (a.d. 275), at a His village in the neighbourhood of Troyes. remains are enshrined in the Cathedral of that city.

sabinianus and potentianus.name: Sabinianus And Potentianus
sabinianus and potentianus.description: Martyrs at Sens (France), of which city they are regarded as Patron Saints, and Sabinianus as first Bishop. They are said to have been of the seventy-two disciples sent out to preach by Christ himself, and to have been directed to Gaul by St. Peter. They appear to have laboured in several districts in that country, until eventually put to death by the Pagans at Sens. It must, however, be borne in mind that many moderns postdate these Martyrs to the third century. (Jan. 25)

sabinus.name: Sabinus
sabinus.description: A Bishop of Canusium (a town now destroyed) near Bari in the South of Italy. He retained that See for more than fifty-two years, and is said to have been over a hundred years old at the time of his death (a.d. 566). Not only was he in the highest repute for sanctity and zeal among his own flock, but he rendered great service to the Church at large, especially in embassies with which he was charged by the Popes to the Byzantine Emperors.

cassia, paula and others.name: Cassia, Paula And Others
cassia, paula and others.description: We know nothing of these Martyrs save the fact that they are registered in the Martyrologies as Syrians. Some Catalogues add twenty African Christians to their number. (July 20) (Dec. 11) (4th cent.) A Bishop of Piacenza (Italy), a colleague of St. Ambrose, who used to send him his own Works for revision and approval. He seems to have been a man of singular holiness and of remarkable erudition. St. Gregory the Great recounts a miracle wrought by him. He attended various Councils against the Arians, and in some played a very prominent and useful part. SABINUS, EXUPERANTIUS, MARCELLUS, (Dec. 30)

venustianus and others.name: Venustianus And Others
venustianus and others.description: St. under Diocletian. Martyrs at Spoleto (Italy) in the Sabinus persecution was a Bishop, and Exuperantius and Marcellus, two of his deacons. But Venustianus was the governor of Etruria or Tuscany. To him Maximian Herculeus, the savage colleague of Diocletian, had addressed a special Decree enjoining the persecution to death of all Christians. Becoming himself a convert, Venustianus, with his wife and family, shared at Assisi the fate of the two deacons, who were St. Sabinus had his hands cut off, beheaded. and died in prison a.d. 302. *SACER (MO-SACRA) (St.) Abbot. (March 3) (7th cent.) An Irish Saint who built the monastery of Saggard, which he governed with zeal and success. He assisted at the great Synod held bv Flann, Archbishop of Armagh. SACERDOS (SARDOU) (St.) Bp. (May 4) (6th cent.) A native of Bordeaux, who founded a monastery near Perigueux, and afterwards became Bishop of Limoges. He was famous for his zeal and miracles. He died about A.D. 530 (having resigned his pastoral charge) while on his return journey to his monastery, where his relics were enshrined.

sacerdos.name: Sacerdos
sacerdos.description: A Spanish Saint honoured as Bishop of Saguntuin (Morviedo), where his relics are. Nothing else is known about him. SACERDOS (SERDOT) (St.) Bp. (Sept. 12) (6th cent.) A distinguished Bishop of Lyons who took part in the Council of Orleans (a.d. 549). He died at Paris, King Childebert, whose spiritual adviser he had been, assisting at his deathbed. His remains were transported to Lyons.

sadoc.name: Sadoc
sadoc.description: A Dominican Saint, received into the Order by St. Dominic himself, and by him sent to Hungary and Poland. He with his community of forty Religious, suffered martyrdom in the Tartar Invasion (A.D. 1260).

sadoth and others.name: Sadoth And Others
sadoth and others.description: A Bishop in Persia who, with one hundred and twenty-eight of his fellow Christians, was put to death (A.D. 345) by King Sapor, near Ctesiphon, soon after the holy Bishop Simeon. *SADWEN (SATURNINUS) (St.) (6th cent.) A brother of (Nov. 29) St. Ultyd and disciple of St. Cadfan. Some Welsh churches are dedicated to him. He lived in the sixth century, as probably did also another Welsh Saint of the same, or nearly the same, name, Sadwen, or Sadyruyn, of Llansadwruen in Carmarthenshire.

sagar.name: Sagar
sagar.description: A Bishop of Laodicea (Asia Minor) who was put to death as a Christian in the reign of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius. The historian Eusebius and others of the But the tradition that ancients mention him. he was a disciple of St. Paul the Apostle seems quite impossible of belief, as the date of his death must have been about a.d. 175, more than a hundred years later than that of the Apostle.

salaberga.name: Salaberga
salaberga.description: cent.) A noble (Sept. 22) French woman of Langres who, left a widow, founded and governed as Abbess a monastery of three hundred nuns at Laon. The Chronicles lay great stress on her gentleness and invariable cheerfulness.

salaun.name: Salaun
salaun.description: A poor man in Brittany who, despised by all, reached a height of interior sanctity such that his tomb remains to this day a place of pilgrimage. He died a.d. 1358. (Sept. 14)

sallustianus.name: Sallustianus
sallustianus.description: A Saint honoured as such from early ages in the Island of Sardinia, but of whom nothing more is now known. Some Catalogues describe him as a Martyr.

salome and judith.name: Salome And Judith
salome and judith.description: Salome is said to have been an (9th cent.) Princess, on whose exile Anglo-Saxon in Germany, Judith, a pious widow, took pity^ They are venerated in Bavaria, where they are reputed to have lived as Recluses ; but their" history is very uncertain. (Oct. 22>'

salome.name: Salome
salome.description: SALOMEA (St.) V. See St. MARY SALOME. (Nov. 17> (13th cent.) A Polish Saint of the Franciscan. Order, betrothed in her early years to a prince, heir to the throne of Hungary. As Abbess of a monastery, she governed with zeal and charity her community, and terminated her labours by a holy death (Nov. 17, A.D. 1268). Her' sacred relics are enshrined at Cracow.

salomon.name: Salomon
salomon.description: malcontents among his subjects. They murThis St. Salomon dered him about a.d. 550. is sometimes confused with Salomon III, also a Duke of Brittany, who nourished in the ninth century, and was likewise a Saint honoured as a Martyr. (Sept. 28) (Date unknown.) He is sometimes set down Salonius. He is in the Manuscripts as St. always described as having been Bishop of Genoa, and rightly, as the claims of Geneva and of the Spanish city of La Puerta (Janua) However, his cultus at are easily ruled out. Genoa in Italy was only established in the sixteenth century. *SALT (ROBERT) (Bl.) M. See CARTHUSIAN MARTYRS.

salvinus.name: Salvinus
salvinus.description: A Bishop of Verona (North of Italy), a learned and eloquent Prelate, remarkable not only for his holiness of life but for his extreme gentleness in treating with others. a.d. 562 is given as the likely date of his death. (Jan. 11) Martyr, otherwise unknown, of whom Possidius tells us that St. Augustine preached the Panegyric. unknown.) The African (Date

salvius.name: Salvius
salvius.description: A Bishop of Amiens, in which See he succeeded St. Honoratus. He was famous for miracles and for his gift of supernatural prayer. He died a.d. 695. Some years later, his body was transferred to Montreuil. (8th cent.)

salvius and superius.name: Salvius And Superius
salvius and superius.description: St. Salvius, born in the South of France, became Bishop of Angoul§me. He later undertook the preaching of Christianity to the Pagans of Flanders, and met his death at their hands in the neighbourhood of Valenciennes, together with St. Superius, his priest or deacon. (6th cent.) SALVIUS (SAUVE) (St.) Bp. (Sept. 10) St. Gregory of Tours gives some account of his life and miracles. He was, it is most likely, of Frankish extraction, and from being a monk and later an Abbot, was promoted to the Bishopric of Albi, where he devoted himself to his flock. He was especially careful of his poor, among whom he more than once There is a distributed all the goods he had. certain confusion in some of the Chronicles, not all of which disentangle, in regard to details, what regards St. Salvius of Albi from matters connected with St. Salvius of Amiens and All three were St. French Saints and Bishops, and more or less contemporaries.

samonas.name: Samonas
samonas.description: Salvius of Angouieme. (Nov. 15) See SS. GURIAS and SAMONAS.

sampson.name: Sampson
sampson.description: A priest at Constantinople who lived in the time of the Emperor Justinian, and earned the title of " Father of the poor." It is related of him that when the Emperor was lavishing money on the building of the magnificent Cathedral of St. Sophia, St. Sampson insisted on the prior claim of the sick and distressed, and that, side by side with the spacious church, should be erected a great Hospital, worthy of its position and of the Imperial magnificence.

samson xenodochius.name: Samson Xenodochius
samson xenodochius.description: Born in Rome, he passed his life in Constantinople, where he devoted himself to the care of the sick poor, and founded an important hospital for their benefit. He died a.d. 530.

samthana.name: Samthana
samthana.description: An Irish Saint, Foundress and first Abbess of Cluain-Bronach in Meath. (Feb. 16) See SS. ELIAS, JEREMIAS, &c.

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.description: The First Book of Kings, on that account often called the First Book of Samuel, contains the history of the Prophet, the wonders of his birth and childhood (i., ii.) ; his Judgeship of Israel (iv.-vii.) ; his anointing his replacing him by Saul, King (viii.-x.) ; David (xvi.) ; and his death (xxv.).

sananus.name: Sananus
sananus.description: An Irish Saint, Patron of Plou Sane in Brittany, where he died A.D. 485.

sancius.name: Sancius
sancius.description: A youth of Cordova in Spain, put to death by the Mohammedans, out of hatred of the Christian religion (a.d. 851). St. Eulogius tells us that St. Sancius perished by the Eastern punishment of impalement.

sanctinus.name: Sanctinus
sanctinus.description: (6th cent.) A Briton who, crossing over to Ireland, was made Bishop of a See near Dublin. He is by some thought to have been a son of St. Salomon of Cornwall and brother of St. Cybi. (Sept. 22) Alleged to have been the first Bishop of Meaux and a disciple of St. Denis This would place him in the third or of Paris. fourth century of the Christian era, accepting the modern theory of the dates of St. Denis and other Apostles of Gaul. or another Saint of the same name, is claimed also by Verdun. We have nothing certain to relate of either. Sanctinus, St.

sandolus.name: Sandolus
sandolus.description: A Spanish Martyr, probably of the beginning of the fourth century. Beyond the mention of him in connection with Cordova, in the Catalogues of Martyrs, we have no information respecting him.

sapientia.name: Sapientia
sapientia.description: Otherwise St. SOPHIA, which see. (4th cent.)

sapor, isaac and others.name: Sapor, Isaac And Others
sapor, isaac and others.description: A band of Martyrs in Persia who endured savage tortures and in the end were beheaded under Sapor II, the persecuting monarch (a.d. 339). SARAGOSSA (MARTYRS of) (SS.) his are Their names (4th cent.) fellow-citizens. (April 26) Prudentius, the Christian poet, himself a native of Saragossa, ce ebrated in the next generation the triumph of these eighteen of OPTATUS, LUPERCUS, SUCCESSUS, MARTIALIS, JULIA, URBAN, QUINTILLIAN, PUBLIUS, FRONTO, FELIX, C^ECILIAN, APODEMUS, EVENTIUS, PRIMITIVUS, SATURNINUS, and three others of the same name. They persecution ordered by Diocletian and under the Prefect Dacian, notorious for the savagery he displayed in carrying out the behests of his Imperial Most of them were put to master (a.d. 304). death on one and the same day ; the others after relics, discovered in a.d. 1389, are enshrined at Saragossa. examination. suffered second Their the in a SARAGOSSA (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (4th cent.) (Nov. 3) Christians of Saragossa, other than the Martyrs commemorated on April 26, done to death in the same year (A.D. 304), in the last great persecution, that of Diocletian The pitiless Datian (or and his colleagues. Dacian), the Official charged with the enforcing in Spain of the Imperial edicts, had his residence The number of his victims in in Saragossa. that city and its neighbourhood is incredible. Neither age nor sex were respected. All alike were savagely tortured, and in various fashions made away with. The bones of Christians, heaped together and bleached in the sun, formed for long afterwards a little white hillock. Hence the name, by which the Saragossa Martyrs of a.d. 304 were known (like others in Africa) of the " Massa Candida (White Mass)." (Jan. 29) Martyrs at Edessa in Syria (a.d. 101), under the Emperor Trajan. They were brother and sister. St. Sarbelius, previous to his conversion to Christianity, had been a They- were atrocipriest in a temple of idols. ously tortured before being executed. (2nd cent.)

sarmata.name: Sarmata
sarmata.description: An Egyptian and a disciple of St. Antony. He is mentioned by St. Jerome. He was put to death in his monastery by a band of wandering Arabs (a.d. 357), but has always been honoured as a Martyr for having suffered in the cause of right.

saturianus.name: Saturianus
saturianus.description: See SS. MARTINIAN, SATURIANUS, Ac. (June 4) (Date unknown.) A Saint said to have come from Germany into the neighbourhood of Arras, and there to have been attacked and put to death while defending her virtue.

saturninus, theophilus and revocata.name: Saturninus, Theophilus And Revocata
saturninus, theophilus and revocata.description: They appear to have been Spanish Christians of the number of the many who gave their lives for their Faith in the persecution under Decius in the middle of the third centurv. and

saturninus, castulus, magnus and lucius.name: Saturninus, Castulus, Magnus And Lucius
saturninus, castulus, magnus and lucius.description: Some of the flock of St. Valentine, Bishop of Terni (Italy), whose fidelity to Christ they imitated, and whom they followed to martrydom.

saturninus and others.name: Saturninus And Others
saturninus and others.description: A group of African Martyrs all the ancient Martyrologies, registered in including that of St. Jerome ; but of whom we have no other record.

saturninus.name: Saturninus
saturninus.description: A Martyr at Cagliari (Sardinia) in the persecution under Diocletian (a.d. 303). Manuscript Acts of this Saint were extant in the sixteenth century, but appear to have been since lost. (Nov. 27)

celestine.name: Celestine
celestine.description: Martyrs in one of the early persecutions, whom the Roman Martyrology as having suffered in Rome. The claims Bollandists, however, have ascertained that at least SS. Saturninus and Neopolus were put to Alexandria. We have otherwise death no particulars about any of the group. at

saturninus and lupus.name: Saturninus And Lupus
saturninus and lupus.description: Cappadocian Martyrs, it would seem, but to which of the early persecutions to attribute their trial and death it is now impossible to decide. SATURNINUS, NEREUS and OTHERS (Oct. 16) r (SS.) MM. (5th cent.) A band of nearly four hundred Catholics, put to death on account of their religion, in Africa, by the Arians, under the Vandal King Genseric. They are registered in the lists immediately after the better- known SS. Martinian and Saturninus, and together with them is noted another company of nearly There is much conthree hundred sufferers. troversy respecting them, particularly as regards date and place, among the learned.

saturninus and sisinnius.name: Saturninus And Sisinnius
saturninus and sisinnius.description: Roman Martyrs in the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian (about A.D. 303). They are associated with Pope St. Marcellus and with SS. Cyriacus, Largus and Smaragdus. They were both very aged ; but were not on that account spared the torture St. Sisinnius was a deacon. before execution. (Nov. 29) This is St. Sernin, the Saint of Toulouse. He was a missionary sent from Rome by Pope St. Fabian (A.D. 251) to preach in Southern Gaul, where he founded the Bishopric St. Sernin, after converting a of Toulouse. multitude of heathens, was arrested in the persecution under Valerian (a.d. 257), and put to an exceptionally cruel death, being fastened behind a wild bull which dragged him about until he was dashed to pieces. (3rd cent.)

saumay.name: Saumay
saumay.description: Otherwise St. PSALMODIUS or PSALMOD, which see.

savin.name: Savin
savin.description: A Spanish Saint who entered a Benedictine monastery in France, hut later lived as a hermit in the neighbourhood of Lourdes, not far from which place of pilgrimage the church of St. Savin may still be seen. He was idolised by the poor folk of the vicinity, who had found in him their counsellor and helper in their every need. The precise year of the death of St. Savin is unknown.

savina.name: Savina
savina.description: A holy woman of Milan who busied herself during the persecution under Diocletian in ministering to the Martyrs while in prison, and in interring their bodies after She herself passed away while execution. praying at the tomb of two of these, SS. Nabor and Felix (a.d. 311).

savinus and cyprian.name: Savinus And Cyprian
savinus and cyprian.description: Two brothers, venerated as Saints at Brescia in Lombardy. There is a doubt as to whether they were Italians or strangers from Gaul. The Acts we have of them are not reliable.

sawyl.name: Sawyl
sawyl.description: A Welsh chieftain, father of St. Asaph. The traditions respecting him are very obscure.

scannal.name: Scannal
scannal.description: St. Scannal of Cell-Coleraine was a disciple of St. Columba. He distinguished himself by his zeal and success as a missionary. (Jan. 2)

scholastica.name: Scholastica
scholastica.description: The sister of St. Benedict, the of Western monasticism. She is legislator regarded as the first nun of his Order. St. Gregory the Great relates of her that by her prayers she miraculously obtained opportune rain from Heaven ; and again that at the moment of her holy death (a.d. 543) St. Benedict in a vision saw her innocent soul, in the semblance of a white dove, wing its flight heavenwards. (6th cent.) *SCHOTIN (SCARTHIN) (St.) (Jan. 6) While a youth, St. Schotin left Ireland to become a disciple of St. David in Wales. On his return to his native country he for many years led the life of an anchorite at Mount Mairge (Queen's County), and practiced heroic penance. He founded a school for youths at Kilkenny, no mean achievement at that place and time.

scillitan martyrs.name: Scillitan Martyrs
scillitan martyrs.description: cent.) (July 17) at Carthage. They suffered under the Emperor Septimius Severus and the Proconsul Saturninus ; and the Official Acts of their trial and condemnation (a.d. 202 about) as Christians are still extant. They were beheaded ; and their dying words were a thanking of Almighty God for having vouchsafed to number them among the Holy Martyrs. SCRYVEN (THOMAS) (Bl.) M. Martyrs famous Twelve (May 4) (3rd See CARTHUSIAN MARTYRS.

scubiculus.name: Scubiculus
scubiculus.description: See SS. NICASIUS, QUIRINUS, &c. *SEACHNALL (SECUNDINUS) (St.) Bp. (Nov. 27) (5th cent.) A nephew and disciple of St. Patrick. He became Bishop of Dunsaghlin and died a.d. 447.

sebaldus.name: Sebaldus
sebaldus.description: A Frank who, after a pilgrimage to Rome, accompanied St. Willibald in his Apostolate to Germany. There he lived a

sebastian.name: Sebastian
sebastian.description: lire, preaching Christ to all who hermit's approached his cell. His relics are enshrined in the church at Nuremberg which bears his name. (Jan. 20) (3rd cent.) One of the most renowned of the Roman Martyrs. He was an officer in the Imperial army, and a favourite of the Emperor Nevertheless, when he became a Diocletian. Christian, no mercy was shown him. Tied to a tree, his body was made a target for the Roman archers, after which, it being discovered that he was still breathing, he was clubbed to death (a.d. 288).

sebastian valfre.name: Sebastian Valfre
sebastian valfre.description: A native of Savoy and a priest of the Oratory of St. Philip Neri. He was a man of God, intent only on prayer and on the doing of good works. In his humility, he refused the Archbishopric of Turin offered him by King Victor Amadeus of Piedmont, who greatly esteemed and respected him. He literally sold all his goods and gave the proceeds to the poor. He died at Turin at the age of eightv (a.d. 1710). (Sept. 16) cent.) A woman of Phrygia (Asia (1st Christianity by the Minor), Later, she was put to death on Apostle St. Paul. account of her religion, at Heraclea in Thrace, not far from Byzantium (Constantinople). converted to

sebbi.name: Sebbi
sebbi.description: A King of the East Saxons in the time of the Heptarchy, a man of God and Growing old, he resigned his a wise ruler. crown to his sons and retired into a monastery to prepare for his end, which came a.d. 697. His shrine in St. Paul's, London, was to be seen till the Great Fire of a.d. 1666.

secundianus.name: Secundianus
secundianus.description: (Oct. 2) (Feb. 17) See SS. DONATUS, SECUNDIANUS, &c. SECUNDIANUS, MARCELLIANUS and

verianus.name: Verianus
verianus.description: Tuscan Martyrs who suffered near Civita Vecchia, under the Emperor Decius Secundianus seems to have been (a.d. 250). a prominent Government Official ; the others are described as " Scholastics." (March 2)

secundinus.name: Secundinus
secundinus.description: A Spanish Saint put to death for the Faith at Cordova. His Acts are is uncertain whether he was a lost, and it victim sacrificed for Christ under one of the Pagan Emperors of Rome, or under the VisiGothic Arian Kings, or under the Mohammedan Caliphs, who each in turn ravaged the Church of Spain. No documents mentioning him are extant.

secundus.name: Secundus
secundus.description: See SS. CARPOPHORUS, EXANTHUS, &c. (Aug. 26) (3rd cent.) One of the officers of the famous Theban Legion, commanded by St. Maurice, which was massacred as wholly composed of Christians by order of Maximian, colleague of St. Secundus was brought with Diocletian. St. Maurice to the coast of the Mediterranean, and there, after a sort of trial, put to death at Ventimiglia, some months after the massacre SECUNDUS, FIDENTIUS and VARIOUS (Nov. 15) (SS.) MM. (Date unknown.) whose names are registered in the ancient Martyrologies, but of whom nothing more is now known. (Dec. 19)

secundus and others.name: Secundus And Others
secundus and others.description: When St. Athanasius was driven by the Arians from his See of Alexandria, the heretic, George, protected by the Emperor Constantius, was intruded in his place. This George forthwith set about persecuting the Catholic Bishops and clergy of Egypt. Secundus and many other priests were scourged to death. Some sixteen Bishops were banished ; and a multitude, both of clergy and laity, were savagely maltreated, so that many died of the were received (A.D. ill-usage rightly honoured as Martyrs. They 357).

seduinus.name: Seduinus
seduinus.description: Possibly identical with St. SWITHIN of WINCHESTER.

seiriol.name: Seiriol
seiriol.description: A Welsh Saint, whose memory is perpetuated by the name of the Island YnysLittle or nothing is otherwise known Seiriol. about him. (Sept. 19) (Feb. 16) See SS. PORPHYRIUS and SELEUCUS.

seleucus.name: Seleucus
seleucus.description: A Syrian Saint, honoured in the East, and often described as a Martyr. But all record of him is limited to Oriental Calendars.

selyf.name: Selyf
selyf.description: Otherwise St. SALOMON, which see. *SENACH (SNACH) (St.) P. Bp. (Aug. 3) (6th cent.) A disciple of St. Finnian and his successor at Clonard. *SENAN (SENAMES) (St.) Bp. (March 8) (6th cent.) Bom in Maglachla (a.d. 488), St. Senan was a disciple of Abbots Cassidus and Natalis. Having established a monastery in the Island of Inniscorthy (Leinster), he visited Rome and Gaul, and became most intimate with St. David. He returned to Ireland and died in Iniscarra, about a.d. 560. A church near Land's End in Cornwall is dedicated to him, though a priest associated with St. Germanus of Auxerre, of much earlier date, may be the true Title Saint.

senan.name: Senan
senan.description: Said to have been a hermit in (7th cent.) There is much confusion in the North Wales. records of Saints of this and similar names, and consequently it is not possible to be precise in giving an account of them.

senator.name: Senator
senator.description: All particulars concerning Saint have been lost. The lists give this " Albanum " as the place of his death. The most probable conjecture is that the town referred to is Apt in the South of France, not far from Viviers, which was anciently known as Alba Helvetiorum.

seraphia.name: Seraphia
seraphia.description: A Christian maiden of Syrian origin, who lived in Rome on the Mount Aventine as the adopted daughter of St. Sabina, a noble matron whom she converted to Chrisbeheaded tianity. (a.d. 122), was given honourable burial by Sabina, who later herself won the crown of martyrdom.

seraphina.name: Seraphina
seraphina.description: We have no record of this Saint, except that in the Martyrologies she is said to have been of " Civitas Mamiensis." It is only by guesswork that some have identified this place with a town in Armenia ; others with one in Spain. and

seraphinus.name: Seraphinus
seraphinus.description: A Capuchin Friar, an Italian of Fermo, who lived a wonderful life of selfdenial and charity as a Lay-brother in the Convent of his Order at Ascoli, where he died a.d. 1604. He was canonised a.d. 1767.

serapion.name: Serapion
serapion.description: An Egyptian monk, later Bishop of Thumuis, who took part (a.d. 347) in the Council of Sardica, and in his time strenuously upheld the Catholic Faith against the Arians. He may have survived another twenty years after the Council. He was associated both with St. Athanasius and St. Antony. St. Jerome also makes mention of him. He was a learned man and wrote several works, of which by far the most important is his "Liturgy," discovered in our own time, and first published A.D. 1899. (March 26)

serena.name: Serena
serena.description: Described as the wife of the Emperor Diocletian, and as secretly a Christian. She certainly sought as far as was in her power After her to mitigate the lot of the Christians. death they venerated her as a Saint. The little we know of her comes from the Acts of St. Susanna, V.M., and from those of Pope St. Caius (A.D. 283-296).

serenus.name: Serenus
serenus.description: Two of this name are registered as fellow sufferers with St. PLUTARCHUS, which see.

sergius.name: Sergius
sergius.description: Of Syrian parentage, but born at Palermo in Sicily, St. Sergius I ruled the Church from a.d. 687 to A.D. 701. He bravely resisted the encroachments of the Emperors of Constantinople, and rejected their false Synod of A.D. 691, known as the Trullanum or FifthSixth. He sent SS. Chilian, Swithbert, Willibrord and others as missionaries to the heathens of Germany. To him is attributed the introduction of the Agnus Dei into the Canon of the Mass.

sergius and bacchus.name: Sergius And Bacchus
sergius and bacchus.description: Romans by birth and officers in the Imperial army, who were put to death by order of Diocletian or of one of his colleagues, towards the end of the third century. The prolix accounts written in the early Middle Ages of their glorious deaths for Christ seem But the of too late date to be really reliable. extension of their cultus throughout the Church was so rapid as to indicate distinctive features in their Passion.

servandus and germanus.name: Servandus And Germanus
servandus and germanus.description: Victims of the persecution under Diocletian in the first years of the fourth century. They suffered at Cadiz, and their memory is in great honour throughout Spain.

servatius.name: Servatius
servatius.description: A Bishop of Tongres in the Low Countries, whence the See was later transferred St. Gregory has left us a long to Maestricht. account of St. Servatius and of the many miracles he wrought. He made a remarkable prophecy, foretelling the invasion of the Huns, One of his which was fulfilled a century later. merits was his having given hospitality to St. Athanasius, when the latter had been driven from Egypt by the Arians. St. Servatius died A.D. 384. (Dec. 31)

servus.name: Servus
servus.description: One of the victims in Africa of the persecuting fury of the Arians under Hunneric, King of the Vandals. St. Servus died in the torture chamber about a.d. 505. He was a man of noble birth, and otherwise distinguished. What we know of him is taken from the Life of St. Eugene, the MartyrBishop of Carthage, written by their contemporary, Victor Vitensis, the historian.

servusdeus.name: Servusdeus
servusdeus.description: SETHRYDA (St.) V. (Jan. 10) (7th cent.) A daughter of a King of East Anglia, who, with her sister, St. Ethelburga, (July 1) See SS. LIBERATUS, BONIFACE, Ac. ; ; ; and her niece, St. Ercongotha, became a nun under St. Burgondofora, or Fara, in the Abbey of St. Sethryda in due Faremoutier in France. time was chosen as its Abbess. She passed away about A.D. 660. cent.) (SS.) (13th

seven brothers.name: Seven Brothers
seven brothers.description: The seven sons of St. Felicitas The names registered are Janu the Martyr. arius, Felix and Philip, scourged to death Sylvanus, thrown headlong over a precipice ; Vitalis and Martial, beheaded. Alexander, Their mother was also beheaded four months These Martyrs appear to have suffered later. under the Emperor Antoninus Pius (A.D. 150) though some scholars insist upon a later date, Their death seems under Marcus Aurelius. to have been rather instigated by the heathen priests than to have been an incident in a general persecution of Christians. They are amongst the most famous of Roman Martyrs. SEVEN FOUNDERS OF THE SERVITE ORDER (Feb. 11) Seven Florentine noblemen, Bonajuncta Mannetti, Manettus of Antella, Amideus Amidei, Uguccio Uguccioni, Sostineus Sostinei and Alexius Falconieri, who (A.D. 1233) retired from the world and laid the foundations of the illustrious Order of Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, known as Servites. The approved by Pope Order was afterwards Their life was one of singular Innocent IV. austerity, and their great devotion that to the Seven Dolours of Our Blessed Lady. The Order quickly spread, especially in Italy, and brought forth many holy men, eminent for their zeal and for their successful missionary labours. The Seven Holy Founders, each famous for the working of miracles, though they died in different years, have always shared a single tomb. They had for six hundred years been venerated as Saints, when Pope Leo XIII solemnly canonised them (A.D. 1888).

seven sleepers.name: Seven Sleepers
seven sleepers.description: St. Gregory of Tours, a historian of the sixth century, gives the accepted tradition concerning these Saints. They were Christians of Ephesus, victims of the persecution under 250). They had taken refuge Decius (a.d. in a cavern at the base of a hill, and in place of being beheaded were walled up therein to die In the time of the Emperor Theoof hunger. dosius (more than a hundred years later) a heresy had arisen denying the Resurrection of The tradition is that by chance the body. the cavern of the Martyrs was then rediscovered and opened. Whereupon, the Seven Saints came forth, gave public testimony to that article of Faith, and returned to their restingplace, thus passing for ever from this world. It is added that on a leaden plate, in or near the cave, were found their names and the date of their martyrdom. The names are : Maximian, Marcus, Martinianus, Dionysius, John, Constantine. Many further Serapion developments of the story of the Seven Sleepers were later introduced, and several rival accounts but in one form or another it obtained universal credence. Even Mahomet introduced a myth borrowed from it into his Koran. The Greeks and all other Eastern Churches note the Seven Sleepers in their Catalogues of Saints. and

severa.name: Severa
severa.description: The sister of Bishop St. Modoald of Treves, Abbess of a monastery of nuns founded by him ; a Religious of austere and prayerful life who preceded her holy brother to Heaven (a.d. 645).

severianus and aquila.name: Severianus And Aquila
severianus and aquila.description: African Martyrs of CaeTheir names are registered sarea in Mauritania. in all the ancient Martyrologies. We know nothing more of them.

severianus.name: Severianus
severianus.description: An Armenian Saint, tortured to death under the Emperor Licinius (a.d. 322) after he had caused the celebrated Forty Martyrs of Sebaste to perish on a frozen lake. St. Severianus was adjudged guilty, not only of being a Christian, but of having induced many Pagans to believe in Christ.

severinus.name: Severinus
severinus.description: There is considerable difficulty The Martyrology in identifying this Saint. notice describing him as brother of the Martyr He was St. Victorinus can scarcely be upheld. probably the missionary Bishop or Abbot, St. Severinus, who evangelised the countries bordering on the Upper Danube, and whose body was brought to Naples six years after his death (a.d. 482). (Feb. 11) (6th cent.) A Burgundian, Abbot of the famous monastery of Agaune (the scene of the martyrdom of the Theban Legion) in Switzerland, a man of eminent sanctity, and worker of many miracles, of some of which, Clovis, First Christian King of the Franks, was eyewitness. He died near Sens, a.d. 507. (6th cent.) An Italian (June 8) Saint, Bishop of Septempeda (San Severino) near Ancona. He was a wealthy man, and had given all his goods to the poor, and retired into a monastery when Pope Vigilius (a.d. 540) forced him to accept a Bishopric. He governed his flock faithfully in terrible times of devastating war, dying about a.d. 550, shortly before the destruction of Septempeda by the Gothic King Totila.

severinus, exuperius and felician.name: Severinus, Exuperius And Felician
severinus, exuperius and felician.description: Martyrs at Vienne in Gaul, under the Emperor Marcus Aurelius, about a.d. 170. No particulars are extant.

severus.name: Severus
severus.description: A Bishop of Barcelona in Spain who was put to death under Diocletian, about A.D. 303. Some have sought to identify him with another Bishop and Martyr of the same name whom they allege to have suffered death for the Faith in the seventh century at the hands of the Goths ; but the story is very improbable. SEVERUS, SECURUS, JANUARIUS and VIC(Dec. 2) African Martyrs who suffered

severus and memnon.name: Severus And Memnon
severus and memnon.description: Orientals, officers in the Imperial army, burned to death as Christians, with thirty-seven other soldiers, in the neighbourhood of Byzantium (Constantinople) at the beginning of the persecution under Diocletian, about A.D. 290. (3rd cent.)

sexburga.name: Sexburga
sexburga.description: The daughter of King Anna of East Anglia, and the wife of King Ercombert Left a widow, she founded the of Kent. monastery of the Isle of Sheppey, in Kent, at the place now called Minster. She governed her monastery for some years as Abbess, but in her old age retired to that of her sister, St. Here also, at Etheldreda, in the Isle of Ely. her sister's death, Sexburga was chosen Abbess, and remained in that charge until her death (A.D. 699).

sezin.name: Sezin
sezin.description: A Saint who was born in England, and as a Christian laboured in Ireland in St. Patrick's time, assisting him in his mission. St. Sezin crossed to Guic-Sezni in Brittany, where he founded a monastery, and where his A.D. 529 is usually relics are still venerated. assigned as the year of his death. SHERT (JOHN) (Bl.) M. See Bl. JOHN SHERT. *SHERWIN (RALPH) (Bl.) M. See Bl. RALPH SHERWIN. (Feb. 7) *SHERWOOD (THOMAS) (Bl.) M. See Bl. THOMAS SHERWOOD. SICILY (MARTYRS of) (SS.) (4th cent.) (Feb. 21) Seventy-nine Christians, put to death as such in Sicily, in the persecution under Diocletian, about A.D. 303.

sidonius apollinaris.name: Sidonius Apollinaris
sidonius apollinaris.description: One of the most notable personages of the Age in which he lived, and distinguished both as an orator and as a poet. He began life as a prominent public man, was married and had children. The Invasion of the Barbarians, which led to the collapse of the Roman Empire, had commenced ; and Sidonius, called to Rome, was appointed Prefect of the City. But the people of Gaul soon reclaimed him and obtained his recall to his own country. Separating from his wife with her consent, he was made Bishop of Clermont in Auvergne. He proved himself a model Bishop, not only by his zeal for religion, but also by his prudence and skill in safeguarding his flock in the troubles of the times. His dealings with Alaric, the chief of the Goths, though they irritated the Barbarians, ultimately resulted in the escape of his people from destruction. St. Sidonius died in A.D. 482, and has left many Like so many of his conletters and poems. temporaries, he could not bring himself to believe that the Roman Empire was to pass away and to be succeeded by a new Europe, peopled by conflicting nations. correspondence specially interesting. This makes his

sidronius.name: Sidronius
sidronius.description: A Martyr of this name suffered in Rome under the Emperor Aurelian (a.d. 270 His relics were in the Middle Ages about). Another St. Sidronius translated into Flanders. The history of is venerated at Sens in France. the one and of the other is confused, and the particulars drawn from tradition are unreliable.

sidwell.name: Sidwell
sidwell.description: Probably of British (not (Date uncertain.) Anglo-Saxon) lineage. She is said to have lived in the West of England ; and there are churches dedicated to her in Devonshire, chiefly in the But particulars of neighbourhood of Exeter. her life, and especially as to how it came about that she was venerated as a Martyr, are lacking. (Jan. 25) (7th cent.) The First Christian King of Felix, who Seconded by St. East Anglia. founded the See of Dunwich, and by St. Fursey, he induced his subjects to embrace Christianity. He had retired into a monastery ; but, when the fierce Penda of Mercia threatened the East Anglians with Are and sword, people recalled Sigebert. He fell in battle (A.D. 635) and, as he was fighting against Pagans, acquired the title and honours of a Martyr.

sigfrid.name: Sigfrid
sigfrid.description: An English (Feb. 15) in Sweden and Norway, favoured by the Christian King Olaf of Norway. He was the instrument chosen by Divine Providence for the conversion of the similarly named King Olaf of Sweden. St. Sigfrid, made Bishop of Wexiow, at length rested from his long life of toil, and his remains were enshrined in his Cathedral. Some writers say that he was canonised by Pope Hadrian IV ; but his name does not occur in the Roman Martyrology.

sigismund.name: Sigismund
sigismund.description: A King of Burgundy, one of the (July 11) (May 28)

sigisbert.name: Sigisbert
sigisbert.description: Principalities into which France was divided after the break-up of the Roman Empire. He reigned but one year, during which he, on account of an unfounded charge against him, allowed or ordered his son to be put to death. Struck by remorse, he founded the monastery of Agaune, in memory of the Martyrs of the Theban Legion, and retired there to do lifelong penance ; but was seized by a rival chieftain and put to death (a.d. 524). He is honoured and his shrine is at Prague in as a Martyr ; Bohemia.

silas.name: Silas
silas.description: The disciple and companion of St. Paul, of whom we read in the Acts of the Apostles spelled Silvanus in the Epistles (1 and 2 Thess.), both written from Corinth. Tradition adds that Silas remained in Europe and died in St. Macedonia. His name is (xv.-xviii.). (1st cent.) (11th cent.) A holy *SILAUS (SILAVE, SILANUS) (St.) P.p. (May 17) Irish Bishop who, returning from a pilgrimage to Rome, died at The many Lucca in Tuscany (A.D. miracles wrought at his tomb led to his being locally venerated as a Saint. 1100). *SILIN (SULIAN) (St.) (Sept. 1) (6th cent.) A Prince of North Wales, who, in the sixth century, after living for some years as a hermit in an island off the coast of Anglesey, passed over into Brittany and, gathering many fellow-workers around him, laboured at the conversion of the heathen still remaining in that country. *SILLAN (SILVAN, SYLVAN) (St.) Abbot. (Feb. 28) (7th cent.) He was the third successor of St. Comgall in the monastery of Bangor, and A.D. 606 bore great reputation for sanctity. and A.D. 610 are the years assigned by the various writers for his departure from this world. cent.)

silvanus and others.name: Silvanus And Others
silvanus and others.description: Egyptian and Palestinian Christians put to death (A.D. 311) under the Emperor Galerius in Palestine. The account of their martyrdom is given by Eusebius, who places first among them St. Silvanus, Bishop of Gaza. The tortures to which they were put were The total number frightful and terribly varied. of victims is not given ; but Eusebius, an eyewitness, tells us that in a single day thirty-nine perished.

silvanus.name: Silvanus
silvanus.description: See SS. DOMNINUS, THEOTIMUS, &c. (Dec. 2) (5th cent.) A Bishop of Troas in Phrygia (Asia Minor), who had previously been a monk at Constantinople. He seems to have been a prelate, distinguished, not only for piety and zeal, but also for skill and forethought. A useful reform he made was that of prohibiting his clergy from acting as Judges in Law Courts. The historian Socrates, from whom we have the above, narrates a striking miracle worked in public by the Saint. The latter lived till after A.D. 450. (June 20) (6th cent.) The successor (A.D. 536) of Pope During his short reign of two St. Agapetus. years, the Emperor Justinian of Constantinople recovered Rome and the greater part of Italy by breaking the power of the Ostro-Goths. St. Silverius firmly withstood the interference in religious matters of the Empress Theodora ; but was on that account persecuted by her to exile and death. After having been taken to Constantinople, he was banished to an island off the coast of Italy, where he died (a.d. 538). He was succeeded by Vigilius, till then an Anti-Pope.

silvester.name: Silvester
silvester.description: ThesuccessorofPope St.Melchiades (A.D. 314). He governed the Church during twenty and more eventful years, marked by the cessation of the age-long persecutions under the Pagan Roman Emperors, by the conversion of the Emperor Constantine and by the celebration of the great Council of Nicsea (A.D. 325) against the Arian heretics. He ably organised the discipline of the Roman Church, happily no longer imprisoned in the Catacombs in one of which, however, his own body remained interred for several centuries after his death (A.D. 335).

silvinus.name: Silvinus
silvinus.description: He is said by some to have been but it at one time Bishop of Toulouse ; is certain that he came to the North of France about A.D. 674, and acted as Bishop of Terouanne over the country round St. Omer. It is recorded of him that he spent his whole fortune in ransoming the Christians carried off into slavery in their inroads by the neighbouring Barbarian tribes.

simeon stylites.name: Simeon Stylites
simeon stylites.description: old age, when he had already earned a reputation of the highest sanctity. (April 21) See 88. ABATOR, FORTUNATUS, &c. (Jan. 5) (5th cent.) A Syrian Saint, whose extraordinary life of penance led on the summit of a pillar has earned him world-wide celebrity, together with the name " Stylites." The son of poor parents, he in early life retired into a It was at the age of thirty-two monastery. that he adopted his characteristic fashion of sanctifying his soul by doing penance and praying on the top of a lofty stone column. In it he persevered for thirty-seven years until his death (A.D. 459). From time to time, he The last, increased the height of his pillar. on which he had lived for twenty years when he died, was forty cubits (say, sixty feet) high. The flat summit was about three feet in diameter. He could stand, kneel or sit, but never lie down. Similarly, his fastings pass belief, as, for instance, his remaining the whole of Lent without taking any food at all. His pillar stood on a hill on the boundary of Syria and Cilicia, and crowds of people thronged daily the enclosure in which it was erected, in order to ask the prayers of the Saint and to listen His whole life was in a sense to his sermons. a miracle and the wonder of the century in which he lived ; nor, had we not the testimony of Theodoret the historian, and of other contemporary writers, could we accept as facts what is narrated of him. (Feb. 18) (2nd cent.) The son of Cleophas and a kinsman of Our Blessed Lord. He was one of those present on the Day of Pentecost, and, after the death of the Apostle St. James the Jerusalem. He Less, governed that Church for over forty years, revered by Jews and Pagans, as by Christians. When over one hundred years of age, he met his death, being crucified in the reign of the Emperor Trajan, about A.D. 112. became Bishop of (March 24) (15th cent.) simeon salus.name: Simeon Salus
simeon salus.description: A Greek monk who came from Sicily to Treves and there lived the life of a Recluse, enclosed in a narrow and bricked-up cell, in which he died A.D. 1035. Many miracles bore witness to his sanctity. (July 1) (6th cent.) An Egyptian Saint who, in order to court derision and ill-treatment, affected the manners and way of speaking of idiots, and thereby earned for himself the surname Salus, which signifies For nearly thirty years he lived as a hermit in a desert near the Red Sea, but afterwards at Emesus in Syria. He was still alive when that city was destroyed by an earthquake (A.D. 588) but the vear of his death is unknown. fool. a

simeon stylites the younger.name: Simeon Stylites The Younger
simeon stylites the younger.description: A Syrian monk who, about one hundred years after the great Pillar Saint, St. Simeon, and in the same neighbourhood, did penance for sixty years on a similar pillar, and The Emperor became almost equally famous. Maurice of Constantinople held him in great veneration.

simeon senex.name: Simeon Senex
simeon senex.description: " The just and devout man, waiting for the consolation of Israel," who in the Temple took the Infant Saviour in his arms, and, inspired by the Holy Ghost, blessed God with the Nunc dimittis (Luke ii. 25-35). Tradition has preserved nothing more regarding him ; but he has always had in the Church a place in her Catalogues of Saints. as

similianus.name: Similianus
similianus.description: A Bishop of Nantes (France), early in the fourth century. He died a.d. 310. His Acts have long since been lost ; but St. Gregory of Tours testifies to his sanctity and to the honour in which his memory was always held.

simitrius and others.name: Simitrius And Others
simitrius and others.description: Roman Martyrs, twenty-three and in without trial, as having been arrested while assembled for prayer in the Title or Church of St. Praxedes (a.d. 159, about). beheaded Christians, number,

simon stock.name: Simon Stock
simon stock.description: Born at Aylesford in Kent. After dwelling as a hermit in the hollow trunk of a tree (Stock), he joined the Carmelite Order, of which he became General, organising its Constitutions and illustrating it by his piety It was to him that Our Blessed and learning. Lady presented the Brown Scapular and gave the promise of her special protection to all who should wear it. St. Simon died at Bordeaux in France, A.D. 1265.

simon of lipnica.name: Simon Of Lipnica
simon of lipnica.description: A Polish Saint of the Order of St. Francis, remarkable for the austerity of his life, who passed away at Cracow, July 18, A.D. 1482.

simon.name: Simon
simon.description: In the New Testament he is surnamed the Chanansean (of Cana of Galilee), Both Greeks and and also Zelotes (the Zealot). Latins hold that after the Ascension he preached the Gospel in Egypt and in North Africa. He is generally believed to have passed thence into Mesopotamia and Persia, in which latter country he laid down his life for Christ.

simpert.name: Simpert
simpert.description: A monk of an Abbey near Colmar who became Bishop of Augsburg, and ruled his Diocese with much zeal and charity. He died A.D. 809.

simplician.name: Simplician
simplician.description: The successor of St. Ambrose in Both St. Ambrose the Archbishopric of Milan. and St. Augustine look up to him as to a father, and the latter used to send works of his own to His name is often Simplician for correction. mentioned in the Ecclesiastical History of the last half of the fourth century. He was very old when he became Bishop, and held his See for only three years, dying a.d. 400.

simplicius.name: Simplicius
simplicius.description: A native of Tivoli who succeeded (A.D. 468) St. Hilary in the Chair of St. Peter, which he occupied for fifteen years, dying in A.D. 483. He strenuously upheld the Council (Dec. 31) of Chalcedon and resisted three successive Emperors of Constantinople, partisans, more or less, of the Eutychian heresy. He did much good in Rome itself, building churches and Some watching over ecclesiastical discipline. of his Epistles are still extant. (May 10)

simplicius, fortunatus and beatrix.name: Simplicius, Fortunatus And Beatrix
simplicius, fortunatus and beatrix.description: Simplicius and Fortunatus, two brothers, were beheaded in Rome as Christians under Diocletian (a.d. 303), and to their remains an honourable burial was given by their sister Beatrix, who herself was soon afterwards arrested and strangled in prison. (SS.) MM. (2nd cent.) A Christian SIMPLICIUS, CONSTANTIUS and VICTORINUS (Aug. 26) in the Abruzzi (South Italy), put to death with his two sons the Emperor Marcus as Aurelius (a.d. 161-186). Christians under

sincheall.name: Sincheall
sincheall.description: One of St. Patrick's disciples. He founded a Religious House and School at Killeigh, and had one hundred and fifty monks under his direction. (Dec. 19)

sindulphus.name: Sindulphus
sindulphus.description: A native of the South of France, who lived a holy and incredibly austere life as a hermit at Aussonce in the neighbourhood of Rheims. Two hundred years after his death, Bishop Hincmar built a noble shrine for his remains. *SIRAN (SIGIRANNUS) (St.) Abbot. (Dec. 4) (7th cent.) A nobleman of France, afterwards Abbot of a monastery near Bourges. He died A.D. 655.

sirenus.name: Sirenus
sirenus.description: A Greek monk who lived as a hermit in Sirmium in the Balkans, a place famous for the Council of a.d. 350. St. Sirenus was a victim of the persecution under Maximian, probably about a.d. 303. (Feb. 21)

siricius.name: Siricius
siricius.description: A Roman by birth who succeeded St. Damasus as Pope (a.d. 384). He is chiefly remarkable for the many reforms he introduced into Church discipline. Several of his Decretals are still extant. He died a.d. 398. (Jan. 2) (Date unknown.) He may be the Isiridion of Antioch mentioned by St. Jerome ; but nothing is reallv known about him.

siridion.name: Siridion
siridion.description: (Feb. 23) cent.) At Sirmium, capital of the Roman Province of Pannonia, seventy-three Christians perished about a.d. 303 in the persecution under Diocletian, and are honoured as Martyrs.

sisenandus.name: Sisenandus
sisenandus.description: Born in Portugal, he became a cleric of the Church of Cordova. He foresaw his own martyrdom, which came to pass at the hands of the Moors about A.D. 851.

sisinius, martyrius and alexander.name: Sisinius, Martyrius And Alexander
sisinius, martyrius and alexander.description: Eastern Christians from Cappadocia (Asia Minor), received by St. Ambrose and sent as missionaries into the Alpine disThere they met with their death at tricts. the hands of the Pagans (a.d. 397). There is extant a letter to St. Simplician, successor of St. Ambrose at Milan, from St. Vigilius, Bishop of Trent at the time. gives a It pathetic account of the sufferings of these Martyrs.

sisinius.name: Sisinius
sisinius.description: A Martyr (A.D. 311) in the great persecution at Cyzicus on the shores of the Hellespont. He is in special veneration among the Greeks.

sisinnius, diocletius and florentius.name: Sisinnius, Diocletius And Florentius
sisinnius, diocletius and florentius.description: Martyrs at Osimo near Ancona (Italy) in the persecution under Diocletian. They were stoned to death at the same time as the better-known Martyr St. Anthimus in the last years of the third century.

sisoes.name: Sisoes
sisoes.description: An Anchoret in Egypt, where he succeeded to some extent to the influence possessed by St. Antony. He died about a.d. 429, having passed sixty-two years in the wilderness.

sithian.name: Sithian
sithian.description: Otherwise St. SEDUINUS (possibly identical with St. Swithun).

siviardus.name: Siviardus
siviardus.description: A French Saint, Abbot of a monastery in the Province of Maine. He is best known as having written the Life of St. Calais, Founder of his Abbey. A.D. 728 is His own life given as the date of his death. by a contemporary, published by Surius, gives some particulars about him.

sixtus.name: Sixtus
sixtus.description: Otherwise St. XYSTUS, which see. *SLEBHENE (SLEBHINE) (St.) Abbot. (March 2) (8th cent.) socrates and dionysius.name: Socrates And Dionysius
socrates and dionysius.description: Martyrs in Pamphylia (Asia Minor) under the Emperor Aurelian (A.D. 270a.d. 275). They are stated as having been stabbed to death, which points to their having perished from the fury of a mob, rather than to a regular execution after trial.

solange.name: Solange
solange.description: A missionary with St. Boniface from England to Germany, where he ended his life as a hermit in Bavaria (a.d. 790). The chroniclers say of him that " he was venerated as a Saint by noble and simple alike." (9th (May 10) cent.) A poor shepherdess the of Always neighbourhood of Bourges in France. held in great respect on account of her piety and virtuous life, she elected rather to die than In his rage at her constancy to consent to sin. the young lord of the district, who was tempting her, brutally murdered her (a.d. 844).

solemnius.name: Solemnius
solemnius.description: A Bishop of Chartres, famous for St. Gregory of Tours and other old A.D. 602 is the miracles. writers make mention of him. probable date of his death.

solina.name: Solina
solina.description: A Christian maiden put to death at Chartres in France for refusing to renounce It is uncertain in which her Faith in Christ. of the third century persecutions her martyrdom took place. (3rd cent.)

solochanus and others.name: Solochanus And Others
solochanus and others.description: Egyptian Martyrs, soldiers in the Imperial army, who were put to death at Chalcedon near Constantinople in the persecution under Diocletian, towards the end of the third century. The Greek traditions enlarge upon the many and various kinds of torture to which they were subjected. Othertvise St. SALOMON, which see. See SS. VALENTINE, SOLUTOR, Ac. (June 25) (Nov. 13)

sophia.name: Sophia
sophia.description: children. (2nd cent.) The mother of the (Sept. 30) VirginFaith, Hope and Charity, who, as Saints, tradition has handed down to us, suffered death for Christ under the Emperor Hadrian (A.D. Three days 117-138), while still later, their mother, while praying over their tomb, herself passed away in peace. This St. Sophia, though the object of much popular devotion in the East, must not be thought to be the Title Saint of the world-famed Basilica That Church of St. Sophia at Constantinople. is dedicated to the Divine Wisdom or Holy Wisdom, which in Greek is equivalent to our Sancta Sophia. B.C.) (7th Sophonias

sophia and irene.name: Sophia And Irene
sophia and irene.description: Save for the entry in the Martyrologies, no memory has remained of these Saints.

sophonias.name: Sophonias
sophonias.description: cent. (Dec. 3) (Zephaniah), who is said to have been of the Tribe of Simeon, prophecied in Juda in the days of King Josias. He foretold the judgments of God upon Jerusalem ; but also the ultimate conversion of the There are no reliable traditions regarding Jews. him ; and Holy Scripture is silent on the subject.

sophronius.name: Sophronius
sophronius.description: A Syrian Saint from Damascus, the friend of St. John the Almoner of AlexanElected Patriarch of Jerusalem (a.d. dria. 033), he showed himself a zealous and selfsacrificing Pastor of souls. He revised the Mencea or Eastern Martyrology, and has left us several works of his own composition. His last Christmas sermon, preached when the Mohammedans had already laid siege to Jerusalem, and the Christians could not, according to custom, go out to keep the festival at Bethlehem, is very touching. He died a.d. 637, of grief, shortly after the Holy City had been taken and devastated by the infidels.

sosipater.name: Sosipater
sosipater.description: A kinsman and disciple of St. He accompanied the Paul (Rom. xvi. 21). Apostle on some of his journeys, and tradition connects his later life with the island of Corfu. He is other than the Sopater of Acts xx., who was of Bercea and a disciple and companion of the same Apostle. (Sept. 19)

sosthenes and victor.name: Sosthenes And Victor
sosthenes and victor.description: Martyrs at Chalcedon, opposite Constantinople (a.d. 307), in the persecution Diocletian. They were among the under executioners appointed to torture St. Euphemia but through her prayers were converted to Christianity and preceded her to martyrdom.

sosthenes.name: Sosthenes
sosthenes.description: The ruler of the synagogue of Corinth (Acts xviii. 17), who became a disciple of St. Paul, and is probably the "brother" Some say that mentioned in 1 Cor. i. Sosthenes was afterwards made a Bishop, and that he ended his life by martyrdom. 1.

soteres.name: Soteres
soteres.description: An Italian by birth, the successor of Pope St. Anicetus. He lived in the time of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius. He was distinguished for charity to the poor and for watchfulness over the Churches, just then threatened by the rising heresy of Montanus. There is a dispute about the exact date of his death, which took place between A.d. 170 and A.d. 182. He is venerated as a Martyr. (Feb. 10) (4th cent.) A Christian maiden in Rome, put to death after torture in the persecution St. Ambrose more under Diocletian (a.d. 304). than once puts Soteres forward as an example to them in his preaching to the virgins of Milan. (Sept. 7) (4th cent.) A Christian in Cilicia who broke up a silver idol and gave the proceeds to the poor. He was burned to death at the stake (a.d. 304, about). (March 15) (6th cent.) One of the first Benedictine monks and Founder of the monastery of the Order at Terracina, between Rome and Naples, on the Mediterranean coast St. Gregory the Great tells of his holy life and of the wonders wrought by Almighty God at the moment of his death, in witness to his sanctity. (Sept. 11) (13th cent.) A relative of St. Ubaldus of Gubbio, who became the Abbess of a Benedictine monastery in Italy, a.d. 1276 is given as the date of her death. Italy. of

spes.name: Spes
spes.description: A holy man of whom St. Gregory the Great relates that for forty years he was totally blind, and that on recovering his sight he laboured for another fifteen years in the a monasteries famous preacher. He had founded an Abbey Italy. He was Central of SPES (HOPE, ELPIS) (St.) V.M.
